Title and author: Bihar al-Anwar al-Jami'a li-Durar Akhbar al-A'imma al-Athar, volume 1: by Muhammad Baqir b. Muhammad Taqi al-Majlisi.
Imprint: Beirut, Dar Ihya' al-Turath al-'Arabi [13– ].
Note: Catalogued on the basis of volume 24, 1403 AH [1360 Sh.].

Contents: vol. 24, The Book of the Imamate. — vol. 52, The History of the Awaited Proof. — vols. 65, 66, 67, Faith and Unbelief. — vol. 87, The Book of Prayer. — vols. 91, 92, Remembrance and Supplication. — vol. 94, The Book of Fasting. — vol. 103, Index of sources. — vol. 108, General index.

Praise be to God, who raised high the heaven of knowledge and adorned it with its constellations for those who behold, and hung upon it the lamps of light — the suns of prophethood and the moons of the Imamate — for whoever would travel the paths of certainty; who made its stars missiles against the whisperings of the devils, and guarded it with its piercing meteors from the doubts of those who lead astray; then with the trials that mislead "He darkened its night" (1), and with the luminous proofs "He brought forth its morning"; and He made level the ground of the believers' hearts for the gardens of Yemeni wisdom and spread it wide, and prepared it for the blossoms of the secrets of the divine sciences, and so "brought forth from it its water and its pasture"; and He guarded it from the tremors of doubt and vain imagining, placing within it a tranquillity from His gentleness, like mountains He set firm. So we thank Him for His blessings, which cannot be counted, confessing our incapacity and our shortcoming; and we seek His guidance to what is right in our affairs, in every ease and every hardship.

And we bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner — a witness of knowledge and certitude, of assent and faith, in which the heart outruns the tongue and the inward accords with the outward. And that the master of His prophets, the choicest of His elect, His light in His earth and His heaven, Muhammad — may God bless him and his family — is His chosen servant, His selected messenger, His beloved in whom hope is placed, and His proof against all creation. And that the friend of God, the well-pleasing, His drawn sword (2), His mighty tiding, His straight path, His firm rope, His secure side, is 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, master of the legatees, Imam of all creation, intercessor on the Day of Judgement, and God's mercy to the worlds. And that the most excellent of his progeny, the most eminent of his descendants and the righteous of his household are the masters of the noble, the Imams of mankind, the lights amid darkness, the keys of speech, the lions of the fray and the rain-clouds of bounty. God created them from the lights of His majesty, deposited with them the secrets of His wisdom, made them the mines of His mercy, and supported them
In al-Sihah: aghtasha Allah al-layl — God made the night dark.
nada his sword, and intadahu: he drew it from its scabbard.

2.text: …with His spirit, and chose them above all His creation. For them the heavens were raised and the expanses spread out; through them the firm mountains were set fast and the Throne rests above the heavens; by the secrets of their knowledge the fruits of gnosis ripened (1) in the hearts of the believers, and by the rains of their bounty the rivers of wisdom ran in the breasts of those possessed of certainty. May God's blessings be upon them so long as blessings upon them are a means to attaining reward, and praise of them a path to the raising of ranks; and may God's curse be upon their enemies so long as the pits of Hell are prepared for the severest punishments, and cursing the enemies of religion is counted among the most excellent acts of worship.

To proceed: says he who is poor before the mercy of his forgiving Lord, son of him who has passed to the gardens of holiness, Muhammad Taqi — may God make his resting place sweet — namely Muhammad Baqir, may God pardon the offences of them both and gather them with their Imams (2): Know, O company of seekers after truth and certainty, who cling to the handhold of following the household of the master of the messengers, God's blessings be upon them all, that in the prime of my youth I was eager in the pursuit of the sciences in all their kinds, avid to gather the branches of high attainment from their boughs (3). By the grace of God, glory be to Him, I came to their pools and entered their gardens, and lighted upon what was sound in them and what was ailing, until I had filled my sleeve with the varied colours of their fruits and my pocket held the choicest kinds among them; and I drank from every watering-place (4) a draught that quenched, and took from every threshing-floor a handful (5) that sufficed. Then I looked to the fruits of those sciences and to their ends, and reflected on the aims of those who acquire them and on what drives them to reach their utmost; and I considered which of them profits in the hereafter, and looked closely at which of them leads to right guidance. And I became certain, by His grace and His inspiration, exalted is He, that the pure water of knowledge does not slake thirst (6) unless it is drawn from a clear spring welling up from the fountains of revelation and inspiration, and that wisdom does not take root (7) if it is not taken from the ordinances of religion and the strongholds of mankind.
yana'a al-thamar: the fruit ripened; and ayna'a has the same meaning.
An account of him and of his father — may God raise their station — was given in the first introduction.
shajara dhat afnan: a tree having many boughs.
al-manhal: the watering-place; a spring of water to which camels come while at pasture.
al-baydar: the place where grain is threshed. al-hafna: as much of it as fills the two hands.
naqa'a al-ma' al-'atash: the water stilled the thirst.
naja'a al-ta'am: the food was wholesome to eat. And it is said of address, admonition and medicine — naja'a fihi — that it penetrated and took effect.

3.text: So I found all knowledge in the Book of God, the Mighty, "which falsehood does not approach from before it or from behind it", and in the reports of the household of the prophetic mission, whom God made the treasurers of His knowledge and the interpreters of His revelation. And I knew that as for the knowledge of the Qur'an, the understandings of God's servants do not suffice to derive it with certainty, and none encompasses it save those whom God has chosen for that from among the Imams of religion, in whose house the Trustworthy Spirit descended. So I left aside that in which I had wasted a period of my life, though it was what had currency in our age, and turned to what I knew would profit me in my hereafter, though it found no market in our time. I chose to search out the reports of the pure and righteous Imams, peace of God be upon them; I set about investigating them, gave reflection upon them its due, and gave training in them its full share.

By my life, I found them a ship of salvation laden with the treasures of felicity, and found them (1) a firmament adorned with luminaries that deliver one from the darknesses of ignorance. I saw their ways plain and their roads clear, the banners of guidance and success raised along their paths, and the voices of those calling to triumph and prosperity audible upon their courses. Travelling their thoroughfares I came to verdant gardens and green groves adorned with the blossoms of every science and the fruits of every wisdom; and among their stages I beheld trodden and well-kept roads leading to every honour and rank. I did not light upon any wisdom but that its purest was there, nor attain any truth but that its root was there.

Then, after covering the well-known books in circulation, I pursued the reliable but neglected primary works — abandoned through long ages and extended times, whether because of the dominance of the rulers of the opponents and the leaders of misguidance, or because of the currency of false sciences among the ignorant who lay claim to merit and perfection, or because a number of later scholars paid them little attention, content with those that had become famous as being more comprehensive, more sufficient, more complete and more satisfying than any single one of them.

So I set about asking after them in the east of the lands and in their west for a time, pressing my request upon everyone I supposed had anything of the sort, even if he was grudging of it (2). In this I was helped by a number of
al-danin: the miser — that is, even if he was grudging in giving it to anyone, whether because his copies were precious or because they were rare.

4.text: …brethren who travelled through the lands to obtain them and sought them in every region and quarter with earnest searching, until — by the grace of my Lord — there gathered with me a great number of the reliable primary works upon which the scholars of past ages relied and to which the eminent of bygone centuries had recourse. I found them to contain abundant benefits absent from the famous books in circulation, and I came upon in them the bases of many rulings which most scholars had confessed could be found nowhere fit to serve as their source. So I spent the utmost of my effort in bringing them into currency, correcting them, ordering them and refining them.

And when I saw the age at the height of its corruption, and found most of its people turning aside (1) from what leads to right guidance, I feared that before long these works would revert to the neglect and abandonment they had known, and I was afraid that dispersal would find its way to them, since treacherous time gives no help. Beyond this, the reports bearing on any one purpose were scattered across the chapters and dispersed through the sections, so that it was rarely possible for anyone to light upon all the reports relating to a single purpose. Perhaps this too was among the causes of their being abandoned, and of people's slight desire to preserve them.

So, after seeking what was best from my Lord, seeking aid in His might and power, and seeking support from His confirmation and mercy, I resolved to compile them, to arrange and order them, and to gather them into a single book with well-ordered (2) sections and chapters and with its purposes and topics carefully set down, upon a remarkable plan and a wonderful arrangement, the like of which is not known in the compositions and compilations of our people. And it came out, praise be to God, as I had intended, in the best fulfilment; and by the grace of my Lord there came to me more than I had prepared for and aimed at, beyond my best hope. I prefaced every chapter with the verses relating to its subject, then set down after them something of what certain of the exegetes have said concerning them, where they stood in need of exegesis and clarification. Then every chapter of it has taken in either the whole of the report relating to its subject, or that part of it which bears upon it — with the whole set down in another place more fitting to it, or with a reference to the place where it is mentioned, that being more suited to it — so as to secure the intended benefit together with complete concision. And I made clear, with a sufficient explanation and in the utmost brevity, whatever among the reports stood in need of elucidation,
hada 'an al-shay': he inclined away from it and turned aside.
ittasaqa al-amr: the matter was well ordered.

5.text: …so that the chapters should not grow long and the bulk of the book increase, making it hard for students to obtain. And I have it in mind, if my term is extended and His grace, mighty and exalted, assists me, to write upon it a complete commentary containing many of the aims not to be found in the writings of our companions, and to treat the matter there at length for those possessed of understanding.

Among the notable benefits of our book is that it takes in books and chapters of abundant benefit and ample return which the authors among our companions, God's good pleasure be upon them, had passed over, setting aside for them neither a book nor a chapter — such as the Book of Divine Justice and the Return, the setting down of the histories of the prophets and the Imams, peace be upon them, and the Book of the Heavens and the World, which takes in the states of the elements and of what is generated from them, and other matters not hidden from one who looks into it.

So, O company of brethren in religion who lay claim to loyalty to the Imams of the believers: come to this banquet of mine (1) in haste, and take it with the hands of acceptance and certainty, and cling to it in confidence, if you are truthful in what you claim. Do not be among those who "say with their mouths what is not in their hearts", whose inward folds seep through the drift of their speech; nor among those into whose hearts the love of innovations and caprices has been made to sink through their ignorance and their misguidance, and who have counted as false coin (2) what the true communities had put into currency, on the strength of what the deniers of the revealed laws had gilded with the specious varnish (3) of their words.

So good tidings to you, and again good tidings to you, my brethren, of a book that gathers the purposes and holds rare and precious things, whose like the ages have not brought forth in beauty and splendour; of a star risen upon the horizon of the unseen, whose equal in light and radiance beholders have not seen; and of a sincere friend whose like in truthfulness and fidelity was not known in ages past. Your blindness is enough for you, O you who deny the loftiness of its boughs (4) and the height of its branches out of envy, obstinacy and bewilderment (5); and your doubt is enough for you, O you who do not acknowledge the elevation of its standing and the sweetness of its exposition, out of ignorance, misguidance and folly. And because it takes in the kinds of the sciences, the maxims and the secrets, and dispenses with all the books of reports, I have named it the Book of
al-adaba and al-ma'daba: food prepared for an invitation or a wedding.
zafat al-darahim: the coins were rejected. And zayyafa al-darahim: he treated them as false coin.
qawl mumawwah: gilded speech, or speech in which truth and falsehood are mixed.
In one copy: the abundance of its benefaction.

6.text: Bihar al-Anwar al-Jami'a li-Durar Akhbar al-A'imma al-Athar — The Oceans of Light, gathering the pearls of the reports of the pure Imams.

I hope from His grace, glory be to Him, upon His servant who hopes for His mercy and His favour, that this book of mine may be, until the rising of the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad — upon them be blessings, peace, greeting and honour — a resource for the noble and eminent, a source for everyone who seeks the sciences of the illustrious Imams, and a humbling of the base heretics; and that He may make it for me, in the darknesses of the Resurrection, a radiance and a light; amid the terrors of the Day of the Greatest Alarm, a security and a joy; amid the disgraces of the Day of Reckoning, an honour and a gladness (1); and in this world, through the ages, an abundant remembrance. For He is the one hoped in for every grace and mercy, the patron of every blessing and the possessor of every good. Praise be to God, first and last, and may God bless Muhammad and the people of his house, the radiant, the blessed, the noble and honoured. And before beginning the chapters let us set down an introduction, to lay out the conventions we have adopted in this book of ours and to explain what must be known in order to come at its benefits; it comprises several sections.
Chapter One: The primary sources and the books drawn upon, which are

(2) The Book of 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him; the Book of 'Ilal al-Shara'i' wa'l-Ahkam; the Book of Ikmal al-Din wa Itmam al-Ni'ma, on the Occultation; the Book of al-Tawhid; the Book of al-Khisal; the Book of al-Amali wa'l-Majalis; the Book of Thawab al-A'mal wa 'Iqab al-A'mal; the Book of Ma'ani al-Akhbar; the Book of al-Hidaya; the Epistle on Doctrines; the Book of Sifat al-Shi'a; the Book of Fada'il al-Shi'a; the Book of Musadaqat al-Ikhwan; the Book of Fada'il al-Ashhur al-Thalatha; the Book of al-Nusus
al-hubur, on the pattern of fulus: joy and blessing.
We have already discussed these books and given accounts of their authors in the second introduction.

7.text: …and the Book of al-Muqni' — all of them by the Shaykh al-Saduq, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi, God's good pleasure be upon him.

And the Book of al-Imama wa'l-Tabsira min al-Hayra, by the most eminent Shaykh Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh, father of al-Saduq — may God make sweet the earth of them both; and another primary work either by him or by another of the early scholars contemporary with him. Certain indications suggest it is the composition of the trustworthy and eminent Shaykh Harun b. Musa al-Tal'ukbari, God have mercy on him.

And the Book of Qurb al-Isnad, by the eminent and trustworthy Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far b. al-Husayn b. Jami' b. Malik al-Himyari al-Qummi. My own view is that the book is his father's and that he is its transmitter, as al-Najashi stated explicitly. But if the book is his, as Ibn Idris stated, God have mercy on him, then the father stands as an intermediary between him and the chains of his book which we have set down.

And the Book of Basa'ir al-Darajat, by the trustworthy Shaykh of great standing Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar; and the Book of al-Majalis, well known as al-Amali; the Book of al-Ghayba; the Book of al-Misbah al-Kabir; the Book of al-Misbah al-Saghir; the Book of al-Khilaf; the Book of al-Mabsut; the Book of al-Nihaya; the Book of al-Fihrist; the Book of al-Rijal; the commentary al-Tibyan; the Book of Talkhis al-Shafi; the Book of al-'Udda fi Usul al-Fiqh; the Book of al-Iqtisad; the Book of al-Ijaz fi'l-Fara'id; the Book of al-Jumal; the Answers to the Ha'iri Questions; and other epistles — all of them by the Shaykh of the community, Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Tusi, God sanctify his spirit.

And the Book of al-Irshad; the Book of al-Majalis; the Book of al-Nusus; the Book of al-Ikhtisas; the Sufficient Epistle on the Invalidity of the Repentance of the Sinful Woman; the Epistle Masar al-Shi'a fi Mukhtasar al-Tawarikh al-Shar'iyya; the Book of al-Muqni'a; the Book of al-'Uyun wa'l-Mahasin, well known as al-Fusul; the Book of al-Maqalat; the Book of al-Mazar; the Book on the Faith of Abu Talib; the epistles on the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book, on temporary marriage, on the Prophet's inadvertence and his sleeping through the prayer, may God bless him and his family, on the Commander of the Faithful's giving his daughter in marriage to 'Umar, and on the obligation of wiping; the answers to the Sarawi, 'Ukbari and Fifty-One questions and others; and the commentary on the doctrines of al-Saduq — all of them by the eminent Shaykh al-Mufid, Muhammad b.

8.text: Muhammad b. al-Nu'man, God sanctify his subtle spirit (1). And the Book of al-Majalis, well known as al-Amali, by the eminent Shaykh Abu 'Ali al-Hasan, son of the Shaykh of the community, God sanctify the spirits of them both.
And the Book of Kamil al-Ziyara, by the noble and trustworthy Shaykh Abu al-Qasim Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Musa b. Qulawayh.

And the Book of al-Mahasin wa'l-Adab, by the accomplished and trustworthy Shaykh Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid al-Barqi; and the Book of Commentary (al-Tafsir), by the eminent and trustworthy Shaykh 'Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim al-Qummi; and the Book of al-'Ilal, by his eminent son Muhammad.
And the Book of Commentary by Muhammad b. Mas'ud al-Sulami, known as al-'Ayyashi, the trustworthy Shaykh and transmitter of reports.
And the Book of Commentary attributed to the mighty and resolute Imam al-Hasan b. 'Ali al-'Askari, God's blessings be upon him, upon his forefathers, and upon his son, the successor and the Proof.

And the Book of Rawdat al-Wa'izin wa Tabsirat al-Mutta'izin, by the Shaykh Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Ahmad al-Farisi. A number of scholars erred and ascribed it to al-Shaykh al-Mufid; but what we have stated was affirmed explicitly by Ibn Shahrashub in al-Manaqib, by al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din in al-Fihrist, by al-'Allama, God have mercy on him, in the Epistle of Authorisation, and by others. Al-'Allama mentioned his chain to this book, as we shall mention in the last volume of the book, God willing.

Then know that al-'Allama, God have mercy on him, gave the author's name as we have given it. But it will emerge from the words of Ibn Shahrashub that the author is Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali al-Fattal al-Farisi, and that the author of the Commentary and the author of the Rawda are one and the same; so too he stated in the Book of Ma'alim al-'Ulama'. Yet it appears from the words of al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din in his Fihrist that they are two men, for he said: "Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Fattal al-Naysaburi, author of the Commentary, trustworthy — and what a trustworthy man!", and then said, after a long interval: "The martyred Shaykh Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Farisi, author of the Book of Rawdat al-Wa'izin."

9.text: Ibn Dawud said in the Book of al-Rijal: "Muhammad b. Ahmad b. 'Ali al-Fattal al-Naysaburi, known as Ibn al-Farisi (lam, kha' jim) (1), a theologian of eminent standing, a jurist, a scholar, ascetic and scrupulous. He was killed by Abu al-Mahasin 'Abd al-Razzaq, the chief of Naysabur, titled Shihab al-Islam, God curse him." End of quotation. It appears from his words that his father's name was Ahmad. As for his ascribing him to the Rijal of al-Shaykh, the slip in this is plain, since there is no trace of him in al-Shaykh's Rijal — quite apart from the fact that this man's time is much later than al-Shaykh's, as appears from the Fihrist of al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din, from the authorisation of al-'Allama, and from the words of Ibn Shahrashub. In any case, what we have quoted makes clear the author's eminence and that his book was among the well-known books of the Shi'a.

And the Book of I'lam al-Wara bi-A'lam al-Huda; the Epistle on Religious Etiquette; the commentary Majma' al-Bayan; and the commentary Jami' al-Jawami' — all of them by the Shaykh Amin al-Din Abu 'Ali al-Fadl b. al-Hasan b. al-Fadl al-Tabrisi, upon whose eminence, merit and trustworthiness there is agreement.

And the Book of Makarim al-Akhlaq, which is ascribed to the aforementioned Shaykh Abu 'Ali. This is not correct; rather it is the composition of Abu Nasr al-Hasan b. al-Fadl, his son, as his own descendant stated explicitly in the Book of Mishkat al-Anwar, and as al-Kaf'ami stated in what he appended to al-Duru' al-Waqiya and in al-Balad al-Amin. And the Book of Mishkat al-Anwar is by the grandson of al-Shaykh Abu 'Ali al-Tabrisi, who composed it to complete the Makarim al-Akhlaq of his eminent father.

And the Book of al-Ihtijaj, which is likewise ascribed to Abu 'Ali. This is an error; rather it is the composition of Abu Mansur Ahmad b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib al-Tabrisi, as al-Sayyid b. Tawus stated explicitly in the Book of Kashf al-Mahajja and Ibn Shahrashub in Ma'alim al-'Ulama'. This will also become clear to you from what we shall quote from the Book of al-Manaqib by Ibn Shahrashub.

And the Book of al-Manaqib; the Book of Ma'alim al-'Ulama'; the Book of Bayan al-Tanzil; and the Epistle on the Ambiguous Verses of the Qur'an — all of them by the jurist Shaykh Rashid al-Din Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Shahrashub al-Mazandarani

"lam": the siglum for one who did not narrate from the Prophet and the Imams, God's blessings be upon them all. "kha' jim": the siglum for the Book of al-Rijal of al-Shaykh al-Tusi, God have mercy on him.

10.text: And the Book of Kashf al-Ghumma, by the trustworthy and pure Shaykh 'Ali b. 'Isa al-Irbili.
And the Book of Tuhaf al-'Uqul 'an Al al-Rasul, composed by the Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Shu'ba.

And the Book of al-'Umda; the Book of al-Mustadrak; and the Book of al-Manaqib — all of them on the reports of those who differ from us concerning the Imamate — by the Shaykh Abu al-Husayn Yahya b. al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Bitriq al-Asadi.
And the Book of Kifayat al-Athar fi'l-Nusus 'ala al-A'imma al-Ithnay 'Ashar, by the felicitous Shaykh 'Ali b. Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Khazzaz al-Qummi.

And the Book of Tanbih al-Khatir wa Nuzhat al-Nazir, by the ascetic Shaykh Warram b. 'Isa b. Abi al-Najm b. Warram b. Hamdan b. Khawlan b. Ibrahim b. Malik al-Ashtar. The chain to this book is set down in the authorisations. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din mentioned him in the Fihrist and said: "He is a scholar, a jurist, righteous; I saw him at Hilla, and the report accorded with the report." Al-Sayyid b. Tawus also praised him.

And the Book of Mashariq al-Anwar and the Book of al-Alfayn, by al-Hafiz Rajab al-Bursi. I do not rely upon what he alone transmits, since his two books take in matter suggesting confusion, conflation and exaggeration; we have extracted from them only what agrees with the reports taken from the reliable primary works.

And the Book of al-Dhikra; the Book of al-Durus; the Book of al-Qawa'id; the Book of al-Bayan; the Book of al-Alfiyya; the Book of al-Nafliyya; the Book of Nukat al-Irshad; the Book of al-Mazar; the Epistle of Authorisations; the Book of al-Lawami'; the Book of al-Arba'in; and an epistle on the exegesis of "the abiding good deeds" — all of them by the felicitous and martyred Shaykh al-'Allama Muhammad b. Makki, God sanctify his subtle spirit. And the Book of al-Istidrak and the Book of al-Durra al-Bahira min al-Asdaf al-Tahira are also his, God sanctify his secret, as I think; the latter I have in a copy taken from his own hand, God have mercy on him — together with the rest of his epistles and the answers to his questions.
And the Book of al-Durar wa'l-Ghurar; the Book of Tanzih al-Anbiya'; the Book of al-Shafi; and the Book of

11.text: the Commentary on the Ode of al-Sayyid al-Himyari; the Book of Jumal al-'Ilm wa'l-'Amal; the Book of al-Intisar; the Book of al-Dhari'a; the Book of al-Muqni' fi'l-Ghayba; the Epistle on the Superiority of the Prophets over the Angels, peace be upon them; the Epistle on the Clear and the Ambiguous; the Book of Munqidh al-Bashar min Asrar al-Qada' wa'l-Qadar; and the answers to various questions — all of them by al-Sayyid al-Murtada 'Alam al-Huda, Abu al-Qasim 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Musawi, God illumine his tomb.

And the Book of 'Uyun al-Mu'jizat, which is ascribed to him, though this is not established with me. It is nonetheless an elegant book, of which we have an old copy; perhaps it is among the compositions of some of the early traditionists (1). It transmits from Abu 'Ali Muhammad b. Hisham and from Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Ibrahim.

And the Book of Nahj al-Balagha; the Book of Khasa'is al-A'imma; the Book of al-Majazat al-Nabawiyya; and a commentary on the Qur'an — by al-Sayyid al-Radi, Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Musawi, God sanctify his secret.

And the Book of Tibb al-A'imma, peace be upon them, by Abu 'Attab 'Abd Allah b. Bistam b. Sabur al-Zayyat and his brother al-Husayn b. Bistam. Al-Najashi mentioned them both without attesting their trustworthiness, and mentioned that they have a book which they compiled on medicine.
And the Book of Sahifat al-Rida, with its chain given by our Shaykh Abu 'Ali al-Tabrisi, God have mercy on him, by his chain to al-Rida, peace be upon him.

And the Book of Tibb al-Rida, peace be upon him, which he wrote for al-Ma'mun, known as the Golden Epistle. And the Book of Fiqh al-Rida, peace be upon him — of which the eminent, learned traditionist and judge al-Amir Husayn, may his resting place be sweet, informed me when he came to Isfahan. He said: It happened during one of the years in which I was resident near the Sacred House of God that a group of the people of Qum came to me on pilgrimage, and with them was an old book whose date agreed with the age of al-Rida, God's blessings be upon him. And I heard my father, God have mercy on him, say: I heard al-Sayyid say: upon it was his own hand, God's blessings be upon him, and upon it were the authorisations of a great number of eminent scholars. Al-Sayyid said: knowledge came to me by those indications that it is the composition of the Imam, peace be upon him; so I took the book, copied it and corrected it. Then my father, God sanctify his spirit, took this book from al-Sayyid, had it copied and corrected it.
It has already been stated that it is by al-Husayn b. 'Abd al-Wahhab, one of the scholars of the fifth century.

12.text: Most of its wording agrees with what al-Saduq Abu Ja'far b. Babawayh sets down in the Book of Man la Yahduruhu al-Faqih without a chain, and with what his father sets down in his epistle to him. Many of the rulings which our companions have stated, and whose basis is not known, are set down in it, as you will come to know in the chapters on the acts of worship.

And the Book of al-Masa'il, which takes in most of what the noble, eminent and distinguished Sayyid 'Ali, son of the Imam al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, asked of his brother al-Kazim, God's blessings be upon them all.
And the Book of al-Khara'ij wa'l-Jara'ih, by the Shaykh and Imam Qutb al-Din Abu al-Hasan Sa'id b. Hibat Allah b. Hasan al-Rawandi.

And the Book of Qisas al-Anbiya', likewise his, as appears from the chains of the book, and as is also well known. It is not unlikely, however, that it is the composition of Fadl Allah b. 'Ali b. 'Ubayd Allah al-Hasani al-Rawandi, as appears from certain chains of al-Sayyid b. Tawus, though he stated explicitly that it is by the former (1) in the Epistle on the Stars and in the Book of Falah al-Sa'il. The matter is of little consequence, since the book is confined to the narratives of the prophets and most of its reports are taken from the books of al-Saduq, God have mercy on him.
And the Book of Fiqh al-Qur'an, likewise by the first of them.

And the Book of Daw' al-Shihab, a commentary on Shihab al-Akhbar, by the second, Fadl Allah, God have mercy on him; and the Book of al-Da'awat; the Book of al-Lubab; the Commentary on Nahj al-Balagha; and the Book of Asbab al-Nuzul, likewise his.

And the Book of Rabi' al-Shi'a; the Book of Aman al-Akhtar; the Book of Sa'd al-Su'ud; the Book of Kashf al-Yaqin fi Tasmiyat Mawlana Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him; the Book of al-Tara'if; the Book of al-Duru' al-Waqiya; the Book of Fath al-Abwab on seeking what is best; the Book of Faraj al-Mahmum bi-Ma'rifat Manhaj al-Halal wa'l-Haram min 'Ilm al-Nujum; the Book of Jamal al-Usbu'; the Book of Iqbal al-A'mal; the Book of Falah al-Sa'il; the Book of Muhaj al-Da'awat; the Book of Misbah al-Za'ir; the Book of Kashf al-Mahajja li-Thamarat al-Muhja; the Book of al-Luhuf 'ala Ahl al-Tufuf; and the Book of Ghiyath

That is, by Abu al-Hasan b. Hibat Allah. He said in the Book of Faraj al-Mahmum, p. 37: "It was transmitted by Sa'id b. Hibat Allah al-Rawandi, God have mercy on him, in the Book of Qisas al-Anbiya'."

13.text: Sultan al-Wara; the Book of al-Mujtana; the Book of al-Taraf; the Book of al-Tahsin fi Asrar ma Zada 'ala Kitab al-Yaqin; the Book of al-Ijazat; and the Epistle on the Reckoning of the Soul — all of them by the trustworthy and ascetic Sayyid and Naqib, the beauty of the gnostics, Abu al-Qasim 'Ali b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Tawus al-Hasani.
And the Book of Zawa'id al-Fawa'id, by his noble (1), exalted and eminent son, who bears his father's name and his agnomen.
And the Book of Farhat al-Ghari, by the venerated Sayyid Ghiyath al-Din, the jurist and genealogist 'Abd al-Karim b. Ahmad b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. al-Tawus al-Hasani.

And the Book of al-Rijal; the Book of Bina' al-Maqala al-Fatimiyya fi Naqd al-Risala al-'Uthmaniyya; the Book of 'Ayn al-'Ibra fi Ghabn al-'Itra; and the Book of Zahrat al-Riyad wa Nuzhat al-Murtad — all of them by the most eminent and excellent Sayyid and Naqib, Ahmad b. Musa b. Tawus, author of the Book of al-Bushra; may God give him good tidings of what is best.

And the Book of Ta'wil al-Ayat al-Zahira fi Fada'il al-'Itra al-Tahira, by the eminent, learned and pure Sayyid Sharaf al-Din 'Ali al-Husayni al-Astarabadi, resident at al-Ghari, author of the Book of al-Ghurawiyya, a commentary on al-Ja'fariyya, and student of the most eminent Shaykh Nur al-Din 'Ali b. 'Abd al-'Ali al-Karaki. Most of it is taken from the commentary of the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. al-'Abbas b. 'Ali b. Marwan b. al-Mahyar. Al-Najashi, after attesting his trustworthiness, mentioned that he has a book on what was revealed of the Qur'an concerning the People of the House; and he was a contemporary of al-Kulayni.

And the Book of Kanz Jami' al-Fawa'id, which is an abridgement of the Book of Ta'wil al-Ayat, either by him or by someone later than him. I have seen in one of its copies what indicates that its compiler is the Shaykh 'Ali (2) b. Sayf b. Mansur.

And the Book of Ghawali al-La'ali and the Book of Nathr al-La'ali, both of them the composition of the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. Jumhur al-Ahsa'i. He has other compositions to which we may have recourse and from which we may cite.
And the Book of Jami' al-Akhbar. Whoever ascribed it to al-Saduq erred; rather its author transmits from al-Saduq through five
In one copy: "and I do not know his name, and most of it is taken from al-Iqbal."
In one copy: 'Alam, with fatha on the 'ayn and the lam.

14.text: intermediaries (1). It is sometimes supposed to be the composition of the author of Makarim al-Akhlaq, and it may be by 'Ali b. Sa'd al-Khayyat, since al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said in his Fihrist: "The righteous jurist Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Abi Sa'd b. Abi al-Faraj al-Khayyat, a scrupulous scholar and preacher; he has the Book of al-Jami' fi'l-Akhbar." From certain places in the book it appears that its author's name is Muhammad b. Muhammad al-Shu'ayri (2), and from others that he transmits from al-Shaykh Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Duristi through an intermediary (3). And the Book of al-Ghayba, by the eminent, accomplished and pure Shaykh Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Nu'mani, student of al-Kulayni.

And the Book of al-Rawda fi'l-Mu'jizat wa'l-Fada'il, by one of our scholars. Whoever ascribed it to al-Saduq erred, for it appears from it that it was composed in the year six hundred and fifty-odd (4). And the two books al-Tawhid and al-Ihlilaja, from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, in the transmission of al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar. Al-Sayyid 'Ali b. Tawus said in the Book of Kashf al-Mahajja li-Thamarat al-Muhja, among his counsels to his son: "Look into the book of al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar, which al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, dictated to him concerning the traces of what God, majestic is His majesty, created; and look into the Book of al-Ihlilaja and the lessons it contains."
And the Book of Misbah al-Shari'a wa Miftah al-Haqiqa, ascribed to our master al-Sadiq, peace be upon him.

For he said on p. 10: "There narrated to us the chief judge and Imam, the glory of rulers, Abu Mansur 'Ali b. 'Abd Allah al-Ziyadi, may God prolong his splendour, dictating in his house on Sunday the second of the mighty month of God, Ramadan, in the year five hundred and eight. He said: There narrated to me the Shaykh and Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Duristi, dictating, who related the account in passing at the end of Dhu al-Hijja in the year four hundred and seventy-four. He said: There narrated to me Abu Muhammad b. Ahmad, who said: There narrated to me the Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn, God be pleased with him" — and so on. And on p. 15 he transmitted with a sound chain from 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi, who said: There narrated to me Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far al-Najjar al-Duristi, who said: There narrated to me my father Muhammad b. Ahmad, who said: There narrated to me the Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi — and so on.
He said on p. 123: "Muhammad b. Muhammad, the author of this book, said…"
As has already been stated here.

He said at its beginning: "To proceed: I have gathered in this book of mine, which I have named al-Rawda and which takes in the merits of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, what I have transmitted from the trustworthy…" — until he said: "the year six hundred and fifty-one, while Taj al-Din, the Naqib of the Hashimites, was preaching to the people from his pulpit."

15.text: And al-Sayyid 'Ali b. Tawus, God be pleased with him, said in the Book of Aman al-Akhtar: "Let the traveller take with him the Book of al-Ihlilaja, which is the book of al-Sadiq's disputation, peace be upon him, with the Indian concerning the knowledge of God, majestic is His majesty, by remarkable, wondrous and compelling arguments, until the Indian acknowledged the divinity and the oneness. And let him take with him the book of al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar which he transmitted from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, on the knowledge of the aspects of wisdom in the fashioning of the lower world and the disclosure of its secrets, for it is wondrous in its meaning. And let him take with him the Book of Misbah al-Shari'a wa Miftah al-Haqiqa from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, for it is a noble and subtle book in acquainting one with the way of travelling to God, majestic is His majesty, of turning toward Him, and of attaining the secrets it contains." End of quotation.

And the Book of Commentary which al-Sadiq transmitted from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, containing the kinds of the verses of the Qur'an and an explanation of its wordings, in the transmission of Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Nu'mani; it will come in full in the Book of the Qur'an.

And the Book of Nasikh al-Qur'an wa Mansukhihi wa Muhkamihi wa Mutashabihihi, by the trustworthy Shaykh of eminent standing Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari, transmitted from him by Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Qulawayh; reference will also be made to it in the Book of the Qur'an.
And the Book of al-Maqalat wa'l-Firaq wa Asma'iha wa Sunufiha, the composition of the aforementioned most eminent Shaykh Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, God have mercy on him.
And the Book of Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilali.

And the Book of Qabas al-Misbah, among the compositions of the eminent Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Sulayman b. al-Hasan al-Sahrashti, one of the well-known students of the Shaykh of the community, on supplication. He transmits from a number of scholars, among them Abu Ya'la Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Hamza al-Ja'fari, the Shaykh of the community, Abu al-Husayn Ahmad b. 'Ali al-Kufi al-Najashi, and Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar b. 'Ali b. Hamdan al-Qazwini from al-Shaykh al-Mufid, God be pleased with them all.
And the Book of Isbah al-Shi'a bi-Misbah al-Shari'a, likewise his.
And the Book of al-Sirat al-Mustaqim and the Epistle of al-Bab al-Maftuh ila ma Qila fi'l-Nafs wa'l-Ruh,

16.text: both of them by the eminent Shaykh Zayn al-Din 'Ali b. Muhammad b. Yunus al-Bayadi.

And the Book of Muntakhab al-Basa'ir, by the eminent Shaykh Hasan b. Sulayman, student of al-Shahid, God have mercy on him. He selected it from the Book of al-Basa'ir of Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah b. Abi Khalaf, and included in it material from other books while naming them explicitly, so that what he took from Sa'd's book should not be confused with anything else. And the Book of al-Muhtadar and the Book of al-Raj'a are likewise his.

And the Book of al-Sara'ir, by the eminent, trustworthy and learned Shaykh Muhammad b. Idris al-Hilli. At the end of that book he set down a chapter containing reports, saying: "I have culled it from the books of the compiling shaykhs and the accomplished transmitters." He gives the name of the author of each book and then sets down the reports extracted from it; in it are rare reports and eminent benefits.

And the Book of Irshad al-Qulub; the Book of A'lam al-Din fi Sifat al-Mu'minin; and the Book of Ghurar al-Akhbar wa Durar al-Athar — all of them by the gnostic Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-Daylami.
And the ancient book which we found at al-Ghari, God's blessings be upon him who ennobles it, the composition of one of the early traditionists on supplications, which we have named the Ghurawi Book.
And the two books Ma'rifat al-Rijal and al-Fihrist, by the two eminent and trustworthy Shaykhs, Muhammad b. 'Umar b. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Kashshi and Ahmad b. 'Ali b. Ahmad al-Najashi.
And the Book of Bisharat al-Mustafa li-Shi'at al-Murtada, by the jurist Shaykh al-'Imad Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim 'Ali al-Tabari.

And a primary work among the primary works of the pillar of the traditionists, the trustworthy Shaykh al-Husayn b. Sa'id al-Ahwazi; and the Book of al-Zuhd and the Book of al-Mu'min, likewise his. From certain places in the first book it appears that it is the Book of al-Nawadir of Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa al-Qummi; on either supposition it is of the utmost reliability. And the Book of al-'Uyun wa'l-Mahasin, by the Shaykh 'Ali b. Muhammad al-Wasiti.
And the Book of Ghurar al-Hikam wa Durar al-Kalim, by the Shaykh 'Abd al-Wahid b. Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Wahid al-Amidi.
And the Book of Jannat al-Aman al-Waqiya, well known as al-Misbah, by the learned, eminent and accomplished Shaykh

17.text: Ibrahim b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-Kaf'ami, God be pleased with him; and the Book of al-Balad al-Amin and the Book of Safwat al-Sifat, a commentary on the Supplication of al-Samat, likewise his.
And the Book of Qada' Huquq al-Mu'minin, by the Shaykh Sadid al-Din Abu 'Ali b. Tahir al-Suri.

And the Book of al-Anwar al-Mudi'a; the Book of al-Sultan al-Mufarrij 'an Ahl al-Iman; the Book of al-Durr al-Nadid fi Maghazi al-Imam al-Shahid; and the Book of Surur Ahl al-Iman — all of them by the Sayyid and Naqib of noble descent, Baha' al-Din 'Ali b. 'Abd al-Karim b. 'Abd al-Hamid al-Husayni al-Najafi, teacher of al-Shaykh Ibn Fahd al-Hilli, God sanctify the spirits of them both.

And the Book of al-Tamhis, by one of our early scholars. From clear indications it appears to be among the compositions of the trustworthy and eminent Shaykh Abu 'Ali Muhammad b. Hammam; and we have a selection from his Book of al-Anwar, God sanctify his secret.
And the Book of 'Uddat al-Da'i; the Book of al-Muhadhdhab; the Book of al-Tahsin; and the rest of the epistles and answers to questions, by the ascetic and gnostic Shaykh Ahmad b. Fahd al-Hilli.
And the Book of al-Junna al-Waqiya, by one of the later scholars; it is sometimes ascribed to al-Kaf'ami.

And the Book of Minhaj al-Salah fi'l-Da'awat wa A'mal al-Sana; the Book of Kashf al-Haqq wa Nahj al-Sidq; the Book of Kashf al-Yaqin fi'l-Imama, which we may refer to as the Book of al-Yaqin; the Book of Muntaha al-Matlab; the Book of Tadhkirat al-Fuqaha'; the Book of al-Mukhtalaf; the Book of Minhaj al-Karama; the Commentary on al-Tajrid; the Commentary on al-Yaqut; the Book of Idah al-Ishtibah; the Book of Nihayat al-Usul; the Book of Nihayat al-Kalam; the Book of Nihayat al-Fiqh; the Book of al-Tahrir; the Book of al-Qawa'id; the Book of al-Alfayn; the Book of Talkhis al-Maram; the Book of Idah Mukhalafat Ahl al-Sunna li'l-Kitab wa'l-Sunna; the Sa'diyya Epistle; the Book of Khulasat al-Rijal; and the rest of the questions, epistles and authorisations — all of them by the learned Shaykh Jamal al-Din Hasan b. Yusuf b. al-Mutahhar al-Hilli, God sanctify his spirit.
And the Book of al-'Adad al-Qawiyya li-Daf' al-Makhawif al-Yawmiyya, the composition of the jurist Shaykh Radi al-Din 'Ali b. Yusuf b. al-Mutahhar al-Hilli.

18.text: And the Book of Muthir al-Ahzan, the composition of the eminent Shaykh Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Nama; and the Book of Sharh al-Tha'r, which takes in the circumstances of al-Mukhtar, the composition of the same Shaykh.
And the Book on the Faith of Abu Talib, peace be upon him, the composition of the eminent and felicitous Sayyid Shams al-Din Fakhkhar b. Ma'add al-Musawi, God sanctify his spirit.
And the Book of Ghurar al-Durar, the composition of al-Sayyid Haydar b. Muhammad al-Husayni, God sanctify his spirit.

And a large book on the visitations, the composition of Muhammad b. al-Mashhadi, as appears from the compositions of al-Sayyid b. Tawus, who relied upon it and praised it; we have named it al-Mazar al-Kabir.

And the Book of al-Nusus; the Book of Ma'dan al-Jawahir; the Book of Kanz al-Fawa'id; an epistle on the superiority of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; an epistle to his son; the Book of al-Ta'ajjub fi'l-Imama min Aghlat al-'Amma; and the Book of al-Istinsar fi'l-Nass 'ala al-A'imma al-Athar — all of them by the exacting and distinguished Shaykh Abu al-Fath Muhammad b. 'Ali b. 'Uthman al-Karajaki. And the Book of al-Fihrist and the Book of al-Arba'in 'an al-Arba'in 'an al-Arba'in, by al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din 'Ali b. 'Ubayd Allah b. al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. Babawayh, God be pleased with them.
And the Book of Tuhfat al-Abrar fi Manaqib al-A'imma al-Athar, by the noble Sayyid Husayn b. Musa'id al-Husayni al-Ha'iri, teacher of al-Kaf'ami, who praised him greatly in his books.

And the Book of al-Manaqib, by the eminent Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Muhammad b. Ahmad b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Shadhan al-Qummi, teacher of Abu al-Fath al-Karajaki, who praises him greatly in his Kanz; Ibn Shahrashub mentioned him in al-Ma'alim.
And the Book of al-Wasiyya and the Book of Muruj al-Dhahab, both of them by the Shaykh 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali al-Mas'udi.
And the Book of al-Nawadir and the Book of Ad'iyat al-Sirr, by the eminent Sayyid Fadl Allah b. 'Ali b. 'Ubayd Allah al-Husayni al-Rawandi.

And the Book of al-Fada'il and the Book of Izahat al-'Illa fi Ma'rifat al-Qibla, by the eminent Shaykh Abu al-Fadl Sadid al-Din Shadhan b. Jibra'il al-Qummi, resident of the place where God's revelation descended and the abode of the emigration of

19.text: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family — so the authors of the authorisations mentioned.
And the Book of Siffin, by the grave and steady Shaykh Nasr b. Muzahim.
And the Book of al-Gharat, by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Muhammad b. Sa'id b. Hilal al-Thaqafi.
And the Book of Muqtadab al-Athar fi'l-A'imma al-Ithnay 'Ashar, peace be upon them, by Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Ayyash.

And the Book of Masalik al-Afham; the Book of al-Rawda al-Bahiyya; the Commentary on al-Alfiyya; the Commentary on al-Nafliyya; the Book of Ghayat al-Murad; the Book of Munyat al-Murid; the Book of Asrar al-Salat; the Epistle on the Obligation of the Friday Prayer; the Epistle on the Deeds of Friday; the Book of Muskin al-Fu'ad; the Epistle on the Occultation; the Book of Tamhid al-Qawa'id; the Book of al-Diraya with its commentary; and the rest of the scattered epistles — by al-Shahid al-Thani, may God raise his rank.

And the Book of al-Mu'tabar; the Book of al-Shara'i'; the Book of al-Nafi'; the Book of Nukat al-Nihaya; the Book of al-Usul; and others — by the felicitous al-Muhaqqiq, the star of the community and of religion, Abu al-Qasim Ja'far b. al-Hasan b. Yahya b. Sa'id, God purify his resting place.

And the Commentary on Nahj al-Balagha and the Book of al-Istighatha fi Bida' al-Thalatha, by the exacting philosopher and scholar Kamal al-Din Maytham b. 'Ali b. Maytham al-Bahrani (1). And the Book of Commentary, by the Shaykh Furat b. Ibrahim al-Kufi.

And the Book of al-Akhbar al-Musalsala; the Book of al-A'mal al-Mani'a min al-Janna; the Book of al-'Arus; and the Book of al-Ghayat — all of them the composition of the distinguished Shaykh Abu Muhammad Ja'far b. Ahmad b. 'Ali al-Qummi, resident of Rayy, God's mercy be upon him.
And the Book of Nuzhat al-Nazir fi'l-Jam' bayn al-Ashbah wa'l-Naza'ir and the Book of Jami' al-Shara'i', both of them by the most excellent Shaykh Najib al-Din Yahya b. Sa'id.
And the Book of al-Wasila, by the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Hamza.
And the Book of Muntaqa al-Juman; the Book of Ma'alim al-Din; the Epistle of Authorisations; and others — by the exacting Shaykh Hasan, son of al-Shahid al-Thani, God rest the spirits of them both.

You have learned in the second introduction that the ascription of the Book of al-Istighatha to him is not sound, and that its author is Abu al-Qasim 'Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa, son of the Imam al-Jawad, peace be upon him.

20.text: And the Book of Madarik al-Ahkam; the Commentary on al-Nafi'; and others — by the foremost of the exacting scholars, Muhammad b. Abi al-Hasan al-'Amili.

And the Book of al-Habl al-Matin; the Book of Mashriq al-Shamsayn; the Book of al-Arba'in; the Book of Miftah al-Falah; the Book of al-Kashkul; and others among the compositions of the Shaykh of Islam and of the Muslims, Baha' al-Milla wa'l-Din Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-'Amili, God sanctify his spirit.
And the Book of al-Fawa'id al-Makkiyya and the Book of al-Fawa'id al-Madaniyya, by the chief of the traditionists, our master Muhammad Amin al-Astarabadi.
And the Book of al-Ikhtiyar, by al-Sayyid 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Baqi, God have mercy on him.
And the Book of Taqrib al-Ma'arif on theology; the Book of al-Kafi fi'l-Fiqh; and others — by the most eminent Shaykh Abu al-Salah Taqi al-Din b. Najm al-Halabi.
And the Book of al-Muhadhdhab; the Book of al-Kamil; and the Book of Jawahir al-Fiqh — by the Shaykh of excellent method, 'Abd al-'Aziz b. al-Barraj.
And the Book of al-Marasim al-'Aliyya and others, by the learned and pure Shaykh Sallar b. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Daylami.

And the Book of Da'a'im al-Islam, the composition of the judge al-Nu'man b. Muhammad; it is sometimes ascribed to al-Saduq, which is an error. And the Book of al-Manaqib wa'l-Mathalib, by the same judge.
And the Book of al-Hidaya fi Tarikh al-A'imma wa Mu'jizatihim, peace be upon them, by the Shaykh al-Husayn b. Hamdan al-Khusaybi.

And the Book of Tarikh al-A'imma, by the Shaykh 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad al-Khashshab; and the Book of al-Burhan fi'l-Nass 'ala Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, the composition of the Shaykh Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Muhammad al-Shimshati; and the epistle of Abu Ghalib Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Zurari, God be pleased with him, to his grandson Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad.
And the Book of Dala'il al-Imama, by the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari the Imami, who is also called al-Mustarshid.

21.text: And the Book of Misbah al-Anwar fi Manaqib Imam al-Abrar, by the Shaykh Hashim b. Muhammad. It is sometimes ascribed to the Shaykh of the community, which is an error, for it often transmits from the Shaykh Shadhan b. Jibra'il al-Qummi, who is several generations later than al-Shaykh.
And the Book of al-Durr al-Nazim fi Manaqib al-A'imma al-Lahamim and the Book of al-Arba'in 'an al-Arba'in, both of them by the jurist Shaykh Jamal al-Din Yusuf b. Hatim al-Shami.

And the Book on the Martyrdom of al-Husayn, God's blessings be upon him, entitled Tasliyat al-Majalis wa Zinat al-Majalis, by the distinguished and learned Sayyid Muhammad b. Abi Talib al-Husayni al-Ha'iri.
And the Book of Safwat al-Akhbar, by one of the excellent scholars.
And the Book of Riyad al-Jinan, by the Shaykh Fadl Allah b. Mahmud al-Farisi.
And the Book of Ghunyat al-Nuzu' fi 'Ilm al-Usul wa'l-Furu', by the learned and accomplished Sayyid Abu al-Makarim Hamza b. 'Ali b. Zuhra al-Husayni.

And the Book of al-Tajrid; the Book of al-Fusul; the Book of Qawa'id al-'Aqa'id; the Book of Naqd al-Muhassal; and others among the compositions of the most excellent of the theosophical philosophers, Nasir al-Milla wa'l-Haqq wa'l-Din, God's mercy be upon him.
And the Book of Kanz al-Fawa'id fi Hall Mushkilat al-Qawa'id; the Book of Tabsirat al-Talibin fi Sharh Nahj al-Mustarshidin; and others — by the eminent Sayyid 'Amid al-Din 'Abd al-Muttalib.

And the Book of Kanz al-'Irfan; the Book of al-Ad'iya al-Thalathin; and others among the compositions of the exacting Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah al-Miqdad b. 'Abd Allah al-Suyuri, together with his authorisations.
And the Book of al-Idah fi Sharh al-Qawa'id and other epistles and questions, by the Shaykh Fakhr al-Muhaqqiqin, son of al-'Allama al-Hilli, God sanctify their subtle spirits.
And the Book of Adwa' al-Durar al-Ghawali li-Idah Ghasb Fadak wa'l-'Awali, by one of the leading scholars.

And the Commentary on al-Qawa'id; the Epistle Qati'at al-Lijaj fi Tahqiq Hill al-Kharaj; the Book of Asrar al-Lahut fi Wujub La'n al-Jibt wa'l-Taghut; and the rest of the epistles, questions and authorisations — by the most excellent of the exacting scholars and the promoter of the school of the pure Imams, Nur al-Din 'Ali b. 'Abd al-'Ali al-Karaki, may God grant him abundant honour.

22.text: And the Book of Ihqaq al-Haqq; the Book of Masa'ib al-Nawasib; the Book of al-Sawarim al-Muhraqa fi Daf' al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa; and others among the compositions of the most eminent and martyred Sayyid, the judge Nur Allah al-Tustari, may God raise his rank.
And the Book of al-Rijal and others among the compositions of the jurist Shaykh Taqi al-Din al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Dawud al-Hilli, God have mercy on him.

And the Book of al-Rijal, by the Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn b. 'Ubayd Allah al-Ghada'iri — so al-Shahid al-Thani stated, God have mercy on him. Yet it appears from the Rijal of al-Sayyid b. Tawus, God sanctify his secret, as our most eminent Shaykh, our master 'Abd Allah al-Tustari, transmitted from him, that the author of the Rijal is Ahmad b. al-Husayn b. 'Ubayd Allah; and perhaps this is the stronger view.
And the Book of al-Malhama, ascribed to al-Sadiq, God's blessings be upon him.
And the Book of al-Malhama, ascribed to Daniel, peace be upon him.

And the Book of al-Anwar on the birth of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family; the Book on the Martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; and the Book on the Passing of Fatima, peace be upon her — all three by the eminent Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Bakri, teacher of al-Shahid al-Thani, God's mercy be upon them both.
And the Book of Balaghat al-Nisa', by Abu al-Fadl Ahmad b. Abi Tahir.

And the Book of Manhaj al-Maqal fi Tahqiq Ahwal al-Rijal, known in its large, middle and small recensions; and the Book of Tafsir Ayat al-Ahkam — all of them by the most eminent and excellent Sayyid Mirza Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Ibrahim al-Astarabadi.
And the Book of the Diwan ascribed to our master the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him.
And the Book of Shihab al-Akhbar, of the sayings and maxims of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family; we shall indicate their author.
And the Commentary on Shihab al-Akhbar and the Great Commentary, both of them by the highly accomplished scholar Shaykh Abu al-Futuh al-Razi.
And the Book of al-Anwar al-Badriyya fi Radd Shubah al-Qadariyya, by al-Fadil al-Muhallabi.

23.text: And the Book of the History of the City of Qum, by the eminent Shaykh Hasan b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Qummi, God have mercy on him.
And the Answers to the Questions of 'Abd Allah b. Salam, and the Book of Tibb al-Nabi, may God bless him and his family, by the Shaykh Abu al-'Abbas al-Mustaghfiri.

And the Commentary on al-Irshad; the Book of Tafsir Ayat al-Ahkam; the gloss on the commentary on the metaphysics of al-Tajrid; and others — by the most excellent of the scrupulous scholars, our master Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Ardabili, God sanctify his subtle spirit.
And the Book of al-'Ayn, by the distinguished grammarian al-Khalil b. Ahmad.
And the Book of al-Muhit fi'l-Lugha, by al-Sahib b. 'Abbad.
And the Book of Shawahid al-Tanzil, by al-Hakim Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah b. 'Abd Allah al-Haskani. Ibn Shahrashub mentioned him in al-Ma'alim, ascribed this book to him and described it as excellent.

And the Book of Maqsad al-Raghib al-Talib fi Fada'il 'Ali b. Abi Talib, by the Shaykh al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan. His time is close to the age of al-Saduq, and he transmits many reports from Ibrahim b. 'Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim.
And the Book of 'Umdat al-Talib fi Nasab Al Abi Talib.
And the Book of Zayd al-Narsi and the Book of Zayd al-Zarrad.
And the Book of Abu Sa'id 'Abbad al-'Usfuri.
And the Book of 'Asim b. Humayd al-Hannat.
And the Book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Shurayh al-Hadrami.
And the Book of Muhammad b. al-Muthanna b. al-Qasim.
And the Book of 'Abd al-Malik b. Hakim.
And the Book of Muthanna b. al-Walid al-Hannat.
And the Book of Khallad al-Suddi.
And the Book of Husayn b. 'Uthman.
And the Book of 'Ubayd Allah b. Yahya al-Kahili.

24.text: And the Book of Sallam b. Abi 'Amra.
And the Book of al-Nawadir, by 'Ali b. Asbat.
And the Book of al-Nabdha, by the Shaykh Ibn al-Haddad.
And the book of the most eminent Shaykh Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Duristi.
And the Book of al-Karr wa'l-Farr, by the Shaykh Abu Sahl al-Baghdadi.

And the Book of al-Arba'in 'an al-Arba'in fi Fada'il Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him, the composition of the eminent Shaykh and hafiz Abu Sa'id Muhammad b. Ahmad b. al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, grandfather of the Shaykh Abu al-Futuh the exegete.
And the Book of Tahqiq al-Firqa al-Najiya; the Epistle of al-Rida, peace be upon him; and others — by the eminent Shaykh Ibrahim al-Qatifi.
These, then, are the books upon which the transmission turns, even if from some of them only rarely. Should we cite from any other, we state so explicitly in the book when setting down the report.

As for the books of those who differ from us, we may have recourse to them in order to establish the wording of a report and determine its meanings — such as the books of lexicography: the Sihah of al-Jawhari, the Qamus of al-Firuzabadi, the Nihaya of al-Jazari, al-Mughrib and al-Mu'rib of al-Mutarrizi, the Mufradat of al-Raghib al-Isfahani and his Muhadarat, al-Misbah al-Munir of Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Muqri, Majma' al-Bihar by one of the scholars of India, Mujmal al-Lugha and al-Maqayis of Ibn Faris, al-Jamhara of Ibn Durayd, Asas al-Balagha of al-Zamakhshari, al-Fa'iq, Mustaqsa al-Amthal and Rabi' al-Abrar likewise his, al-Gharibayn, Gharib al-Qur'an, Majma' al-Amthal of al-Maydani, Tahdhib al-Lugha of al-Azhari, and the Book of Shams al-'Ulum; and the commentaries on their reports, such as the commentary of al-Tibi on al-Mishkat, Fath al-Bari fi Sharh al-Bukhari of Ibn Hajar, the commentary of al-Qastallani, the commentary of al-Kirmani, the commentary of al-Zarkashi, the commentary on al-Maqasid al-'Aliyya, al-Minhaj, the two commentaries of al-Nawawi and al-Ubbi on the Sahih of Muslim, Nazir 'Ayn al-Gharibayn, al-Mafatih fi Sharh al-Masabih, the commentary on al-Shifa', and Sharh al-Sunna of al-Husayn b. Mas'ud al-Farra'.
And we may cite from the books of their reports in order to refute them, or to indicate an instance of dissimulation, or to corroborate

25.text: what has been transmitted by our own path — such as what we have transmitted from their six Sahih collections; Jami' al-Usul of Ibn al-Athir; the Book of al-Shifa' of the judge 'Iyad; the Book of al-Muntaqa fi Mawlud al-Mustafa of al-Kazaruni; Kamil al-Tawarikh of Ibn al-Athir; the Book of al-Kashf wa'l-Bayan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an of al-Tha'labi and his Book of al-'Ara'is — for he, whether from his Shi'i leanings or from the slightness of his partisanship, often transmits from our reports, and for that reason we have had recourse to his two books more than to the rest; the Book of Maqatil al-Talibiyyin of Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani, which takes in much of the circumstances of the Imams and their kinsfolk, peace be upon them, by our paths and by the paths of those who differ from us, and his Book of al-Aghani likewise; the Book of al-Isti'ab of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr; the Book of Firdaws al-Akhbar of Ibn Shirawayh al-Daylami; the Book of Dhakha'ir al-'Uqba fi Manaqib Dhawi al-Qurba of al-Suyuti; the Tarikh al-Futuh of al-A'tham al-Kufi; the History of al-Tabari; the History of Ibn Khallikan; the two books Sharh al-Mawaqif and Sharh al-Maqasid by the two well-known scholars; the History of Ibn Qutayba; the Book of al-Maqtal of the Shaykh Abu Mikhnaf; the Book on the Character and Qualities of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family; the Book of al-Faraj ba'd al-Shidda of the judge al-Tanukhi; the commentary Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi; the Book of Hayat al-Hayawan of al-Damiri; the Book of Zahr al-Riyad wa Zulal al-Hiyad, the composition of the eminent Sayyid al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Shadqam al-Husayni al-Madani — and it appears that he was of the Imamiyya; it is a fine history containing many reports; the Book of Jawahir al-Matalib fi Fada'il Mawlana 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, a comprehensive book taking in his merits, his campaigns, his sermons and the noblest of his sayings, God's blessings be upon him; the Book of al-Muntazam of Ibn al-Jawzi; the Commentary on Nahj al-Balagha of 'Abd al-Hamid b. Abi al-Hadid; al-Fusul al-Muhimma fi Ma'rifat al-A'imma; Matalib al-Su'ul fi Manaqib Al al-Rasul; al-Sawa'iq al-Muhriqa of Ibn Hajar and his al-Taqrib; the Manaqib of al-Khwarazmi; the Manaqib of al-Maghazili; al-Mishkat; al-Masabih; the Musnad of Ahmad b. Hanbal; the Great Commentary of al-Fakhr al-Razi, his Nihayat al-'Uqul, al-Arba'in, al-Mabahith al-Mashriqiyya and the rest of his compositions; the commentaries al-Basit and al-Wasit and Asbab al-Nuzul, all of them by al-Wahidi; al-Kashshaf of al-Zamakhshari; the commentary of al-Naysaburi; the commentary of al-Baydawi; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti; and others of their books which we mention when citing anything from them. We shall set out the books, their authors and their circumstances in detail in the last of the volumes of the book, if God the Generous and Bestowing wills.

26.text: Chapter Two: The reliability of those books, and the differences among them

Know that most of the books on which we have relied in transmission are well known and of established attribution to their authors — such as the books of al-Saduq, God have mercy on him, for apart from al-Hidaya, Sifat al-Shi'a, Fada'il al-Shi'a, Musadaqat al-Ikhwan and Fada'il al-Ashhur, they fall no way short in fame of the four books upon which everything turns in these times. They are included in our authorisations, and those eminent and excellent scholars who came after al-Saduq transmitted from them. The Book of al-Hidaya is also well known, though not to that degree (1). God has made available to us old and corrected copies of these: as for the Book of al-Amali, we found of it a corrected and vowelled copy written close to the age of the author, which had been read before many of the shaykhs and bore their authorisations. So too the Book of al-Khisal, which we collated against two old copies, one of which bore the authorisation of al-Shaykh Miqdad. So too the Book of Ikmal al-Din, which we had copied from an old book whose date of writing was close to the time of composition. And so too the Book of 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him, for we corrected its first part from a corrected copy said to be in the hand of its compiler, God have mercy on him — though in my view it was not in his hand, but bore his writing and his correction.

As for the Book of al-Imama, its author is among the greatest of the traditionists and jurists, and our scholars count his legal opinions among the reports themselves. An old, corrected copy of it reached us. The other primary work contains noble and solid reports with reliable chains, and the eminence of its author is apparent from it. The Book of Qurb al-Isnad is among the reliable and well-known primary works; we copied it from an old copy taken from the hand of al-Shaykh Muhammad b. Idris, upon which was the following in his own hand: "The original

In one copy: "And as for the Book of Da'a'im al-Islam which we have, I consider it possible that it is the composition of some other of the leading scholars." (It has already been stated that it is by the judge al-Nu'man b. Muhammad.)

27.text: from which I transmitted it contained plain solecisms and disordered wording, so I have reproduced it as I found it, for fear of altering and changing it. Let whoever looks into it find an excuse for me, for I have set out my excuse in the matter."
The Book of Basa'ir al-Darajat is among the reliable primary works from which al-Kulayni and others transmitted.

The books of al-Shaykh are likewise among the well-known books, except the Book of al-Amali, which is not as widely known as the rest of his books; yet we found old copies of it bearing the authorisations of eminent scholars, and we found what the traditionists and scholars after him transmitted from it to agree with what is in it.

The Amali of his learned son is, in our time, better known than his own Amali, and most people suppose it to be al-Shaykh's Amali — which is not so, as has become clear to me from evident indications. Yet his son's Amali falls no way short of his own in reliability and renown, even if al-Shaykh's Amali is, in my view, sounder and more trustworthy.

The Book of al-Irshad is better known than its author, God have mercy on him. Of the Book of al-Majalis we found old copies, and the indications point to its soundness (1). As for the Book of al-Ikhtisas, it is an elegant book containing the circumstances of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and of the Imams, peace be upon them, and in it are rare reports. I transmitted it from an old copy, upon whose title was written: "A book extracted from the Book of al-Ikhtisas, the composition of Abu 'Ali Ahmad b. al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. 'Imran, God have mercy on him." Yet after the preface it ran thus: "Muhammad b. Muhammad b. al-Nu'man said: There narrated to me Abu Ghalib Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Zurari and Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Qulawayh…" to the end of the chain; and so to the end of the book it begins from the shaykhs of al-Shaykh al-Mufid. So it appears that it is among the compositions of al-Mufid, God have mercy on him. The rest of his books are too well known to need comment.
The Book of Kamil al-Ziyara is among the recognised primary works; al-Shaykh drew upon it in al-Tahdhib, as did other traditionists.
The Book of al-Mahasin of al-Barqi is among the reliable primary works; al-Kulayni transmitted from it, as did every compiler after him.
The commentary of 'Ali b. Ibrahim is among the recognised books; al-Tabrisi and others transmitted from it.
In one copy: "And the Book of al-Nusus is likewise only presumed to be his, though it may be by one of the eminent scholars of his age; it is sometimes ascribed to Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Qummi."

28.text: As for the Book of al-'Ilal, although its author is not mentioned in the books of rijal, its reports are carefully set down and agree with what his father, al-Saduq and others transmitted; and its author is mentioned in the chains of certain narrations. Al-Kulayni transmitted, in the chapter on those who saw the Qa'im, peace be upon him, from Muhammad and al-Hasan, the two sons of 'Ali b. Ibrahim, through the intermediacy of 'Ali b. Muhammad; and likewise in another place in that chapter from him alone through the same intermediary. This is among what supports relying upon him, though it is not free of oddity, since he transmits a great deal from 'Ali b. Ibrahim without an intermediary. Indeed the more evident view, as has lately occurred to me, is that he is Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Hamadani, who was the agent of the Sacred Precinct, as I have explained in my notes on al-Kafi.

As for the commentary of al-'Ayyashi, al-Tabrisi and others transmitted from it, and we have seen two old copies of it. It is counted among his books in the works of rijal; but one of the copyists deleted its chains for the sake of brevity and offered at its beginning an excuse more objectionable than his offence.

The commentary of the Imam, peace be upon him, is among the recognised books. Al-Saduq relied upon it and drew from it, even though some traditionists have impugned it; yet al-Saduq, God have mercy on him, was better informed and closer in time than those who impugned it, and most scholars have transmitted from it without casting doubt upon it.

As for the Book of Rawdat al-Wa'izin, we have already stated that it is included in the authorisations of the leading scholars and that eminent and noble men transmitted from it; and you have learned its condition and that of its author from what we quoted from our illustrious predecessors. So too the Book of I'lam al-Wara, whose author is too well known to need comment; my copy is in the hand of its author, God have mercy on him.
The Epistle on Etiquette is likewise recognised; his son drew upon it in al-Makarim. As for his two commentaries, the large and the small, they need no advertising.
The Book of al-Makarim is, in its fame, like the sun at midday, and a number of excellent scholars have praised its author.
The Book of Mishkat al-Anwar is a fine book containing rare reports.

As for the Book of al-Ihtijaj, although most of its reports lack complete chains, it is among the recognised and widely circulated books. Al-Sayyid b. Tawus praised both the book and its author, and most of the later scholars have drawn upon it.

29.text: The two books al-Manaqib and al-Ma'alim are among the reliable books; the authors of the authorisations mentioned them, and their author is too well known in learning, trustworthiness and eminence for his condition to be hidden from anyone.
Bayan al-Tanzil is a small book of many benefits; we have taken only a little from it, since most of it is set down elsewhere.
The Book of Kashf al-Ghumma is among the best known of books, and its author is among the Imami scholars named in the chains of the authorisations.

Of the Book of Tuhaf al-'Uqul we came upon an old copy; its arrangement points to the loftiness of its author's standing. Most of it consists of admonitions and of well-established principles for which we need no chain.

The Book of al-'Umda and its author are both well known and named in the chains of the authorisations, and so likewise al-Manaqib. As for al-Mustadrak, we have an old copy of it which we suppose to be in the hand of its author. The Book of al-Kifaya is a noble book; nothing like it has been composed on the Imamate. This book and its author are named in the authorisation of al-'Allama and elsewhere, and its composition is the clearest proof of his learning, trustworthiness and piety. Al-'Allama attested his trustworthiness in al-Khulasa, saying: "He was trustworthy, one of our companions, a jurist of standing." And Ibn Shahrashub said in al-Ma'alim: "'Ali b. Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Khazzaz al-Razi, also called al-Qummi; he has books on theology and on jurisprudence, among them al-Kifaya fi'l-Nusus." So too the Book of Tanbih al-Khatir and its author are named in the authorisations and well known; but since his book was confined to admonitions and maxims, he did not, God have mercy on him, sift the poor from the sound, and mixed the reports of the Imamiyya with the traditions of those who differ from us. For that reason we have not set down everything in that book, but have confined ourselves to transmitting what is more reliable — for by the blessings of the pure Imams, peace be upon them, we have no need of the reports of those who differ from us.
As for the two books Mashariq al-Anwar and al-Alfayn, you have learned their condition.

The compositions of al-Shahid are as well known as their learned author, except the Book of al-Istidrak, for I did not come upon the original of the book; I found reports taken from it in the hand of the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Juba'i, who stated that he had transmitted them from the hand of al-Shahid, may God raise his rank. And al-Durra al-Bahira, which did not

30.text: become as widely known as the rest of his books; it is confined to setting down brief sayings handed down from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and from each of the Imams, God's blessings be upon them all.
The books of the two eminent Sayyids, like their authors, need no comment.

The Book of Tibb al-A'imma is among the well-known books, though it is not on the level of the rest, its author being unknown. That does no harm, since little of it bears upon the derivative rulings; and in matters of remedies and supplications we have no need of strong chains.

The Book of Sahifat al-Rida, peace be upon him, is among the books well known to both the Shi'a and the wider community. The eminent Sayyid 'Ali b. Tawus transmitted from it by his chain to al-Shaykh al-Tabrisi, God have mercy on him; and I found in the old copies of it chains to the said Shaykh and from him to the Imam, peace be upon him. Al-Zamakhshari said in the Book of Rabi' al-Abrar: "Yahya b. al-Husayn al-Husayni used to say of the chain of the Sahifat al-Rida: were this chain recited into the ear of a madman he would recover his senses." Al-Najashi referred to it in his notice on 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad b. 'Amir al-Ta'i and on his father, the transmitter of this epistle; he praised it and gave his chain to it. In sum, it is among the well-known primary works and may soundly be relied upon.

So too the Book of Tibb al-Rida, peace be upon him, is among the recognised books. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din mentioned in the Fihrist that al-Sayyid Fadl Allah b. 'Ali al-Rawandi wrote a commentary upon it which he named Tarjamat al-'Alawi li'l-Tibb al-Radawi. And Ibn Shahrashub said in al-Ma'alim, in his notice on Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Jumhur al-Qummi: "He has al-Malahim wa'l-Fitan, al-Wahida, and the Golden Epistle from al-Rida, God's blessings be upon him, on medicine." End of quotation. Al-Shaykh mentioned the like of this in the Fihrist and gave his chain to it; we shall set it down in full in the Book of the Heavens and the World, in the chapters on medicine.
As for the Book of Fiqh al-Rida, peace be upon him, you have learned its condition.
The Book of al-Masa'il — its traditions agree with what is in the books in circulation, and its transmitter is too well known for his condition and eminence to be hidden from anyone.
The two books al-Khara'ij and Fiqh al-Qur'an are of established attribution to their author, who is among

31.text: the eminent and trustworthy of our companions; the two books are named in the catalogues of the scholars, and our companions have transmitted from them.

Of the Book of al-Du'a' we found an old copy; in it are brief and noble supplications taken from the reliable primary works — and in any case the matter of a chain in supplication is of little consequence.
As for the Book of al-Qisas, you have learned its condition; we collated it against a copy bearing the hand and the correction of al-Shahid al-Thani, God have mercy on him.
The Book of Daw' al-Shihab is a noble book containing abundant benefits absent from the books of both the Shi'a and the wider community.
The Book of al-Lubab contains some benefits.
The commentary on the Nahj is well known and recognised; most of the commentators have had recourse to it.
The Book of Asbab al-Nuzul contains benefits.

The books of the eminent Sayyids, the sons of Tawus, are all recognised. We have left aside among them the Book of Rabi' al-Shi'a, since it agrees with the Book of I'lam al-Wara in all its chapters and arrangement — which is a matter for wonder.
As for the Book of Ta'wil al-Ayat and the Book of Kanz Jami' al-Fawa'id, I have seen a number of later scholars transmit from them, and their author is of the utmost learning and piety.

The Book of Ghawali al-La'ali, although well known and its author recognised for learning, did not sift the husk from the kernel, and brought the reports of the bigots among those who differ from us in among the narrations of our companions; for that reason we have confined ourselves to transmitting only some of it. The like holds of the Book of Nathr al-La'ali and the Book of Jami' al-Akhbar.

The Book of al-Nu'mani is among the most eminent of books. Al-Shaykh al-Mufid, God have mercy on him, said in his Irshad, after setting down the explicit designations of the Imamate of the Proof — upon him and upon his forefathers be blessings and peace: "The narrations on this are many, and the traditionists of this party have recorded them in their books. Among those who established them with exposition and detail is Muhammad b. Ibrahim, with the agnomen Abu 'Abd Allah al-Nu'mani, in the book he composed on the Occultation."

32.text: The Book of al-Rawda does not stand at a high level of reliability.

As for the two books al-Tawhid and al-Ihlilaja, you have learned their condition, and their manner of expression points to their soundness. Ibn Shahrashub said in al-Ma'alim: "Al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar has a testament."

The Book of al-Ihlilaja is from the dictation of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, on divine unity; and some of the scholars of those who differ from us have likewise ascribed this book to him, peace be upon him. Al-Najashi said in his notice on al-Mufaddal: "He has a Book of Reflection" — a book on the beginning of creation and on urging men to draw lessons; perhaps this is a reference to al-Tawhid. And he counted the Book of al-Ihlilaja among the books of Hamdan b. al-Mu'afa; perhaps the meaning is that it is among what he transmitted.

As for the Book of Misbah al-Shari'a, it contains some matter that gives the discerning and skilled reader pause, and its manner does not resemble the rest of the sayings and traditions of the Imams. Al-Shaykh transmitted some of its reports in his Majalis thus: "There informed us a company, from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, by his chain from Shaqiq al-Balkhi, from one of the people of learning who informed him." This indicates that the book was with al-Shaykh, God have mercy on him, and existed in his time, and that he drew from it — yet without placing complete trust in it, nor was it established with him that it was transmitted from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him. Its chain terminates among the Sufis, and for that reason it takes in many of their technical terms and transmission from their shaykhs and from those upon whom they rely in their narrations. And God knows.

As for the two books of commentary, their two transmitters are reliable and well known, and their contents agree with one another and with the rest of the reports; 'Ali b. Ibrahim and other excellent scholars drew upon them. Al-Najashi counted among the books of Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah the Book of Nasikh al-Qur'an wa Mansukhihi wa Muhkamihi wa Mutashabihihi, and gave sound chains to his books.

The Book of al-Maqalat was counted by al-Shaykh and al-Najashi among the books of Sa'd, and both set down their sound chains to it. Its author is beyond description in trustworthiness, learning and eminence; al-Shaykh transmitted from this book in the Book of al-Ghayba, as did al-Kashshi in the Book of al-Rijal.

The Book of Sulaym b. Qays is of the utmost fame. A number of scholars have impugned it, but the truth is that it is among the reliable primary works; we shall discuss it and its like in the last volume of our book, and shall set down its chain in the fifth section.

33.text: As for the Book of Qabas al-Misbah, you have learned the eminence of its author, besides which it is confined to supplication.
The books of al-Bayadi and Ibn Sulayman are all fit to be relied upon; their two authors are among the stalwart scholars, and the utmost solidity and soundness is apparent in them.
As for the Book of al-Sara'ir, reliance upon it and upon its author is no secret to men of discernment.
The Book of Irshad al-Qulub is an elegant book containing solid and rare reports.

From the two books A'lam al-Din and Ghurar al-Akhbar we have transmitted few reports, since most of their reports are set down in books more reliable than they — even though the eminence of their author is apparent from the whole and from the transmission of the great scholars from them.

The ancient book is wholly on supplications.
