It contains complete, eloquent and rare supplications, from each of which the light of inimitability and of instruction shines forth; every clause of them is an upright witness to their issuing from the Imams of mankind and the princes of speech. Al-Sayyid b. Tawus, God have mercy on him, transmitted much from it in al-Muhaj and elsewhere. The date of writing of the copy from which we extracted was the year five hundred and seventy-six. It appears from al-Kaf'ami that it is the collection of supplications of the eminent Shaykh Abu al-Husayn Muhammad b. Harun al-Tal'ukbari, who is among the greatest of the traditionists.

The two books of rijal are what the excellent scholars turn upon in every age and land. From them we confine ourselves to setting down what concerns matters other than the establishing of the circumstances of transmitters — that is, what bears upon the other chapters.

The Book of Bisharat al-Mustafa is among the well-known books; many of our scholars have transmitted from it, and its author is among the most eminent traditionists. He occurs in most of our chains to the Shaykh of the community, and he transmits from Abu 'Ali, son of the Shaykh of the community, all his books and narrations. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said in the Fihrist: "The Shaykh and Imam 'Imad al-Din Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim al-Tabari, a trustworthy jurist; he studied under al-Shaykh Abu 'Ali al-Tusi and has compositions; Qutb al-Din al-Rawandi studied under him."

The eminence of al-Husayn b. Sa'id and of Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa spares us any need to treat of the condition of their compositions; and the attribution of the Book of al-Zuhd to al-Husayn is established.
As for the other primary work, its opening ran thus: "Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id";

34.text: then in the remaining chapters it begins with the shaykhs of al-Husayn. This gives rise to the supposition that it is his; yet it may be by Ahmad, on account of certain indications, as we have noted, and because the book opens with him.

As for the Book of al-'Uyun wa'l-Mahasin, since it is confined to maxims and admonitions, our ignorance of its author does us no harm. We have of it an old, corrected copy. It contains the choice sayings, and adds to them many of the precious maxims which al-Amidi did not come upon. It appears from what we shall quote from Ibn Shahrashub that al-Amidi was among our scholars and that he authorised him to transmit this book. He said in Ma'alim al-'Ulama': "'Abd al-Wahid b. Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Wahid al-Amidi al-Tamimi; he has Ghurar al-Hikam wa Durar al-Kalim, in which he sets down the sayings and maxims of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him."
The fame of al-Kaf'ami's books and the learning of their author spare us any need to treat of their condition or of his.
The Book of Qada' al-Huquq is a good book containing fine reports.

As for the books of al-Sayyid Baha' al-Din b. 'Abd al-Hamid: the first two contain rare reports on the return and on the circumstances of the Qa'im, peace be upon him; the third takes in the merits of the Imams, the manner of the martyrdom of the Master of Martyrs and of his blessed companions, peace be upon him and upon them, and an account of al-Mukhtar's rising to seek vengeance together with the sum of his circumstances; and the fourth contains rare reports. The said Sayyid is among the most eminent of the naqibs and the distinguished.

The solidity of the Book of al-Tamhis points to the learning of its author; and if its author is Abu 'Ali, as appears to be the case, then his learning and his attested trustworthiness are well known.
The books of the two eminent scholars al-'Allama and Ibn Fahd, God sanctify the spirits of them both, are in fame and reliability as their authors are.

The Book of al-'Adad is an elegant book on the deeds of the days of the months and their auspicious and inauspicious days; half of it has come into our hands. Its author is known for learning and named in the authorisations; he is the brother of al-'Allama al-Hilli, God sanctify their subtle spirits.
As for al-Shaykh Ibn Nama and al-Sayyid Fakhkhar, they are among the most eminent of our transmitters and shaykhs; mention of them will come in the authorisations of our companions.

35.text: The Book of al-Ghurar contains eminent reports together with their exposition, and its author is among the excellent Sayyids. He transmits from Ibn Shahrashub, from 'Ali b. Sa'id b. Hibat Allah al-Rawandi, from 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far al-Duristi, and from other eminent and leading scholars.

As for al-Mazar al-Kabir, the manner of its chains shows it to be a reliable book; the two Sayyids, the sons of Tawus, took many reports and visitations from it. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said in the Fihrist: "Al-Sayyid Abu al-Barakat Muhammad b. Isma'il al-Mashhadi, a trustworthy jurist and traditionist; he studied under the Imam Muhyi al-Din al-Husayn b. al-Muzaffar al-Hamadani." And in his notice on al-Hamadani he said: "Al-Sayyid Abu al-Barakat al-Mashhadi informed us of his books."

As for al-Karajaki, he is among the most eminent of scholars, jurists and theologians; all the holders of authorisations give their chains to him. His Book of Kanz al-Fawa'id is among the well-known books from which most who came after him drew, and the rest of his books are of the utmost solidity. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said in his Fihrist: "The learned and trustworthy Shaykh Abu al-Fath Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Karajaki, the jurist of the companions; he studied under al-Sayyid al-Murtada 'Alam al-Huda and al-Shaykh al-Muwaffaq Abu Ja'far, God have mercy on them both. He has compositions, among them the Book of al-Ta'ajjub and the Book of al-Nawadir. Our father informed us, from his father, from him." End of quotation. It appears from the authorisations that he was the teacher of Ibn al-Barraj.

Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din is among the well-known trustworthy men and traditionists, and his Fihrist is of the utmost fame. He is among the descendants of al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Babawayh, and al-Saduq is his great-uncle. Al-Shahid al-Thani said in the Book of Authorisation: "And I have authorised him to transmit from me all that was transmitted by 'Ali b. 'Ubayd Allah b. al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Babawayh, and all that his Fihrist contains of the names of the scholars later than al-Shaykh Abu Ja'far al-Tusi. This man was of good precision and transmitted a great deal from numerous shaykhs." End of quotation. His Arba'in contains rare and elegant reports.
The Book of al-Tuhfa is a book of many benefits, yet we have transmitted from it only rarely, since its reports are taken from books better known than it.

36.text: As for Ibn Shadhan, you have learned his condition.

As for al-Mas'udi, al-Najashi counted him in his Fihrist among the transmitters of the Shi'a and said: "He has books, among them the Book of Ithbat al-Wasiyya li-'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, and the Book of Muruj al-Dhahab. He died in the year three hundred and thirty-three."

As for the Book of al-Nawadir, its author is among the noble and eminent. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said in the Fihrist: "The scholar of his age; he combined with loftiness of lineage the perfection of learning and standing, and was the teacher of the leading men of his time. He has compositions; I met him and read some of them before him." End of quotation. Most of the traditions of this book are taken from the books of Musa b. Isma'il b. Musa b. Ja'far, peace be upon them both, which Sahl b. Ahmad al-Dibaji transmitted from Muhammad b. Muhammad b. al-Ash'ath, from him. As for Sahl, al-Najashi praised him; and Ibn al-Ghada'iri, after censuring him, said: "There is no harm in what is transmitted of the Ash'athiyyat and the like of them, of what others have transmitted." As for Ibn al-Ash'ath, al-Najashi attested his trustworthiness and said that he transmits a recension from Musa b. Isma'il. Al-Saduq transmitted from his book in al-Majalis by another chain, thus: "There narrated to us al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. Idris, from his father, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa, from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Musa b. Isma'il." By these indications, acting upon its traditions is strengthened. As for Ad'iyat al-Sirr, we shall set them down in full in their place.

As for the Book of al-Fada'il and the Book of Izahat al-'Illa, their author is among the most eminent of the trustworthy and learned, and the holders of authorisations have praised him greatly. Al-Shahid, God sanctify his secret, said in al-Dhikra: "The Shaykh Abu al-Fadl Shadhan b. Jibra'il al-Qummi — who is among our eminent jurists — mentioned in the Book of Izahat al-'Illa fi Ma'rifat al-Qibla…", and then he set down a portion of it. As for the Book of Siffin, it is a reliable book from which al-Kulayni and the other traditionists drew. Al-Najashi said: "Nasr b. Muzahim al-Minqari al-'Attar, Abu al-Mufaddal, a Kufan of upright method and sound conduct, save that he transmits from the weak. His books are excellent, among them the Book of al-Jamal and the Book of Siffin." And he set down his chains to the two books and to the rest of his books; al-Shaykh likewise set down in the Fihrist his chain to his books.

37.text: As for the Book of al-Gharat, its author is among the well-known traditionists. Al-Najashi and al-Shaykh mentioned him, counted the Book of al-Gharat among his books and praised him, saying that he was a Zaydi and then became an Imami. Al-Sayyid b. Tawus transmitted many traditions from his books. One of the eminent traditionists informed us that he had found a sound, vowelled and old copy of it, written close to the time of the compiler and bearing the hands of a number of eminent scholars, and that he had it copied from that; so we took a copy from him. It agrees with what Ibn Abi al-Hadid and others extracted from it.

As for the Book of al-Muqtadab, al-Shaykh and al-Najashi mentioned it in their catalogues, counted this book among his books and praised him for the abundance of his transmission — yet they ascribed to him that he became confused at the end of his life. Ibn Shahrashub mentioned him and listed his compositions without impugning him in anything. In sum, his book is among the primary works reliable in the eyes of the Shi'a, as appears upon investigation.
The fame of al-Shahid al-Thani and of al-Muhaqqiq spares us any need to treat of the condition of their books; God illumine their tombs.
Al-Muhaqqiq al-Bahrani is among the most eminent and best known of scholars, and his two books are of the utmost fame.

As for the commentary of Furat: although our companions have treated its author with neither praise nor censure, the fact that its reports agree with the reliable traditions that have reached us, and the good precision of his transmission of them, is what yields confidence in its author and a good opinion of him. Al-Saduq, God have mercy on him, transmitted reports from him through the intermediacy of al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi; and al-Hakim Abu al-Qasim al-Haskani transmitted from him in Shawahid al-Tanzil and elsewhere.

As for the four books of Ja'far b. Ahmad, some are on the merits and some on character, etiquette and rulings; the legal rulings in them are rare. Their author is not mentioned in the books of rijal, but he is among the early scholars, close to the age of al-Mufid or in his age. He transmits from al-Safwani, the transmitter of al-Kulayni, through an intermediary, and also transmits from al-Saduq, as will come in the chain of the commentary of the Imam, peace be upon him. In them are fine and rare reports, and we have old corrected copies of them. Al-Sayyid b. Tawus transmits from his books in the Book of al-Iqbal and elsewhere, which supports reliance upon them. Al-Shahid al-Thani, God have mercy on him, transmitted from some of his books in

38.text: the Commentary on al-Irshad, on the merit of the congregational prayer, as did other eminent scholars.

As for the Book of Nuzhat al-Nazir and al-Jami', their author is among the well-known and exacting scholars; his opinions circulate among the later scholars, and he is the paternal cousin of al-Muhaqqiq, the author of al-Shara'i' and al-Mu'tabar.

The Book of al-Wasila and its author are both well known, and his opinions circulate among the later scholars. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said: "The Shaykh and Imam 'Imad al-Din Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Hamza al-Tusi al-Mashhadi, a learned jurist and preacher; he has compositions, among them al-Wasila."

As for the books of the noble shaykhs and illustrious masters al-Shaykh Hasan, al-Sayyid Muhammad and al-Shaykh al-Baha'i — God illumine their resting places — their eminence and the distinction of their authors are well known; and so too the two books of our master Muhammad Amin, God sanctify his secret.
Al-Sayyid b. Baqi is of the utmost learning and accomplishment, though most of his book is taken from the Misbah of al-Shaykh, God have mercy on him.
The Book of Taqrib al-Ma'arif is a good book on theology containing fine reports, some of which we have set down in the Book of Trials; and the standing of its author is too great to need comment.
So too the books of the two eminent Shaykhs Ibn al-Barraj and Sallar are, like their authors, of the utmost reliability.

As for the Book of Da'a'im al-Islam, most of the people of our age used to imagine that it was the composition of al-Saduq, God have mercy on him. It has become clear to us that it is the composition of Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man b. Muhammad b. Mansur, judge of Egypt in the days of the Isma'ili dynasty. He was at first a Maliki, then was guided aright and became an Imami. Most of the reports of this book agree with what is in our well-known books, save that he did not transmit from the Imams after al-Sadiq, out of fear of the Isma'ili caliphs; yet beneath the veil of dissimulation he disclosed the truth to whoever looks into it deeply. His reports are fit to serve for corroboration and confirmation. Ibn Khallikan said: "He is one of the eminent men who are looked to. The Amir al-Mukhtar al-Masihi mentioned him in his history and said: he was of such learning, jurisprudence, religion and distinction as could not be surpassed. He has several compositions, among them the Book of Ikhtilaf Usul al-Madhahib and others." End of quotation. He was of the Maliki school and then passed over to the school of the Imamiyya. Ibn Zulaq said in his notice on his son 'Ali b. al-Nu'man: "His father al-Nu'man b. Muhammad the judge was of the utmost learning, one of the people of

39.text: the Qur'an and knowledge of its meanings, learned in the aspects of jurisprudence, in the science of the disagreements of the jurists, in lexicography, in poetry, and in acquaintance with the days of men, together with intelligence and fairness. He composed for the People of the House thousands of pages of books, in the finest composition and the most agreeable rhymed prose, and produced on the merits and the faults an excellent book. He has refutations of his opponents: a refutation of Abu Hanifa, of Malik, of al-Shafi'i and of Ibn Shurayh; and a Book of Disagreement in which he champions the People of the House, peace be upon them." I say: he then set down much of his merits and circumstances, and al-Yafi'i and others mentioned the like. Ibn Shahrashub said in the Book of Ma'alim al-'Ulama': "The judge al-Nu'man b. Muhammad is not an Imami, and his books are excellent; among them Sharh al-Akhbar fi Fada'il al-A'imma al-Athar, in which he sets down the merits down to al-Sadiq, peace be upon him; al-Ittifaq wa'l-Iftiraq; al-Manaqib wa'l-Mathalib; al-Imama; Usul al-Madhahib; al-Dawla; al-Idah." End of quotation.
The Book of al-Manaqib wa'l-Mathalib is an elegant book containing eminent benefits.
The book of al-Husayn b. Hamdan contains many reports on the merits, though some of the scholars of rijal have cast doubt upon him.

As for Ibn al-Khashshab, his history is well known; the author of Kashf al-Ghumma drew from it, and its reports are reliable. It is a small book confined to their births and deaths and the spans of their lives, peace be upon them.

The Book of al-Burhan is a solid book containing rare reports, and its author is among the well-known eminent scholars. Al-Najashi said: "'Ali b. Muhammad al-'Adawi al-Shimshati was a shaykh in al-Jazira, the most learned and most cultivated man of his time." He then listed many compositions of his and counted this book among them.

The epistle of Abu Ghalib contains the circumstances of Zurara b. A'yan, his brothers, their children and grandchildren, their chains, their books and their narrations; in it are abundant benefits. This man — I mean Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Sulayman b. al-Hasan b. al-Jahm b. Bukayr b. A'yan b. Sinsin, titled Abu Ghalib al-Zurari — was among the most eminent of the trustworthy and of the traditionists, and was teacher of the leading eminent scholars such as al-Shaykh al-Mufid, Ibn al-Ghada'iri and Ibn 'Abdun, God sanctify their secrets. Al-Najashi and others counted this epistle among his books, and we shall set the epistle down in full in the last of the volumes of this book, if God the Exalted wills.
The Book of Dala'il al-Imama is among the reliable and well-known books; most who came after him drew from it,

40.text: such as al-Sayyid b. Tawus and others. We found an old, corrected copy of it in the library of our master the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. Its author is among the trustworthy transmitters of our Imami community, and he is not Ibn Jarir the historian, who differs from us. Al-Najashi, God have mercy on him, said: "Muhammad b. Jarir b. Rustam al-Tabari al-Amuli, Abu Ja'far, an eminent man among our companions, of much learning and excellent theology, trustworthy in hadith. He has the Book of al-Mustarshid fi Dala'il al-Imama. There informed us Ahmad b. 'Ali b. Nuh, from al-Hasan b. Hamza al-Tabari, who said: There narrated to us Muhammad b. Jarir b. Rustam this book and the rest of his books." And al-Shaykh said in the Fihrist: "Muhammad b. Jarir b. Rustam al-Tabari the elder, with the agnomen Abu Ja'far, religious and learned; he is not the author of the History, for that man was of the wider community's school. He has numerous books, among them the Book of al-Mustarshid."

The Book of Misbah al-Anwar contains choice reports, and it appears from the book that its author is among the great eminent scholars; he transmits from the reliable primary works of both the Shi'a and the wider community.

The Book of al-Durr al-Nazim is a noble and generous book containing many reports on the merits, by our paths and by the paths of those who differ from us. It sometimes transmits from the Book of Madinat al-'Ilm and from other reliable books. Its author was a contemporary of al-Sayyid 'Ali b. Tawus, God have mercy on him; we have seldom had recourse to it, for certain reasons.
As for the Book of al-Arba'in, most of our scholars have drawn from it and relied upon it.
The Book of Tasliyat al-Majalis — its author is among the eminent Sayyids of the later scholars. It is a large book containing many reports, some of which we have set down in the tenth volume.
The Book of Safwat al-Akhbar and Riyad al-Jinan contain rare reports on the merits; we have extracted from them what agrees with the reports of the reliable books.
As for the Book of al-Ghunya, its author has no need of praise; he is among the most eminent jurists, and his books are reliable and well known, this book above all.
The books of al-Muhaqqiq al-Tusi — God rest his sanctified spirit — and their author are better known than the sun at midday.

Al-Sayyid 'Amid al-Din is among the well-known scholars; the holders of authorisations have praised him, and his books are recognised and in circulation, though we have had recourse to them only a little.

41.text: So too the most eminent Shaykh al-Miqdad b. 'Abd Allah is among the most eminent jurists, and his compositions are of the utmost reliability and fame.
So too Fakhr al-Muhaqqiqin, the most exacting of the later jurists; his books are in circulation and recognised.
The Book of al-Adwa' contains many benefits, though we have not had recourse to it often.

As for the Shaykh who promoted the school, Nur al-Din — may God gather him with the pure Imams — his claims upon the faith and its people are greater than the least of them could be thanked for, and his compositions are of the utmost gravity and solidity.

And the guided martyr al-Sayyid al-Tustari — may God gather him with the first of the martyrs — expended every effort in aiding the manifest religion and repelling the doubts of those who differ from us. His books are recognised, though we have taken their reports from their own sources.
Al-Shaykh Ibn Dawud is of the utmost fame among the later scholars, and they have gone to lengths in praising him in the authorisations; our recourse to his books has been slight.

So too the Rijal of Ibn al-Ghada'iri: if its author is al-Husayn, then he is among the most eminent of the trustworthy; but if he is Ahmad, as appears to be the case, then I do not rely upon him greatly. In any case, relying upon this book would require rejecting most of the reports of the well-known books.
The two books of al-Malhama are well known, but I do not rely upon them greatly.

As for the Book of al-Anwar, some of the companions of al-Shahid al-Thani praised its author and counted him among his shaykhs. The contents of its reports agree with the reliable reports transmitted by sound chains, and it was well known among our scholars, who used to recite it in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in gatherings and assemblies until the day of the noble birth. So too the other two books are reliable, and we have set down some of their reports in this book.

The book of Ahmad b. Abi Tahir contains the sermon of Fatima, God's blessings be upon her, and the sermons of the women of the People of the House, peace be upon them, at Karbala; its author is reliable in the eyes of both parties.

And the most glorious Sayyid Mirza Muhammad, God sanctify his spirit, was among the distinguished and eminent and among the godfearing and exemplary. He dwelt near the Sacred House of God until he passed to God's mercy, and his books are of the utmost solidity and soundness.

42.text: As for the Book of the Diwan, its attribution to him, God's blessings be upon him, is well known, and many of the verses set down in it are transmitted in other books; yet it is difficult to judge the whole of it sound. From the Ma'alim of Ibn Shahrashub it may be gathered that it is the composition of 'Ali b. Ahmad al-Adib al-Naysaburi, one of our scholars; and al-Najashi counted among the books of 'Abd al-'Aziz b. Yahya al-Juludi a Book of the Poetry of 'Ali, peace be upon him.

As for the Book of al-Shihab, although it is among the compositions of those who differ from us, most of its clauses are set down in the books and reports transmitted by our paths; for that reason our scholars relied upon it and undertook to comment upon it. Al-Shaykh Muntajab al-Din said: "Al-Sayyid Fakhr al-Din Shumayla b. Muhammad b. Abi Hashim al-Husayni, a righteous scholar; he transmitted to us the Book of al-Shihab of the judge Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad b. Salama b. Ja'far al-Quda'i, from him."
Al-Shaykh Abu al-Futuh is well known for learning, and his books are recognised and familiar.
The Book of al-Anwar al-Badriyya contains some evident benefits.

The History of the City of Qum is a reliable book, but the original of the book was not available to us; only its translation reached us, and we have extracted some of its reports in the Book of the Heavens and the World.
The answers to the questions of Ibn Salam we have set down in their places.

As for the Book of Tibb al-Nabi, may God bless him and his family, although most of its reports are by the paths of those who differ from us, it is well known and in circulation among our scholars. Nasir al-Milla wa'l-Din al-Tusi said in the Book of Adab al-Muta'allimin: "He must learn something of medicine and seek blessing in the traditions handed down on medicine which the Shaykh and Imam Abu al-'Abbas al-Mustaghfiri gathered in his book entitled Tibb al-Nabi, may God bless him and his family."

Al-Muhaqqiq al-Ardabili reached the utmost limit in scrupulousness, godfearing, asceticism and learning; I have not heard of his like among the earlier or the later scholars. May God join him with the pure Imams. His books are of the utmost exactitude and investigation.

Al-Khalil and al-Sahib were both of the Imamiyya, and both are landmarks in lexicography, prosody and Arabic. Al-Sahib is he in whose name al-Saduq prefaced 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him, and to whom he presented it.
Al-Shawahid is a good book containing an exposition of the revelation of the verses concerning the People of the House, peace be upon them,

43.text: and al-Tabrisi and other leading scholars often cite from it.
Al-Maqsad contains rare reports and unusual rulings, some of which we set down for corroboration and confirmation.
Al-'Umda is the best known and most reliable of books on genealogy.

Al-Narsi is among the possessors of primary works; he transmitted from al-Sadiq and al-Kazim, peace be upon them both. Al-Najashi set down his chain to Ibn Abi 'Umayr from him; al-Shaykh in al-Tahdhib and elsewhere transmits from his book; and al-Kulayni likewise transmitted from his book in several places — among them, in the chapter on kissing, from 'Ali b. Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from him; and among them, in the Book of Fasting, by another chain from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from him.

So too the book of Zayd al-Zarrad, from which the people of learning and right guidance have drawn. Al-Najashi likewise set down his chain to Ibn Abi 'Umayr from him. Al-Shaykh said in the Fihrist and the Rijal: "They have two primary works which Ibn Babawayh and Ibn al-Walid did not transmit; Ibn al-Walid used to say that the two are forged." And Ibn al-Ghada'iri said: "Abu Ja'far erred in this statement, for I have seen their books heard from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr." End of quotation. I say: although the masters of rijal did not attest their trustworthiness, the fact that the greatest of the traditionists drew from their two books and relied upon them — even al-Saduq in Ma'ani al-Akhbar and elsewhere — together with Ibn Abi 'Umayr's transmission from them and al-Shaykh's counting their book among the primary works, is perhaps enough to permit reliance upon them. Besides which, we took them from an old, corrected copy in the hand of al-Shaykh Mansur b. al-Hasan al-Abi, who transmitted it from the hand of the eminent Shaykh Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Qummi; the date of its writing was the year three hundred and seventy-four. He mentioned that he took these and the rest of the primary works mentioned hereafter from the hand of the most eminent Shaykh Harun b. Musa al-Tal'ukbari, God have mercy on him. At the beginning of al-Narsi's book he set down his chain thus: "There narrated to us the Shaykh Abu Muhammad Harun b. Musa al-Tal'ukbari, may God support him, who said: There narrated to us Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hamadani, who said: There narrated to us Ja'far b. 'Abd Allah al-'Alawi Abu 'Abd Allah al-Muhammadi, who said: There narrated to us Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr, from Zayd al-Narsi." Chapter Three: The sigla assigned to those books

We set them at the head of every report so that it may be known from which primary work it is taken, and whether it is in a single work or repeated across the works. Where there is a difference in the chain, we set the report down from one of the two books and refer to the other after it, carrying it through to the point of agreement. Where there is a difference in the text that alters the meaning, we make it clear. Where the content is the same but the wording differs and the report suits two chapters, we set it down with one wording in the one chapter and with the other wording in the other.

Let us then set down the sigla: n for 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him; ' for 'Ilal al-Shara'i'; k for Ikmal al-Din; yd for al-Tawhid; l for al-Khisal; li for the Amali of al-Saduq; thw for Thawab al-A'mal; m' for Ma'ani al-Akhbar; hd for al-Hidaya; 'd for al-'Aqa'id. As for the rest of al-Saduq's books and the two books of his father, we had no need of sigla for them, their reports being few. b for Qurb al-Isnad; yr for Basa'ir al-Darajat; ma for the Amali of al-Shaykh; ght for the Ghayba of al-Shaykh; msba for the two Misbahs; sha for al-Irshad; ja for the Majalis of al-Mufid; khts for the Book of al-Ikhtisas. We assigned them no siglum either because they are set down in full in their places, as you have learned; or because our recourse to them is slight, most of their reports being from the wider community; or because the book is of small bulk and its reports few; or because of the absence of complete reliance upon it; or for other such considerations and purposes.

Then know that we have left aside setting down the reports of certain widely transmitted books in this book of ours — such as the four books — because they are widely transmitted and carefully preserved, so that perhaps it is not permissible to expend effort in copying them and leaving them aside. Yet if in some places we need to set down a report from them, these are their sigla: ka for al-Kafi; yb for al-Tahdhib; sa for al-Istibsar; yh for Man la Yahduruhu al-Faqih. When we come to the derivative rulings we shall leave the sigla aside and give the names explicitly, if God the Exalted wills, for benefits particular to that which are not hidden from men of understanding. And there too we shall leave aside the abbreviations in the chains which we have adopted in the following section, given how much the chain is needed there.
Chapter Four: Conventions adopted for abbreviating the chains of transmission

— while guarding against the omission that leads to slight reliance. For most compilers have made a habit of lengthening their mention of the men of a report, so as to adorn the book and multiply the chapters; while some of them drop the chains altogether, so that the reports thereby fall from the rank of those with full chains, and the distinction between reports in strength and weakness, completeness and deficiency, is lost — for it is by the reporter that the standing of the report is known, and it is by reliance upon the transmitters that the loftiness of a narration and a tradition is inferred. So we chose to set down the chain in its entirety while observing the utmost concision: contenting ourselves, in the case of well-known men, with mentioning their father, or their title, or their bare name, without ascription to grandfather or father and without mention of the descriptive epithet, the agnomen and the title; and, where a chain recurs often across the chapters, referring to the whole of it by a siglum, a mark and a convention laid down at the head of the book — so that nothing of the benefits of the primary works should be left out of our book and it thereby fall from the rank of complete acceptability.

Musa al-Rida, peace be upon them both, at Tus in the year one hundred and ninety-eight. In that year we travelled to him by way of Basra, and we came upon 'Abd al-Rahman b. Mahdi ill, so we stayed with him some days; and 'Abd al-Rahman b. Mahdi died, and we attended his funeral, and Isma'il b. Ja'far prayed over him. Then my brother Di'bil and I travelled on to my master and stayed with him until the end of the year two hundred, and we set out for Qum after my master Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, had bestowed upon my brother Di'bil a green silk shirt and a silver ring set with carnelian, and handed him some Ridawi dirhams and said to him: Di'bil, go to Qum, for you will profit there. And he said to him: Guard this shirt well, for I have prayed a thousand rak'as in it (1) and completed the Qur'an in it a thousand times. He related to us by dictation in Rajab of the year one hundred and ninety-eight. He said: There related to me my father Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, God's blessings be upon them all.

And whatever occurs in it with the chain of al-Mujashi'i is what al-Shaykh related. He said: There informed us a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, who said: There related to us al-Fadl b. Muhammad b. al-Musayyab Abu Muhammad al-Sha'rani al-Bayhaqi, at Jurjan, who said: There related to us Harun b. 'Amr b. 'Abd al-'Aziz b. Muhammad Abu Musa al-Mujashi'i, who said: There related to us Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Muhammad, who said: There related to us my father Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him. Al-Mujashi'i said: And there related to us al-Rida 'Ali b. Musa, from his father Musa, from his father Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, from 'Ali, peace be upon him.
In al-Amali: for I have prayed in it a thousand nights, a thousand rak'as each night.

54.text: And everything we mention when citing the reports of the Mustatrafat al-Sara'ir in the Kitab al-Masa'il is a reference to what Ibn Idris — may God have mercy on him — mentioned, where he said: And among that is what we have selected from the book of the questions of the men and their correspondence with our master Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the answers thereto — the narration of Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah b. al-Hasan b. 'Ayyash al-Jawhari, and the narration of 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far al-Himyari, may God be pleased with them both.

And whatever occurs in it as the Nawadir of al-Rawandi with his chain — this is its chain, which I have transcribed as I found it: There informed us the Sayyid, the Imam, Diya' al-Din, chief of the Imams, Shams al-Islam, crown of the Talibids, possessor of the two glories, beauty of the family of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — Abu al-Rida Fadl Allah b. 'Ali b. 'Ubayd Allah al-Hasani al-Rawandi, may God preserve his beauty and perpetuate his excellence. He said: There informed us the Imam, the martyr, Abu al-Mahasin 'Abd al-Wahid b. Isma'il b. Ahmad al-Ruyani, by licence and by audition. He said: There informed us the Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Tamimi al-Bakri, by licence or by audition. He said: There related to us Abu Muhammad Sahl b. Ahmad al-Dibaji, who said: There related to us Abu 'Ali Muhammad b. Muhammad b. al-Ash'ath al-Kufi, who said: There related to me Musa b. Isma'il b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, who said: There related to me my father Isma'il b. Musa, from his father Musa, from his grandfather Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from his father (1) 'Ali b. Abi Talib, God's blessings be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said. I say: from the books of rijal other routes to this book become apparent, which we shall set down at the end of the volumes of this book of ours, if God the Exalted wills.

And whatever occurs in the Kitab Qisas al-Anbiya' with the chain to al-Saduq is what he mentioned in several places. He said: There informed me the Shaykh 'Ali b. 'Abd al-Samad al-Naysaburi, from his father, from the Sayyid Abu al-Barakat 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Khuzi, from al-Saduq, may God have mercy on him. And in another place he said: There informed us the Sayyid Abu al-Harb al-Mujtaba b. al-Da'i al-Husayni, from al-Duristi, from his father, from him. And he said in another place: There informed us the Sayyid Abu al-Samsam Dhu al-Fiqar b. Ahmad b. Ma'bad al-Husayni, from the Shaykh Abu Ja'far al-Tusi, from al-Mufid, from al-Saduq. And in another place: There informed us the Sayyid Abu al-Barakat Muhammad b. Isma'il, from 'Ali b. 'Abd al-Samad, from the Sayyid Abu al-Barakat al-Khuzi. And in a place
So it is in the copies we have.

55.text: other: There informed us the Sayyid (1) Abu al-Qasim b. Kamh, from al-Duristi, from al-Mufid, from al-Saduq. And in another place: There informed us the master Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. al-Marzuban, from al-Duristi, from his father, from him. And in another place: There informed us the litterateur Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn al-Mu'addib al-Qummi, from al-Duristi, from his father, from him. And in another position: There informed us Abu Sa'd al-Hasan b. 'Ali and the Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-Hadiqi, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. al-'Abbas, from his father, from al-Saduq. And in another position: Abu 'Ali al-Fadl b. al-Hasan b. al-Fadl al-Tabrisi, from Ja'far al-Duristi, from al-Mufid, from al-Saduq. And in another place: There informed us the Shaykh Abu al-Husayn Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Muhammad, from Ja'far b. Ahmad, from al-Saduq. And in another spot: There informed us Hibat Allah b. Da'waydar, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Duristi, from Ja'far b. Ahmad al-Marisi, from him. And in another spot: There informed us the Sayyid 'Ali b. Abi Talib al-Saliqi (2), from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. al-'Abbas, from his father, from him. And in another: There informed us Abu al-Sa'adat Hibat Allah b. 'Ali al-Shajari, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. al-'Abbas, from his father. And in another: There informed us the Shaykh Abu al-Mahasin Mas'ud b. 'Ali b. Muhammad, from 'Ali b. 'Abd al-Samad, from 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from him. And in another report: There informed us a group, among them the two brothers Muhammad and 'Ali, the sons of 'Ali b. 'Abd al-Samad, from their father, from the Sayyid Abu al-Barakat 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Husayni, from him.

And as for what is from the Kitab Siffin, I found at the beginning of the book and in its middle, in several places, its chain thus: There informed us the Shaykh, the hafiz, Shaykh al-Islam, Abu al-Barakat 'Abd al-Wahhab b. al-Mubarak b. Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Anmati, who said: There informed us the Shaykh Abu al-Husayn al-Mubarak b. 'Abd al-Jabbar b. Ahmad al-Sayrafi, by my recitation to him in the month of Rabi' al-Akhir of the year four hundred and eighty-four, who said: There informed us Abu Ya'la Ahmad b. 'Abd al-Wahid b. Muhammad b. Ja'far b. al-Wakil, by recitation to him while I listened, in Rajab of the year four hundred and thirty-eight, who said: There informed us Abu al-Hasan Muhammad b. Thabit b. 'Abd Allah b. Muhammad b. Thabit al-Sayrafi, by recitation to him while I listened, who said: There informed us 'Ali b. Muhammad b. 'Uqba b. al-Walid b. Hammam b. 'Abd Allah, by recitation to him in the year three hundred and forty, who said:

56.text: There informed us Abu al-Hasan Muhammad b. Sulayman b. al-Rabi' b. Hisham al-Hindi al-Khazzaz, who said: There informed us Abu al-Fadl Nasr b. Muzahim al-Tamimi. Perhaps this is from a chain of the wider community, since they too have transmitted through him; Ibn Abi al-Hadid related many traditions from him in his commentary on the Nahj al-Balagha, and said: He is in himself reliable, sound in transmission, not ascribed to partisanship nor to corruption, and he is among the men of the people of hadith — end of quotation. And we have extracted most of his reports in the Kitab al-Fitan from the said commentary, so that they may be a proof against those who differ.

As for the chains of our companions to him, they are mentioned in the books of rijal. And I found on the back of the Kitab al-Muqtadab what runs thus: There informed me of it the Shaykh, the Imam, the learned, Najm al-Din Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Musa, from his grandfather Muhammad b. Musa b. Ja'far, from his grandfather Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ahmad b. al-'Ayyash al-Duristi, from al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Isma'il b. Ashnas al-Bazzaz, from its compiler Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Ayyash.

And at the opening of the book of Ibn al-Khashshab was: There informed us the Sayyid, the learned, the jurist, Safi al-Din Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ma'add al-Musawi, in the last ten days of Safar of the year six hundred and sixteen. He said: There informed us the most eminent, the learned, Zayn al-Din Abu al-'Izz Ahmad b. Abi al-Muzaffar Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah b. Muhammad b. Ja'far, by recitation to him, and he acknowledged it — that being at the close of the day of Thursday, the eighth of Safar of the said year, in the City of Peace, at Darb al-Dawabb. He said: There informed us the Shaykh, the Imam, the learned, the peerless, Hujjat al-Islam Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad b. Ahmad b. Ahmad b. al-Khashshab. He said: I recited to the Shaykh Abu Mansur Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Malik b. al-Hasan al-Muqri' on Saturday the twenty-fifth of Muharram of the year five hundred and thirty-one, from his original in the hand of his uncle Abu al-Fadl Ahmad b. al-Hasan, his audition of it from him being recorded therein in his uncle's hand on Friday the sixteenth of Sha'ban of the year four hundred and eighty-four: There informed you Abu al-Fadl Ahmad b. al-Hasan — and he acknowledged it. He said: There informed us Abu 'Ali al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. al-'Abbas b. al-Fadl, by recitation to him while I listened, in Rajab of the year four hundred and twenty-eight. He said: There informed us Ahmad b. Nasr b. 'Abd Allah b. al-Fath, the cultivator of Nahrawan, there, by recitation to him while I listened, in the year three hundred and sixty-five. He said: There related to us Harb b. Ahmad al-Mu'addib, who said: There related to us

57.text: al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-'Ammi al-Basri, from his father, who said: There related to us Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him. Then he repeats the chain from Harb b. Muhammad.

Aban is Ibn 'Uthman. Ahmad al-Hamadani is Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Sa'id Ibn 'Uqda al-Hamadani al-Kufi al-Hafiz — we may express him as Ibn 'Uqda, and at times as Ahmad al-Kufi. Ahmad b. al-Walid is Ibn Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. al-Walid. Ishaq is Ibn 'Ammar. Ayyub is Ibn Nuh — we may express him as Ibn Nuh. Tamim al-Qurashi is Tamim b. 'Abd Allah b. Tamim al-Qurashi, the master of al-Saduq. Tha'laba is Ibn Maymun. Ja'far al-Kufi is Ibn Muhammad. Jamil is Ibn Darraj. Al-Husayn, from his brother, from his father — they are al-Husayn b. Sayf b. 'Amira, from his brother 'Ali, from his father Sayf. Hafs is Ibn Ghiyath the judge. Hamdan is Ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from whom Ibn Qutayba relates. Hamza al-'Alawi is Hamza b. Muhammad b. Ahmad al-'Alawi. Hamawayh is Abu 'Abd Allah Hamawayh b. 'Ali b. Hamawayh al-Nadri — al-Shaykh, may God have mercy on him, said: There informed us, by recitation to him at Baghdad in the house of al-Ghada'iri on Saturday the middle of Dhu al-Qa'da of the year four hundred and thirteen. Hannan is Ibn Sadir. Durust is Ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti. Al-Rayyan is Ibn al-Salt. Sa'd is Ibn 'Abd Allah. Sama'a is Ibn Mihran. Sahl is Ibn Ziyad. Safwan is Ibn Yahya. 'Abd al-A'la is the client of the family of Sam. Al-'Ala', from Muhammad — they are Ibn Razin and Ibn Muslim. 'Allan is 'Ali b. Muhammad, known as 'Allan. 'Ali, from his father, is 'Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim. Furat is Furat b. Ibrahim b. Furat al-Kufi, and usually comes after Ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi. Al-Fadl is Ibn Shadhan. Al-Qasim, from his grandfather, is al-Qasim b. Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid. Muhammad al-Himyari is Ibn 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far. Muhammad b. 'Amir is Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amir. Muhammad al-'Attar is Ibn Yahya. Al-Muzaffar al-'Alawi is Abu Talib al-Muzaffar b. Ja'far b. al-Muzaffar al-'Alawi al-Samarqandi. Ma'mar is Ibn Yahya. Harun is Ibn Muslim. Yunus is Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. Al-Adami is Sahl b. Ziyad. Al-Azdi is Muhammad b. Ziyad, and it may also be applied to Bakr b. Muhammad. Al-Asadi is Abu al-Husayn Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Asadi — we may express him as Muhammad al-Asadi; and al-Asadi at the beginning of

Al-Dabbi is al-'Abbas b. Bakkar. Al-Tatari is 'Ali b. al-Hasan. Al-Talaqani is Muhammad b. Ibrahim b.

Ibn al-Mughira is 'Abd Allah. Ibn Musa is 'Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa, the master of al-Saduq. Ibn al-Muhtadi is al-Hasan b. al-Husayn b. 'Abd al-'Aziz b. al-Muhtadi. Ibn Mihran is Isma'il. Ibn Mahrawayh is 'Ali b. Mahrawayh al-Qazwini. Ibn Mahziyar is 'Ali. Ibn Maymun is 'Abd Allah, expressed at times as al-Qaddah. Ibn Natana is al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana. Ibn Nubata is al-Asbagh. Ibn Nuh is Ayyub. Ibn al-Walid is Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. al-Walid. Ibn Hashim is Ibrahim, the father of 'Ali. Ibn Hammam is Isma'il, and his agnomen is Abu Hammam. Ibn Yazid is Ya'qub.

62.text: Chapter Five: Necessary remarks drawn from the prefaces of the source books

Ibn Shahrashub said in al-Manaqib: The compiling of that book came after a number of the people of learning and religion had granted me licence by audition, by recitation, by handing over, by correspondence and by written authorization; so it became sound for me to relate from them, saying: there related to me, and there informed me, and there announced to me, and I heard.

As for the routes of the wider community: the chain of al-Bukhari is sound for us from Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad b. al-Fadl al-Sa'idi al-Farawi, and from Abu 'Uthman Sa'id b. 'Abd Allah al-'Ayyar al-Su'luki, and from al-Janazi, all of them from Abu al-Maytham al-Kushmayhani, from Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad al-Firabri, from Muhammad b. Isma'il b. al-Mughira al-Bukhari; and from Abu al-Waqt 'Abd al-Awwal b. 'Isa al-Sinjari, from al-Dawudi, from al-Sarakhsi, from al-Firabri, from al-Bukhari.

The chain of Muslim: from al-Farawi, from Abu al-Husayn 'Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi al-Naysaburi, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. 'Amrawayh al-Juludi, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Faqih, from Abu al-Husayn Muslim b. al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi.

The chain of al-Tirmidhi: from Abu Sa'id Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Saffar al-Isfahani, from Abu al-Qasim al-Khuza'i, from Abu Sa'id b. Kulayb al-Shashi, from Abu 'Isa Muhammad b. 'Isa b. Sawra al-Tirmidhi.
The chain of al-Daraqutni: from Abu Bakr Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Yasir al-Jayyani, from al-Mansuri, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mihrabi, from Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Mahdi al-Daraqutni.

The chain of Ma'rifat Usul al-Hadith: from 'Abd al-Latif b. Abi Sa'd al-Baghdadi al-Isfahani, from Abu 'Ali al-Haddad, from al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah al-Naysaburi Ibn al-Rabi'. (1) The chain of al-Muwatta': from al-Qa'nabi, and from Ma'i, from Yahya b. Yahya, by way of Muhammad b. al-Hasan, from Malik b. Anas al-Asbahi.

The chain of the Musnad of al-Shafi'i: from al-Jayyani, from Abu al-Qasim al-Sufi, from Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Sawi, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from al-Rabi', from Muhammad b. Idris al-Shafi'i.

'Ali al-Hulwani (2), from them both; and by right of my narration from al-Sayyid al-Muntaha, from his father Abu Zayd, and from Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Fattal al-Farisi, from his father al-Hasan — both of them from al-Murtada. And al-Muntaha and al-Fattal also heard it by their fathers' recitation to him.
