And al-Firuzabadi said: kabbahu — he overturned him and threw him down, like akabba. And al-Jawhari said: kabbahu upon his face — that is, he threw him down, so akabba he upon his face; and this is among the rarities. And al-Jazari said:
And in the tradition: and does anything cast people upon their nostrils in the Fire but the harvests of their tongues?

that is, what they reap of speech in which there is no good; its singular is hasida, by likening it to what is harvested of crops, and by likening the tongue and what it reaps of speech to the edge of the sickle (2) with which one harvests. And he said: it is said, this is a matter that does not concern me — that is, it does not occupy me nor matter to me. And from it is the tradition: of the goodness of a man's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him — that is, what does not matter to him.

Hisham, a man is not a believer until he is fearing and hoping; and he is not fearing and hoping until he is acting for what he fears and hopes. Hisham, God, majestic and mighty, said: By My might and My majesty and My greatness and My power and My splendour and My exaltedness in My place, no servant prefers My will to his own will but that I place sufficiency in his soul and his concern in his hereafter, and secure for him his livelihood, and make the heavens and the earth guarantee his sustenance, and am for him behind the trade of every trader.

Elucidation: His words, exalted be He, "in My place" — that is, in My rank and the degree of My exaltedness. His words "and secure for him his livelihood": it is said kafaftuhu 'anhu — that is, I turned it away and repelled it. And al-day'a is loss and corruption, and what is
That is, he backbites him and mentions him with the evil that is in him.
With kasra on the mim and quiescence of the nun and fatha on the jim: a curved iron implement with which crops and the like are cut.

151.text: in the way of loss, of family and property and other things. And he said in al-Nihaya: and a man's day'a is what his livelihood comes from, such as craft, trade, agriculture and other things. And from it is the tradition: God has spread out his day'a — that is, He has made his livelihood abundant for him — end of quotation. So it is possible that what is meant is: I have turned away from him his loss and his destruction, by implying the sense of solicitude; or 'ala is in the sense of 'an; or I have turned away from him his earning, in that he does not need it; or I have gathered for him his livelihood, or what of it was in the way of loss — as he said in al-Nihaya: "he does not kaff it", that is, he does not gather it nor draw it together. And from it is the tradition: the believer is the brother of the believer, he gathers for him his livelihood — that is, he gathers for him his means of living and draws it together to him. And this sense is the more evident; but I have not found kaff in this sense save in his words (1). And His words, exalted be He, "and am for him behind the trade of every trader", admits of several aspects. The first: that what is meant is, I am for him behind the trade of the traders, to drive it to him. The second: that what is meant is that I suffice for his important affairs besides what I drive to him of the trade of the traders. The third: that its meaning is, I give him a recompense for what has escaped him of the profits of the traders' trade. And perhaps the first is the more evident.

Hisham, anger is the key of evil. And the most complete of the believers in faith is the best of them in character. And if you mix with people, then if you are able not to mix with any of them save one over whom your hand is the upper, do so.
Elucidation: the upper hand is the giving hand, or the abstaining hand.
Hisham, take to gentleness, for gentleness is a blessing and roughness is an ill omen (2). Gentleness and piety and goodness of character make dwellings flourish and increase sustenance.
Elucidation: al-Firuzabadi said: al-khurq, with damma and with the vowelling, is the opposite of gentleness, and it is not doing work well nor managing affairs well, and it is folly.

Hisham, God's saying "Is the recompense of goodness anything but goodness?" runs in the believer and the unbeliever, the pious and the profligate. Whoever has a kindness done to him, it is incumbent upon him to requite it. And requital is not that you do
Rather this is among the senses which the books of lexicography have recorded.
Al-yumn: blessing; and al-shu'm: its opposite.

152.text: as he did, until you see your own excess; for if you do as he did, his is the excess by the beginning. Hisham, the likeness of this world is the likeness of the serpent: its touch is soft, and in its belly is the killing venom. Men of intellect are wary of it, while children reach for it with their hands. Hisham, be patient upon the obedience of God, and be patient away from the acts of disobedience to God; for this world is but an hour. What has passed of it — you find in it neither joy nor grief; and what has not yet come (1) of it — you do not know it. So be patient upon that hour in which you are, as though you had already been taken away.

Elucidation: in al-Nihaya: everyone who dies without a cause has been i'tubita; and so-and-so died 'abtatan — that is, young and sound. And in some copies it is with the dotted ghayn — that is, if you are patient, then shortly you will become one envied in the hereafter, whose station people will wish for.

Hisham, the likeness of this world is the likeness of the water of the sea: whenever the thirsty man drinks of it, he increases in thirst until it kills him. Hisham, beware of pride; for none enters the Garden in whose heart is the weight of a grain of pride. Pride is God's mantle; so whoever contends with Him for His mantle, God casts him into the Fire upon his face.
Al-Jazari said, in the tradition: God the Exalted said: Greatness is My waist-wrapper and pride is My mantle.

He struck the mantle and the waist-wrapper as a likeness for His being alone in the attribute of greatness and pride — that is, they are not like the rest of the attributes with which creation may be qualified figuratively, such as mercy. And he likened them to the waist-wrapper and the mantle because the one qualified by them is enveloped by them as the mantle envelops a man; and because none shares with him in his waist-wrapper and his mantle — so likewise God, it does not befit that anyone share with Him in the two.

Hisham, he is not of us who does not call himself to account every day: so if he has done well, he seeks increase of it; and if he has done ill, he asks God's forgiveness for it and turns to Him in repentance. Hisham, this world was represented to the Messiah, peace be upon him, in the form of a blue-eyed woman. So he said to her: How many have you married? She said: Many. He said: Did each divorce you? She said: No, rather I killed each one. The Messiah said: Woe to your remaining husbands — how do they not take a lesson from the past ones?
In one copy: and what has not passed.

153.text: Elucidation: blueness in the eye is well known, and it is sometimes applied to blindness. And it is said zariqat his eye towards me — it turned and its white appeared (1). So upon the first, perhaps what is meant is the setting out of its ill omen, for the Arabs take blueness of the eye as an ill omen; or the ugliness of its aspect. And upon the second it is evident. And upon the third it is a figure for the intensity of anger. And the first is the more evident. And wayh is a word of compassion and commiseration, said of one who has fallen into a destruction he does not deserve; and it is sometimes said in the sense of praise and wonder (2). And it is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and is sometimes put in the nominative. Hisham, the light of the body is in its eye: so if the sight is luminous, the whole body is lit. And the light of the spirit is the intellect; so when the servant is possessed of intellect he is knowing of his Lord, and when he is knowing of his Lord he sees his religion clearly; and if he is ignorant of his Lord, no religion stands for him. And as the body does not stand save by the living soul, likewise religion does not stand save by the truthful intention; and the truthful intention is not established save by the intellect. Hisham, the crop grows in the soft ground and does not grow in the hard rock. Likewise wisdom flourishes in the heart of the humble and does not flourish in the heart of the proud tyrant; because God made humility the instrument of the intellect and made pride of the instrument of ignorance. Do you not know that whoever raises his head high to the ceiling, it breaks his head; and whoever lowers his head, it shades him beneath it and shelters him? Likewise whoever does not humble himself before God, God lowers him; and whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him.

Elucidation: al-sahl is the soft ground that accepts the crop; and al-safa is the plural of safat, which is the hard stone that does not grow anything. And ta'muru, with fatha on the ta' and the mim — that is, it lives long; or with damma on the mim — that is, it makes the heart flourishing; or with damma on the ta' and fatha on the mim — that is, wisdom becomes flourishing in the heart. And shamakha — that is, it became tall and high. And shajja his head — that is, it broke it. And al-khafd is the opposite of raising. And akannahu — that is, it covered him and protected him from heat and cold.
Hisham, how ugly is poverty after wealth (3); and how ugly is fault after devotion; and uglier than

And it is sometimes applied to intensity of enmity. It is said: a blue enemy — that is, intense in enmity. And that is because blueness of the eyes predominates among the Byzantines and the Daylamites, and between them and the Arabs was an intense enmity; so they named every enemy by that.
And it is said that it also comes in the sense of wayl. You say: wayh li-Zayd, and wayhan li-Zayd, and wayhahu.

What is meant by poverty is either spiritual poverty — that is, how ugly it is for a man to have inward virtues and noble character, or true beliefs and a pleasing creed, and then to leave them and exchange for them the blameworthy qualities, the base characters or the false beliefs, so that the issue of his affair comes to loss and his end to annihilation. Or what is meant by it is material poverty — that is, how ugly it is for a man to be a possessor of wealth and property and then to squander it and be prodigal with it and spend it upon what neither sets right his world nor earns him reward in his hereafter, so that he becomes poor and comes to need his peers.

154.text: that is the worshipper of God who then leaves his worship.
Elucidation: al-nusuk is the pilgrimage, or worship in general.
Hisham, there is no good in living save for two men: for a listener who retains, and a scholar who speaks.
Elucidation: al-'aysh is life; and wa'ahu — that is, he retained it.

Hisham, nothing more excellent than the intellect has been apportioned among the servants. The sleep of the man of intellect is more excellent than the vigil of the ignorant. And God has not sent a prophet save possessed of intellect, so that his intellect is more excellent than all the striving of those who strive. And the servant has not performed an obligation of God's obligations until he understood from Him.
Elucidation: al-ijtihad is the expending of effort in acts of obedience.

Hisham, the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: When you see the believer much given to silence (1), draw near to him, for he casts wisdom. And the believer is little in speech, much in deed; and the hypocrite is much in speech, little in deed. Hisham, God revealed to David: Say to My servants, let them not set between Me and them a scholar infatuated with this world, for he will turn them away from My remembrance and from the way of My love and My intimate converse. Those are the highwaymen among My servants. Indeed, the least of what I shall do with them is that I strip the sweetness of My worship and My intimate converse from their hearts.
Elucidation: in other reports than this: highwaymen of My servants.

Hisham, whoever magnifies himself in his own soul is cursed by the angels of heaven and the angels of earth. And whoever is proud over his brethren and overbears them has opposed God. And whoever claims what is not his, he is a'na li-ghayr.

Elucidation: "whoever magnifies himself" — that is, he counts himself great. His words a'na li-ghayr — that is, he brings another into toil and trouble, of those to whom his affair is confused, more than what befalls him of that. And it is possible that it is a miscopying of a'ta li-ghayrih, from al-'utuww, which is insolence and tyranny. And that too was possible in the source from which it was taken.
Hisham, God revealed to David: Warn and caution your companions against the love of appetites; for those whose hearts are attached to the appetites of this world, their hearts are veiled from Me (2).
With fatha on the sad and damma on the mim: much given to silence.

That is, their hearts are covered from the disclosure of the splendours of My face and My majesty, and from the shining of the lights of My greatness, and from the knowing of the evidences of My divinity and My beauty; and prevented from the attaining of true sciences in them, because of the alighting of the love of the ornaments of this world in them and their attachment to it.

155.text: Hisham, beware of pride over My friends and of overbearing by your knowledge, lest God detest you; then after His detestation (1) neither your world nor your hereafter will profit you. And be in this world like the dweller of a house that is not his, who only awaits departure. Hisham, sitting with the people of religion is the honour of this world and of the hereafter; and consulting the man of intellect who counsels sincerely is a blessing and an increase and right direction and success from God. So when the man of intellect who counsels sincerely gives you counsel, beware of opposing it, for in that is destruction.
Elucidation: the people of religion are those who know the laws of religion and act by them. And al-'atab, with the vowelling, is destruction.

Hisham, beware of mixing with people and of intimacy with them, unless you find among them one possessed of intellect and trustworthy — then be intimate with him, and flee from the rest of them as you flee from ravening beasts. And it behoves the man of intellect, when he does a deed, to be ashamed before God — since He alone has favoured him with blessings — that he should make anyone other than Him a partner in his deed. And when a matter presses upon you (2) such that you do not know which of the two is better and more right, look which of the two is nearer to your caprice and oppose it; for much reward is in opposing your caprice. And beware of being overcome in wisdom and of placing it in ignorance. Hisham said: So I said to him: And if I find a man seeking, save that his intellect is not wide enough to grasp what I cast to him? He said: Then be gentle with him in counsel; and if his heart is straitened, do not expose yourself to trial. And beware of the rejection of the proud; for knowledge indicates that it be carried to one who does not come to his senses (3). I said: And if I do not find one who understands the asking about them? He said: Then take his ignorance of the asking as a prize, until you are safe from the trial of speech and from the great trial of rejection. And know that God has not raised the humble by the measure of their humility, but has raised them by the measure of His greatness and His glory; and He has not made the fearful secure by the measure of their fear, but has made them secure by the measure of His nobility and His generosity; and He has not gladdened the grieving by the measure of their grief, but
Al-maqt, with fatha on the mim and quiescence of the qaf: intense hatred.
In the printed Tuhaf: and when there passes by you.

His words "indicates": it is possible that it is of the form daraba, yadribu — that is, it is coy and turns aside from being carried to one who has not returned from his intoxication, his swoon and his heedlessness. And in the printed Tuhaf "yujla" in place of "yuhmal" — that is, knowledge is coy and turns aside from being displayed to one who does not come to his senses. And my opinion is that "yuhmal" or "yujla" is a miscopying of "yunjal" — that is, knowledge guides to its being poured out upon one who does not come to his senses; or that in the sentence is a miscopying and an error, and the correct is: for knowledge indicates that it be carried to one who is not able.

156.text: has gladdened them by the measure of His compassion and His mercy. So what is your opinion of the Compassionate, the Merciful, who shows affection to one who harms Him through His friends? How then with one who is harmed for His sake? And what is your opinion of the Ever-Relenting, the Merciful, who relents towards one who is hostile to Him? How then with one who seeks His good pleasure and chooses the enmity of creation for His sake?
Elucidation: al-siba' al-dariya — that is, those addicted to tearing prey and accustomed to it. And hazabahu a matter — that is, it befell him and troubled him.

His words, peace be upon him, "and beware of being overcome in wisdom" — thus in the copy we have. And perhaps in it is an omission and a joining — that is, that you be overcome regarding wisdom, that is, one who does not deserve it takes it from you by force, by reading it in the passive form; or in the active — that is, you overcome wisdom, for it resists whoever does not deserve it. And it is possible that it is with the fa', from al-iflat in the sense of letting loose; for they say infalata minni a speech — that is, it issued without deliberation. His words "then be gentle with him in counsel" — that is, you mention to him something of that wisdom gently, by way of testing. And al-ifaqa is the returning from intoxication, swoon and heedlessness to the state of uprightness. His words "who harms Him through His friends" — that is, by reason of harming them. And tarraddahu — that is, he sought His good pleasure.

Hisham, whoever loves this world, the fear of the hereafter departs from his heart. And no servant is given knowledge and then increases in love for this world but that he increases in distance from God, and God increases in anger against him. Hisham, the man of intellect, the understanding, is he who leaves what he has no power for. And most of what is right is in opposing caprice. And whoever's hope is long, his deed is evil. Hisham, were you to see the journeying of the appointed term, it would divert you from hope.
Elucidation: al-labib is the man of intellect (1); and the qualifying is for clarification and emphasis. And alhaka — that is, it made you heedless.

Hisham, beware of covetousness, and take to despair of what is in people's hands. And put to death covetousness of created beings; for covetousness is the key of lowliness, and the snatching away (2) of the intellect, and the wearing out of manly qualities, and the sullying of

Al-lubb: the intellect pure of impurities, or what is keen of the intellect. So every lubb is intellect, but not conversely. And al-labib is one who possesses lubb; so every labib is a man of intellect, but not conversely.
Al-ikhtilas: swift snatching in a moment of heedlessness, unlike al-istilab, in which heedlessness is not a condition.

157.text: honour, and the taking away of knowledge. And take to holding fast to your Lord and to trusting in Him. And strive against your soul to turn it back from its caprice; for that is incumbent upon you as is the striving against your enemy. Hisham said: Then which of the enemies is the most incumbent to strive against? He said: The nearest of them to you, and the most hostile of them to you, and the most harmful of them to you, and the greatest of them in enmity towards you, and the most hidden of them from you in person despite his nearness to you, and the one who incites your enemies against you — and that is Iblis (1), charged with the whispering of hearts. So against him let your enmity be firm; and let him not be more persevering in striving against you for your destruction than you are in your patience in striving against him. For he is weaker than you in the foundation of his strength, and less than you in harm despite the abundance of his evil — when you hold fast to God; and whoever holds fast to God has been guided to a straight path.

Elucidation: al-ikhtilas is snatching. And ikhlaq of a garment is the wearing of it out. And al-danas is dirt. And the applying in these places is by way of hyperbole. And his words "and who incites" admits of the dotted and the undotted — urging and rousing, as He, exalted be He, said: "Rouse the believers to fight" (2).

Hisham, whoever God has honoured with three, He has been gracious to him: an intellect that suffices him against the burden of his caprice; a knowledge that suffices him against the burden of his ignorance; and a sufficiency that suffices him against the fear of poverty. Hisham, beware of this world and beware of its people; for people in it are of four classes. A man fallen into ruin, embracing his caprice. And a learner, a reciter, who whenever he increases in knowledge increases in pride, making himself high by his recitation and his knowledge over one below him. And an ignorant worshipper who belittles one below him in his worship, loving to be magnified and revered. And a man of insight, a scholar, knowing the way of truth, loving to uphold it — yet he is unable, or overcome, and has no power to uphold what he knows, so he is grieved and distressed by that. And he is the most excellent of the people of his age and the most worthy of them in intellect.

Elucidation: taradda in the well — that is, he fell. And al-mutaraddi — that is, the one fallen into the places of destruction from which escape is hard. And al-mutaqarri' is the devotee, the worshipper; or the one who seeks understanding — that is, one learning recitation. His words "making himself high by his recitation" — it seems it was yasta'li; and it is possible that its sense is implied in it. And al-amthal is the most excellent. And "the most worthy of them in intellect" — perhaps what is meant is that their intellect is more worthy with God than the intellects of others; or they are the worthiest of people for intellect.

Ablasa: his good from God's mercy became little; he despaired. And Iblis is a proper name for Satan; so it is either in the sense of one of little good, or in the sense of one despairing of the mercy of God the Exalted.

158.text: Hisham, know the intellect and its host, and ignorance and its host, and you will be among the rightly guided. Hisham said: So I said: We know only what you have made known to us. So he, peace be upon him, said: Hisham, God created the intellect — and it is the first creature God created among the spiritual beings — on the right of the Throne, from His light. He said to it: Go back — and it went back. Then He said to it: Come forward — and it came forward. So God, majestic and mighty, said: I have created you a great creation and honoured you above all My creation. Then He created ignorance from the bitter, dark sea. He said to it: Go back — and it went back. Then He said to it: Come forward — and it did not come forward. So He said: You have grown proud. And He cursed it. Then He appointed for the intellect seventy-five hosts. And when ignorance saw what God had honoured the intellect with and what He had given it, it concealed enmity towards it, and ignorance said: My Lord, this is a creature like me; You created it and honoured it and strengthened it, and I am its opposite and have no strength against it. Give me of the host the like of what You have given it. So He, blessed and exalted, said: Yes; but if you disobey Me after that, I shall drive you and your host out of My neighbourhood and out of My mercy. It said: I am content. So God gave it seventy-five hosts. And among what He gave the intellect of the seventy-five hosts was: good — and it is the vizier of the intellect; evil — and it is the vizier of ignorance. Faith, unbelief. Assent, denial. Sincerity, hypocrisy. Hope, despondency. Justice, injustice. Contentment, displeasure. Gratitude, ingratitude. Despair, covetousness. Trust, greed. Compassion, harshness. Knowledge, ignorance. Chastity, shamelessness. Abstinence, desire. Gentleness, roughness. Awe, boldness. Humility, pride. Deliberateness, haste. Forbearance, foolishness. Silence, babbling. Submission, haughtiness. Surrender, tyranny. Pardon, rancour. Mercy, hardness. Certainty, doubt. Patience, anxiety. Overlooking, vengeance. Sufficiency, poverty. Reflection, inadvertence. Retention, forgetfulness. Mutual joining, severance. Contentment, greed (1). Mutual sharing, withholding. Love, enmity. Fidelity, treachery. Obedience, disobedience. Submissiveness, overbearing. Safety, affliction. Understanding, obtuseness. Knowing, disavowal. Forbearing courtesy, open contention. Soundness in absence, guile. Concealment, divulging. Piety, undutifulness. Genuineness, procrastination. The good, the reprehensible. Prudent concealment, broadcasting. Equity, wrongdoing. Freedom from envy (2), envy. Cleanliness, filth. Modesty, impudence.
With kasra on the dotted shin: evil, sharpness, briskness and anger, recklessness, greed. And the last is what is meant here.

159.text: Moderation, prodigality. Rest, toil. Ease, difficulty. Well-being, trial. Sufficiency of means, vying for more. Wisdom, caprice. Dignity, levity. Felicity, wretchedness. Repentance, persistence. Fear, carelessness. Supplication, disdaining. Briskness, sloth. Gladness, sorrow. Fellowship, separation. Open-handedness, miserliness. Humility, self-admiration. Truthfulness of speech, talebearing. The seeking of forgiveness, self-deception. Shrewdness, folly (1).
Elucidation: al-nafy is the negating of envy from the soul; and it appears that it has been miscopied. And al-qiha, on the pattern of 'ida, is impudence and little modesty.

Hisham, these qualities are not gathered save for a prophet, or the legatee of a prophet, or a believer whose heart God has tested for faith. As for the rest of that among the believers — one of them does not fail to have in him some of these hosts among the hosts of the intellect, until the intellect becomes complete and he is delivered from the hosts of ignorance; and at that point he is in the highest degree with the prophets and the legatees, peace be upon them. May God grant us and you success in obeying Him.
«30»- al-Durra al-Bahira: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The man of intellect is he who casts off falsehood.
«31»- Da'awat al-Rawandi: al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Much looking into knowledge opens the intellect.
«32»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The tongue of the man of intellect is behind his heart, and the heart of the fool is behind his tongue.

The Sayyid, may God be pleased with him, said: This is among the wondrous, noble meanings. And what is meant by it is that the man of intellect does not let his tongue loose save after consulting deliberation and taking counsel with thought; while the fool's tongue-flingings and the slips (2) of his speech outrun the returning of his thought and the sifting of his judgement. So it is as though the tongue of the man of intellect were a follower of his heart, just as the heart of the fool is a follower of his tongue. And this meaning has been related from him, peace be upon him, in another wording, namely
his words, peace be upon him: The heart of the fool is in his mouth, and the tongue of the man of intellect is in his heart.
and the meaning of the two is one.
«33»- And he, peace be upon him, said: When the intellect is complete, speech diminishes.
«34»- And he, peace be upon him, said: The ignorant is not seen but as one going to excess or one falling short.
The explanation of these qualities has already passed.
The plural of al-falta: his slips and his lapses.

160.text: «35»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: It was said to him, peace be upon him: Describe to us the man of intellect. He said: He is the one who puts each thing in its place. It was said to him: Then describe to us the ignorant. He said: I have done so.

The Sayyid, may God be pleased with him, said: He, peace be upon him, means that the ignorant is the one who does not put things in their places; so the leaving of his description was a description of him, since it was the opposite of the description of the man of intellect.
«36»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: He, peace be upon him, said: There suffices you of your intellect what makes plain to you the way of your error (1) from your right direction.

«37»- And he, peace be upon him, said in his testament to al-Hasan, peace be upon him: And the intellect is the keeping of experiences; and the best of what you have experienced is what has admonished you.

«38»- Kanz al-Karajaki: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The man of intellect is he who obeys God, even if he be of blameworthy aspect and slight account; and the ignorant is he who disobeys God, even if he be of comely aspect and great account. The most excellent of people is the most intelligent of people.
«39»- And it is related from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that he said: The intellect is a birth, and knowledge is an acquisition, and sitting with the learned is an increase.
«40»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever keeps company with an ignorant man diminishes from his intellect.
«41»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Firmness is the head of intellect, and sharpness is the head of folly.
«42»- And he, peace be upon him, said: The anger of the ignorant is in his speech, and the anger of the man of intellect is in his deed.
«43»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Intellects are gifts, and disciplines are acquisitions.
«44»- And he, peace be upon him, said: The corruption of characters is associating with fools, and the setting right of characters is associating with the people of intellect.
«45»- And he, peace be upon him, said: The man of intellect is he whom experiences have admonished.
«46»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Your messenger is the interpreter of your intellect.
«47»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever leaves off listening to the possessors of intellects, his intellect dies.
«48»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever keeps away from his caprice, his intellect is sound.
«49»- And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever is pleased with his own opinion goes astray; and whoever deems himself sufficient by his intellect slips; and whoever is proud over people is abased.
With fatha on the ghayn and with kasra, and doubling of the ya' with fatha: going astray.

161.text: «50»- And he, peace be upon him, said: A man's being pleased with himself is an indication of the weakness of his intellect.
«51»- And he, peace be upon him, said: How wondrous is the man of intellect — how does he look at an appetite whose looking upon it bequeaths him regret?
«52»- And he said: The concern of the intellect is the leaving of sins and the setting right of faults.

«1»- m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar; n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him: my father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Yazid, from 'Ubayd b. Hilal, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, saying: I love that the believer should be one spoken to. He said: I said: And what thing is the one spoken to? He said: The one given understanding.

«2»- 'a, 'Ilal al-Shara'i': my father, from Muhammad al-'Attar, from Ibn Yazid, from al-Bazanti, from Tha'laba, from Mu'ammar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him: What is it with people that they understand and yet do not know? He said: God, blessed and exalted, when He created Adam, set his appointed term between his eyes and his hope behind his back. And when he committed the fault, He set his hope between his eyes and his appointed term behind his back. So from then they understand and do not know.

Elucidation: perhaps what is meant by the appointed term's being between his eyes is his being ever mindful of it, as it is said, so-and-so has set death before his eyes; and by hope's being behind his back, the forgetting of hope and its not occurring to his mind, so that his hope is not long. And this is common in usage and in the language: it is said, he cast it behind his back — that is, he left it and forgot it. So the questioner's meaning is: what is it with people that, being of the people of intellect, they do not know and do not expend their effort as they ought in acquiring knowledge? So the answer is that the cause of that is what befell Adam, peace be upon him, after committing what was less than the best, and passed into his children — the forgetting of death and length of hope; for the recollection of death urges a man to acquire what profits him after death, before its coming; and length of hope entails procrastination in the doing of good and in the seeking of knowledge. And it is possible that the questioner meant by intellect the intellect of livelihood and the managing of the affairs of this world, and by knowledge the knowledge of what profits in the hereafter — that is, what is it with people that in the matter of their world they are men of intellect who let nothing escape them of the interests of their world, while in the matter of their hereafter they are foolish, as though they knew nothing? So the answer is that the cause of that is the forgetting of death and length of hope; for these two entail the leaving of what

162.text: profits in the hereafter, since it is forgotten, and the confining of one's concern to the acquiring of livelihood and to the mending of the affairs of this world, since these are ever before his eyes. And it is also possible that what is meant by intellect is the knowledge of what profits in the hereafter, and what is meant by knowledge is the complete knowledge that bequeaths action. So what is meant is: what is it with people that they know death and the reckoning and the punishment and believe in them, yet the trace of that knowledge does not appear in their deeds, so that in the faults they commit they are as though they knew nothing of that? And the answer is evident. And it appears that here is a miscopying from the copyists, and it was la ya'malun, with the mim before the lam; so it comes back to what we mentioned last. And God knows.
Chapters on Knowledge: its etiquette, its kinds and its rulings
Chapter 1: The obligation of knowledge, the duty of seeking it, encouragement toward it, and the reward of the scholar and the student
Al-Baqara: "and increased him amply in knowledge"
Al-A'raf: "Thus do We set out the signs in detail for a people who know"; and He, exalted be He, said: "but most people do not know"

Al-Tawba: "and We set out the signs in detail for a people who know"; and He said: "God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know"; and He said: "The bedouin are more intense in unbelief and hypocrisy, and more fitted not to know the bounds of what God has sent down upon His Messenger"; and He, exalted be He, said: "Why then should not a party of every group among them go forth, that they may gain understanding in religion and warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may beware"; and He said: "God has turned away their hearts, because they are a people who do not comprehend"
Yunus: "He sets out the signs in detail for a people who know"
Yusuf: "We raise in degrees whom We will; and above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows"
Al-Ra'd: "Is then he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like him who is blind? Only the possessors of understanding take heed"
Ta Ha: "And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge"

163.text: Al-Anbiya': "And Lot — We gave him judgement and knowledge"; and He, exalted be He, said: "And to each We gave judgement and knowledge"
Al-Hajj: "and that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, and so believe in it, and their hearts be humbled to Him"

Al-Naml: "And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said: Praise be to God, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants"; and He, exalted be He, said: "Surely in that is a sign for a people who know"; and He, glory be to Him, said: "Nay, most of them do not know"

Al-Qasas: "And when he reached his full strength and was made even, We gave him judgement and knowledge"; and He, exalted be He, said: "And those who had been given knowledge said: Woe to you, the reward of God is better for one who believes and does righteousness"
Al-'Ankabut: "and none understands them but those who know"; and He, exalted be He, said: "Nay, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge"

Al-Rum: "Surely in that are signs for those who know"; and He, glory be to Him, said: "And those who had been given knowledge and faith said: You have tarried, in God's decree, until the Day of the Raising; and this is the Day of the Raising — but you did not know"; and He, exalted be He, said: "Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know"
Saba': "And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth"
Al-Zumar: "Say: are those who know equal with those who do not know? Only the possessors of understanding take heed"
Al-Fath: "Nay, they comprehended only a little"
Al-Rahman: "He taught the Qur'an. He created man. He taught him the clear expression"
Al-Mujadala: "God raises in degrees those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge"
Al-Hashr: "That is because they are a people who do not comprehend"
Al-Munafiqun: "but the hypocrites do not comprehend"; and He, exalted be He, said: "but the hypocrites do not know"
Al-'Alaq: "And your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know"
«1»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: al-Sinani, from al-Asadi, from al-Nakha'i, from al-Nawfali, from Muhammad b. Sinan,

164.text: from al-Mufaddal, from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The most knowing of people is he who gathers the knowledge of people to his own knowledge; and the greatest of people in worth is the most abundant of them in knowledge; and the least of people in worth is the least of them in knowledge.
I say: the report in full is in the chapter of the admonitions of the Messenger, may God bless him and his family.

«2»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: al-Muktib, from 'Ali, from his father, from al-Qaddah, from al-Sadiq, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever travels a road seeking knowledge in it, God travels with him a road to the Garden. And the angels lower their wings to the seeker of knowledge, in contentment with him. And there seek forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge whoever is in heaven and whoever is on earth, even the fish in the sea. And the excellence of the scholar over the worshipper is as the excellence of the moon over the rest of the stars on the night of the full moon. And the learned are the heirs of the prophets: the prophets bequeathed neither dinar nor dirham, but they bequeathed knowledge; so whoever takes of it has taken an ample portion.

thw, Thawab al-A'mal: my father, from 'Ali, from his father, the like of it. — yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ahmad b. Muhammad, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Hammad b. 'Isa, from al-Qaddah (1), the like of it. Elucidation: "God travels with him" — the ba' is for transitivity, that is, God causes him to travel on a road leading to the Garden in the hereafter; or in this world, by granting him success in a deed among the deeds of good that brings him to the Garden. And in the route of the wider community: God makes easy for him a road among the roads of the Garden. His words, peace be upon him, "they lower their wings" — that is, that they may be a carpet for him when he walks. And it is said it is in the sense of humility, in magnifying his due; or of tenderness, in kindness to him, since the bird spreads its wing over its chicks. And He, exalted be He, said: "And lower your wing to the believers" (2); and He, glory be to Him, said: "And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy" (3). And it is said what is meant is their alighting at the gatherings of knowledge and their leaving off flying. And it is said he meant by it their shading them with them. And it is said its meaning is the spreading of the wing to carry him

He is 'Abd Allah b. Maymun b. al-Aswad al-Qaddah, client of Banu Makhzum, who trimmed arrow-shafts. The authors of biographical entries gave his entry in their books. Al-Najashi said in his Rijal, p. 148, after giving his entry as we have given it: His father related from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon them both; and he himself relates from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, and he was trustworthy. He has books, among them the Book of the Sending of the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — and his reports; and the Book of the Description of the Garden and the Fire. And al-Kashshi related in his Rijal, p. 160, by his chain from Abu Khalid, from him, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, that he said: Son of Maymun, how many are you at Mecca? I said: We are four. He said: You are a light in the darknesses of the earth. And Ibn al-Nadim counted him in his Fihrist among the jurists of the Shi'a.

165.text: upon them, and to carry him where he wishes of the lands. And its meaning is help in the seeking of knowledge. And the first is supported by what will come of the report of al-Miqdad (1). His words "in contentment with him" is an object of cause; and it is possible that it is a circumstantial expression by construal — that is, being content, not compelled. His words, peace be upon him, "they bequeathed neither dinar nor dirham" — that is, the greatest part of their inheritance was knowledge. And it is possible to construe it literally, in that there did not remain of them a dinar nor a dirham.

«3»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq, in a sermon which the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, delivered after the passing of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family: And there is no treasure more profitable than knowledge.

«4»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq; n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him — among the sayings of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, in the narration of 'Abd al-'Azim al-Hasani: The worth of every man is what he does well.
l, al-Khisal, by another narration; it will come among his admonitions, peace be upon him.

«5»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, from 'Ubayd Allah b. al-Hasan b. Ibrahim al-'Alawi, from his father, from 'Abd al-'Azim al-Hasani al-Razi (2), from Abu Ja'far the Second, from his forefathers, from 'Ali,

Al-Najashi set him down in his Rijal, p. 173, saying: 'Abd al-'Azim b. 'Abd Allah b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Zayd b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them, Abu al-Qasim; he has a book of the sermons of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn b. 'Ubayd Allah said: There related to us Ja'far b. Muhammad Abu al-Qasim, who said: There related to us 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, who said: There related to us Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid al-Barqi, who said: 'Abd al-'Azim came to Rayy fleeing from the sultan and dwelt in a cellar in the house of a man of the Shi'a in the Lane of the Clients. He would worship God in that cellar, fasting his day and standing his night; and he would go out concealed and visit the grave facing his own grave, with the road between them, and say: it is the grave of a man of the children of Musa b. Ja'far, peace be upon him. He continued to take shelter in that cellar, and news of him reached one after another of the Shi'a of the family of Muhammad, peace be upon them, until most of them knew him. Then a man of the Shi'a saw in a dream the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, who said to him: a man of my descendants will be carried from the Lane of the Clients and buried by the apple tree in the garden of 'Abd al-Jabbar b. 'Abd al-Wahhab — and he pointed to the place in which he was buried. So the man went to buy the tree and its place from its owner, who said to him: For what do you seek the tree and its place? So he told him of the vision. And the owner of the tree mentioned that he had seen the like of this vision, and that he had made the place of the tree together with the whole garden an endowment for the noble, and the Shi'a bury in it. Then 'Abd al-'Azim fell ill and died, God's mercy be upon him; and when he was stripped to be washed, there was found in his pocket a note in which was the mention of his lineage. And al-Saduq related in the book Thawab al-A'mal, p. 56, on the excellence of visiting him, a narration by his chain from 'Ali b. Ahmad, from Hamza b. al-Qasim al-'Alawi, from Muhammad b. Yahya al-'Attar, from one of the people of Rayy who entered upon Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Muhammad al-Hadi, peace be upon him, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-'Askari, peace be upon him, and he said: Where have you been? I said: I visited al-Husayn, peace be upon him. He said: Indeed, had you visited the grave of 'Abd al-'Azim among you, you would have been like one who visited al-Husayn b. 'Ali, peace be upon them both.

166.text: peace be upon him, who said: I said four things, and God the Exalted sent down confirmation of me in them in His Book. I said: A man is hidden beneath his tongue; when he speaks, he appears. So God the Exalted sent down: "and you will surely know them by the cast of their speech." I said: Whoever is ignorant of a thing is hostile to it. So God sent down: "Nay, they cried lies to what they did not encompass in knowledge." And I said: The measure — or the worth — of every man is what he does well. So God sent down, in the story of Talut: "God has chosen him over you and increased him amply in knowledge and in body." And I said: Killing lessens killing. So God sent down: "And in retaliation there is life for you, O possessors of understanding."

Elucidation: "hidden" — that is, veiled beneath his tongue; neither his completeness nor his deficiency is known, nor his truthfulness and his certainty, nor his lying and his hypocrisy, save when he speaks. And His words, exalted be He, "and you will surely know them", are the answer to an omitted oath. And "the cast of speech" is its manner and its inclining towards a side of allusion and equivocation. And from it the one who errs is called lahin, because he turns speech away from what is correct. And al-basta is amplitude.

«6»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: Muhammad b. al-'Abbas the grammarian, from 'Abd Allah b. al-Faraj, from Sa'id b. al-Aws al-Ansari, who said: I heard al-Khalil b. Ahmad saying: The most urging word to the seeking of knowledge is the saying of 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both: The measure of every man is what he does well.
Elucidation: al-Jawhari said: he yuhsinu a thing — that is, he knows it.

«7»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: my father, from Sa'id, from al-Yaqtini, from Yusuf b. 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Hasan b. Ziyad al-'Attar, from Ibn Tarif, from Ibn Nubata, who said: The Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, said: Learn knowledge; for the learning of it is a good deed, and the studying of it is a glorification, and the searching into it is a striving, and the teaching of it to one who does not know it is a charity. And it is an intimate in desolation, and a companion in solitude, and a weapon against enemies, and the adornment of friends. By it God raises up peoples and makes them leaders in good, followed as examples; their deeds are watched and their traces are taken as a light. The angels desire their friendship and stroke them with their wings in their prayers — because knowledge is the life of hearts, and the light of eyes from blindness, and the strength of bodies from weakness. And God settles its bearer in the stations of the righteous and grants him the company of the best in this world and in the hereafter. By knowledge God is obeyed and worshipped; and by knowledge God is known and declared one; and by knowledge the ties of kinship are joined; and by it the lawful and the unlawful are known. And knowledge is the leader of the intellect, and the intellect is its follower. God inspires it in the felicitous and withholds it from the wretched.
«8»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Yaqtini, from a group of his companions, raising it to the Commander of the Faithful,

167.text: peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Learn knowledge — the report.

Except that in it, in place of "with God for its people", is "the bestowing of it upon its people"; and after his words "in solitude", "and an indication in prosperity and in adversity"; and after his words "in their prayers", "and there seeks forgiveness for them everything, even the fish of the seas and their creeping things, and the beasts of the land and its cattle"; and in place of al-abrar, al-akhyar, and in place of al-akhyar, al-abrar. I say: the like of that has been related in f from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family. Elucidation: it is said ramaqtuhu — that is, I looked at him; that is, people look at their deeds so as to follow them as examples. And "the light of eyes" — that is, the eyes of hearts. And "the strength of bodies" — since by knowledge and certainty the limbs are strengthened for action.

«9»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from 'Ali, from his father, from Ibn Maymun (1), from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The excellence of knowledge is more beloved to God than the excellence of worship; and the most excellent of your religion is scrupulousness.
Elucidation: that is, the most excellent of the deeds of your religion.

«10»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Ahmad b. Idris, from al-Ash'ari, from Ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali (2), from his brother, from his father, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was asked about the most knowing of people. He said: He who gathers the knowledge of people to his own knowledge.

«11»- l, al-Khisal: al-Khalil b. Ahmad, from Ibn Mani', from Harun b. 'Abd Allah, from Sulayman b. 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi, from Khalid b. Abi Khalid al-Arzaq, from Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Rahman — and I think he is Ibn Abi Layla — from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — that he said: The most excellent of worship is understanding of religion, and the most excellent of religion is scrupulousness.
«12»- l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Mughira, with his chain, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers,
He is 'Abd Allah b. Maymun al-Qaddah, whose entry has already been given at the end of the second tradition.

What is meant by him is 'Ali b. Sayf b. 'Amira; and by his brother, al-Husayn b. Sayf; and by his father, Sayf b. 'Amira. And 'Amira is on the pattern of safina. As for Sayf, he was of Kufa, trustworthy; he related from al-Sadiq and al-Kazim, peace be upon them both, and the scholars of rijal declared him trustworthy. As for al-Husayn, al-Shaykh set him down and mentioned him with neither praise nor blame, save that he has two books which the men relate from him. As for 'Ali, al-Najashi gave his entry and declared him trustworthy.

168.text: from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no good in living save for two men: a scholar who is obeyed, or a listener who retains.

«13»- Nawadir al-Rawandi, with his chain from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — who said: There is no good in living save for a listener who retains or a scholar who speaks.

«14»- And by this chain he said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Four are binding upon every possessor of discernment and intellect of my community. It was said: Messenger of God, what are they? He said: The hearing of knowledge, and the keeping of it, and the spreading of it among its people, and the acting by it.

«15»- l, al-Khisal: Majilawayh, from his uncle, from al-Barqi, from his father, from a number of his companions, raising it to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: Two greedy ones are never sated: one greedy for knowledge and one greedy for wealth.
Elucidation: al-Jawhari said: al-nahma is the reaching of one's aim in a thing; and nahima with such a thing, so he is manhum — that is, addicted to it. And
in the tradition: two greedy ones are never sated: one greedy for wealth and one greedy for knowledge.

«16»- l, al-Khisal: it will come among the noble characters of 'Ali b. al-Husayn, God's blessings be upon him, that he, peace be upon him, when a seeker of knowledge came to him, would say: Welcome to the testament of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family. Then he would say: When the seeker of knowledge goes out from his dwelling, he does not set his foot upon anything moist or dry of the earth but that it glorifies for him down to the seventh earths.

Elucidation: it is possible that what is meant by the glorification of the earth is the glorification of its people among the angels and the jinn. And it is possible that what is meant is that there is written for him the like of the reward of this supposed glorification. And it has been said that there is a weak perception in inanimate things; but al-Sayyid al-Murtada said that that is contrary to a necessary tenet of religion (1). And it is possible that what is meant by the glorification of inanimate things and of animals is what reaches the scholar of rewards in exchange for them, since the scholar has a part in their subsisting and their ordering and the profiting of the rest of creation by them; so the scholar is rewarded in exchange for each of them, as though they glorified for him. And God knows.
«17»- n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him, with the Tamimi chain, from al-Rida, from his forefathers, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: Knowledge is the believer's lost thing.
No ground has appeared for his words, may God have mercy on him; and the apparent sense of the Qur'anic verses is contrary to it, and there are evidences from the reports upon it.

169.text: «18»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from al-Maraghi, from 'Ali b. al-Hasan, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Marwan, from his father, from Ahmad b. 'Isa, from Muhammad b. Ja'far, from his father Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Two qualities (1) are not gathered in the hypocrite: understanding in Islam, and a goodly bearing in the face.

Nawadir al-Rawandi, with his chain from al-Kazim, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — the like of it. Elucidation: al-samt is the bearing of the people of good.

«19»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from Ibn Quluwayh, from Ibn 'Amir, from al-Isfahani, from al-Minqari, from Hammad b. 'Isa, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Among what Luqman admonished his son was that he said to him: My son, set in your days and your nights and your hours a portion for yourself in the seeking of knowledge; for you will never find a squandering of it like the leaving of it.

fs, the Tafsir of al-Qummi: my father, from al-Isfahani, the like of it. Elucidation: its meaning is the urging to persevere in the seeking of knowledge and the studying of it; for the leaving of it entails the loss of what has been attained, and its going and its being forgotten.

«20»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from al-Ju'abi, who said: There related to me the righteous Shaykh 'Abd Allah b. Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah b. Yasin, who said: I heard the righteous servant 'Ali b. Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him, at Surra Man Ra'a, mentioning from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Knowledge is a noble inheritance, and disciplines are fair garments, and thought is a clear mirror, and the making of excuse is a warner who counsels. And it suffices you as discipline for yourself that you leave what you dislike for another.

ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: al-Ju'abi, the like of it. Elucidation: his words, peace be upon him, "and the making of excuse is a warner who counsels" — that is, there suffices for the leaving of acts of disobedience and of evils what follows upon them of the making of excuse; so how much more with the fear of punishment. And it seems to be a miscopying, and the more evident is al-i'tibar, as in the Nahj al-Balagha and elsewhere.
With fatha on the kha' and the doubled lam: the two qualities.

170.text: «21»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Hallal, from al-Hasan b. al-Husayn al-Ansari, from Zufar b. Sulayman, from Ashras al-Khurasani, from Ayyub al-Sijistani, from Abu Qilaba, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever goes out from his house seeking knowledge, seventy thousand angels escort him, seeking forgiveness for him.

«22»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi, with the chain of Abu Qatada, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: I do not love to see the young man among you save going forth early (1) in one of two states: either a scholar or a learner. For if he does not do so, he falls short; and if he falls short, he squanders; and if he squanders, he sins; and if he sins, he dwells in the Fire — by Him who sent Muhammad with the truth.

«23»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, from Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. al-Mufaddal al-Du'ali, from 'Abd al-Hamid b. Sabih, from Hammad b. Zayd, from Abu Harun al-'Abdi (2), who said: When we came to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (3) he would say: Welcome to the testament of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family. I heard the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — saying: There will come to you a people from the regions of the earth seeking understanding in religion; so when you see them, treat them well. He said: And he would say: And you are the testament of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family.

The author of Tanqih al-Maqal set him down in vol. 3, p. 38, of the agnomens, and said: I have not come upon his name nor his state in the books of our companions. Yes — from Ibn Hajar in al-Taqrib, that he gave his entry and said: his name is 'Umara b. Juwayn, with jim, in the diminutive; well known by his agnomen; abandoned, and accused by one who called him a liar; a Shi'i of the fourth generation; he died in the year 134.

Ascribed to Khudra — with damma on the kha', quiescence of the dal and fatha on the ra' — and it is a clan of the Helpers. His name is Sa'd b. Malik b. Sinan b. 'Ubayd b. Tha'laba al-Abjar; and al-Abjar is Khudra b. 'Awf b. al-Harith b. al-Khazraj. The particular and the general gave his entry in their books. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr counted him in al-Isti'ab (vol. 2, at the foot of p. 44 of al-Isaba) among the Companions and said: his first battle was the Trench, and he campaigned with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant him peace, in twelve campaigns; and he was among those who preserved from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, many practices, and much knowledge was related from him; and he was among the noble of the Helpers and their learned and their excellent. He died in the year 74, and a group of the Companions and a group of the Successors related from him. And the author of al-Isaba (vol. 2, p. 33) transmitted, on the date of his death, three other opinions: the years 63, 64 and 65; and he said: he was deemed too young at Uhud, and his father was martyred there. And al-Kashshi transmitted at p. 25 of his Rijal, from al-Fadl b. Shadhan, that he was among the foremost who returned to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; and he set down at p. 26 narrations indicating his praise and that he was upright. And at p. 131 of al-Tahdhib is a narration indicating his uprightness.

171.text: «24»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Hasani, may God have mercy on him, from Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Zayd b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, who said: There related to me al-Rida 'Ali b. Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa b. Ja'far, from his father Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father Muhammad b. 'Ali, from his father 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn, from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — saying: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. So seek knowledge in the places where it is to be looked for, and take it as a light from its people; for the teaching of it for God's sake is a good deed, and the seeking of it is worship, and the discussing of it is a glorification, and the acting by it is a striving, and the teaching of it to one who does not know it is a charity, and the bestowing of it upon its people is a means of nearness to God the Exalted. Because it is the marks of the lawful and the unlawful, and the beacon of the paths of the Garden, and the intimate in desolation, and the companion in exile and in solitude, and the speaker in seclusion, and the indication in prosperity and in adversity, and the weapon against enemies, and the adornment among friends. By it God raises up peoples and makes them leaders in good: their traces are taken as a light, and guidance is sought by their deeds, and recourse is had to their judgement. And the angels desire their friendship, and with their wings they stroke them, and in their prayers they bless them. There seeks forgiveness for them everything moist and dry, even the fish of the sea and its creeping things, and the beasts of the land and its cattle. Knowledge is the life of hearts from ignorance, and the light of eyes from darkness, and the strength of bodies from weakness. It brings the servant to the stations of the best and the gatherings of the righteous, and to the highest degrees in this world and in the hereafter. Remembrance in it equals fasting, and the studying of it equals night-vigil. By it the Lord is obeyed and worshipped; and by it the ties of kinship are joined; and by it the lawful and the unlawful are known. Knowledge is the leader of action, and action is its follower. He inspires it in the felicitous and withholds it from the wretched. So blessed is he whom God does not deprive of his portion of it.

Abu al-Mufaddal said: And there related to us Ja'far b. 'Isa b. Mudrik the date-seller, from Muhammad b. Muslim al-Razi, from Hisham b. 'Abd Allah, from Kinana b. Jabala, from 'Asim b. Raja', from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman b. Ghanm, from Mu'adh b. Jabal, who said: Learn knowledge, for the teaching of it for God's sake is a good deed — and he mentioned the like of it.

He said: And there related to us Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Shadhan al-Azdi, from Kathir b. Muhammad al-Khuzami, from Hasan b. Husayn al-'Arabi, from Yahya b. Ya'la, from Asbat b. Nasr, from a shaykh of the people of

172.text: Basra, from Anas b. Malik, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Learn knowledge, for the teaching of it for God's sake is a good deed — and he mentioned the like of the tradition of al-Rida, peace be upon him.

«»- 'udda, 'Uddat al-Da'i: the author of the book Muntaqa al-Yawaqit related it therein, raised to Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn, and mentioned the like of it. Elucidation: it is said iqtabastu from him a fire, and iqtabastu from him knowledge — that is, I gained it. And al-manar is the marker of the road. And the angels' stroking with their wings is either to show friendship, or to convey blessing, or to gain it.

«25»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi, with the chain of al-Mujashi'i, from Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The scholar among the ignorant is like the living among the dead. And there seeks forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge everything, even the fish of the sea and its creeping things, and the beasts of the land and its cattle. So seek knowledge, for it is the link between you and God, Almighty and Glorious. And the seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.
ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: al-Ju'abi, from Ibn 'Uqda, from Harun b. 'Amr al-Mujashi'i, from Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon him, the like of it.

«26»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan b. Zayd b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from his father, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. Indeed, God loves the seekers (1) of knowledge.

«27»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Muhammad b. Hassan, from Muhammad b. 'Ali, from 'Isa b. 'Abd Allah al-'Umari, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation in every state.
«28»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat, by this chain, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation among the obligations of God.
yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah, from 'Isa b. 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad b. 'Umar b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, the like of it.

«29»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from a man of our companions, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.
With damma on the ba', the plural of baghin — that is, seeker.

173.text: Elucidation: These reports indicate the obligation of seeking knowledge. And there is no doubt as to the obligation of seeking the necessary measure of the knowledge of God and His attributes and the rest of the principles of religion, and of the knowledge of the acts of worship and their conditions and of the prohibitions — even if by taking it from a scholar — as an individual obligation. And the more widely held view among the companions is that the acquiring of more than that is either among the collective obligations or among the recommended acts.

«30»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: For the seeker of knowledge everything seeks forgiveness, even the fish in the seas and the birds in the air of heaven.

«31»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: al-Hasan b. 'Ali, from al-'Abbas b. 'Amir, from Fudayl b. 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubayda (1), from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: Indeed all the beasts of the earth pray for the seeker of knowledge, even the fish in the sea.
«32»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ahmad b. Muhammad, from 'Ali b. al-Hakam, from Fudayl b. 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him — the like of it.

«33»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn b. Sayf, from his father, from Wahb b. Sa'id, from Husayn b. al-Sabbah, from Jarir b. 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, who said: God revealed to me that whoever travels a path in which he seeks knowledge, I make easy for him a road to the Garden.

«34»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn b. Sayf, from his father, from Sulayman b. 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah b. al-Hasan b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali, from his father, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The seeker of knowledge is escorted by seventy thousand angels from the crown of heaven, saying: Bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

Elucidation: the mafriq of the head is its middle; and it was annexed to heaven because it lies in its direction, or what is meant by it is the middle of heaven. And perhaps there is an omission in it, and it was: from the crown of his head to heaven.

«35»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ahmad b. Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Amr b. Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The scholar and the learner are partners in the reward; for the scholar

In the diminutive. He is Ziyad b. 'Isa, or Raja', of the companions of al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, peace be upon them both; he related from them both. The scholars of rijal gave his entry and declared him trustworthy. He accompanied Abu Ja'far to Mecca, and he was of good standing with the family of Muhammad. He died in the time of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him; and he had a sister named Hammada who relates from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him.

174.text: there are two rewards, and for the learner one reward; and there is no good in any beside that.

«36»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from 'Amr b. 'Uthman and Ibn Faddal together, from Jamil, from Muhammad b. Muslim, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: Indeed he among you who has learned knowledge has the like of the reward of him who teaches it, and the latter has the excellence over him. Learn knowledge from the bearers of knowledge, and teach it to your brethren as the scholars taught you.
Elucidation: the pronoun in "for him" refers back to the teacher. And his words "as they taught you" — that is, without alteration; and it is possible that the kaf is causal.

«37»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ahmad b. Muhammad, from Muhammad b. 'Ali, from al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Yusuf, from Muqatil, from al-Rabi' b. Muhammad, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: There is no servant who goes forth at morning in the seeking of knowledge and returns at evening but that he plunges into mercy, a plunging.
Elucidation: "he plunges into mercy" — that is, he enters into it such that it encompasses him.

«38»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad al-Barqi, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The scholar and the learner are equal in reward.
Elucidation: that is, in the root of the reward, not in its measure — lest it contradict the other reports.

«39»- thw, Thawab al-A'mal: Majiluwayh, from his uncle, from al-Kufi, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Yusuf, from Muqatil b. Muqatil, from al-Rabi' b. Muhammad, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: There is no servant who goes forth at morning in the seeking of knowledge, or returns at evening, but that he plunges into mercy, and the angels call out to him: Welcome, O visitor of God! and he travels in the Garden the like of that path.
Elucidation: whoever visits the scholar for God and for the seeking of knowledge for the face of God, it is as though he had visited God.

«40»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Abu Sukhayla (1), from the Commander of the Faithful, God's blessings be upon him, who said: O people, there is no good in a religion in which there is no understanding, and no good in a world in which there is no reflection, and no good in devotion in which there is no scrupulousness.
Elucidation: perhaps what is meant by reflection upon the world is management in it, and the abandoning of extravagance and of stinting;

With damma on the undotted sin and fatha on the dotted kha'. Al-Shaykh counted him among the companions of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. His name is 'Asim b. Tarif; and on p. 17 of al-Kashshi is a narration indicating the goodness of his state.

175.text: or the pondering of its passing away and of what calls to the abandoning of it. And al-nusuk is worship, and al-wara' is the shunning of forbidden things, or of doubtful things as well.

«41»- f, Tuhaf al-'Uqul, from the Commander of the Faithful, God's blessings be upon him, who said: O people, know that the perfection of religion is the seeking of knowledge and the acting by it; and that the seeking of knowledge is more incumbent upon you than the seeking of wealth. Indeed wealth is apportioned among you, guaranteed to you; a Just One has apportioned it among you and has guaranteed it, and He will fulfil it to you (1). But knowledge is stored up for you with its people; you have been commanded to seek it from them, so seek it. And know that abundance of wealth is a corruption for religion, a hardening for hearts; and that abundance of knowledge and the acting by it is a good for religion, a cause of the Garden. Expenditures diminish wealth, but knowledge grows by its expending; and the expending of it is its spreading (2) to those who preserve it and relate it. And know that the companionship of the scholar and the following of him is a religion by which God is served, and that obedience to him is a gaining of good deeds, an erasing of evil deeds, a treasure for the believers, an elevation in their lifetimes, and a fair mention of them after their death. Indeed knowledge has many excellences: its head is humility, its eye is freedom from envy, its ear is understanding, its tongue is truthfulness, its retention is examination, its heart is goodness of intention, its intellect is the knowledge of the causes of things, its hand is mercy, its resolve is soundness, its foot is the visiting of the scholars, its wisdom is scrupulousness, its abode is deliverance, its benefit is well-being, its mount is fidelity, its weapon is gentleness of speech, its sword is contentment, its bow is forbearance, its army is discourse with the scholars, its wealth is refinement (3), its treasure is the shunning of sins, its provision is kindness, its shelter is peaceableness, its guide is right guidance, and its comrade is the fellowship of the good.

Elucidation: mafsada and maksaba and their like — each of them is either an active participle, or a mimic verbal noun, or a noun of instrument, or a noun of place; and in some of them certain of these possibilities are inadmissible, as is not hidden. And al-uhdutha with damma is that which is talked of. Then he, peace be upon him, intended to draw attention to the excellences of knowledge, so he likened it to a complete spiritual person having limbs and faculties, all of them spiritual, some of them outward and some of them inward. The outward are like the head, the eye, the ear, the tongue, the hand and the foot; and the inward like retention, the heart, the intellect, resolve and wisdom. And it has a spiritual abode, and a mount, and a weapon, and a sword, and a bow, and an army
And in one copy: wa sa-yafi lakum bihi.
batha the report: he broadcast it and spread it.
A disposition that preserves the one in whom it is from what disgraces him.

176.text: and wealth, and a treasure, and provision, and a shelter, and a guide, and a comrade — all of them inward and spiritual. Then he, peace be upon him, set forth the correspondence of this spiritual person, in all its parts, to this bodily frame, in completion of the likeness and in declaration that knowledge, when it settles in the heart of a man, takes possession of all his limbs and its effects appear from every one of them. So the head of knowledge, which is humility, takes possession of this bodily head and drives out from it pride and haughtiness, of which it is the seat, and employs it in what humility requires of brokenness and self-abasement. And just as the bodily head, by its removal, removes the life of the body, so likewise by the removal of humility before the Creator and the creatures the life of knowledge is removed, and it becomes like a body without a spirit, not becoming a source of any effect. And these two aspects are to be observed in all the clauses; and the mention of them would occasion prolixity, and what we have mentioned suffices those possessed of understanding.

«42»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Yunus, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: There is no latitude for people until they ask or gain understanding.

«43»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father and Musa b. al-Qasim, from Yunus, from some of our companions, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far, peace be upon them both, was asked: Is there latitude for people in leaving off the asking about what they have need of? He said: No.

«44»- sn, al-Mahasin: al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Fie upon every Muslim who does not set aside in every week a day in which he gains understanding of the matter of his religion and asks about his religion. And some have related: Fie upon every Muslim man.
Elucidation: what is meant by al-jum'a is the week — naming the whole by the name of the part.

«45»- sn, al-Mahasin: Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said in a discourse of his: Let not the ignorant man be ashamed, when he does not know, to learn.

«46»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: in the hadith of Abu Umama al-Bahili, that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Take to knowledge before it is seized and before it is gathered — and he joined together two of his fingers, the middle one and the one next to the thumb. Then he said: The scholar and the learner are partners in the reward, and there is no good in the rest of people thereafter.
Elucidation: perhaps what is meant by the gathering is likewise the seizing of it and the taking of it from its places, that it may be gathered in a single place —

177.text: in His knowledge and the knowledge of those brought near to His presence.

«47»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: it is related from al-Miqdad b. al-Aswad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — saying: Indeed the angels lay down their wings for the seeker of knowledge, so that he treads upon them, in contentment with him.
«48»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: A single jurist is harder upon Iblis than a thousand worshippers.
«49»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whomever God intends good for, He gives him understanding in religion.
«50»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever does not endure the humiliation of learning for an hour remains in the humiliation of ignorance forever.
«51»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: The seeker of knowledge does not die until his striving enjoys according to the measure of his toil.
