Elucidation: aw here is in the sense of "until" or "unless". And al-jidd, with kasra, is exertion in a matter; and the ascribing of enjoyment to striving is figurative.
«52»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Knowledge is stored up with its people, and you have been commanded to seek it from them.
«53»- And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: If people knew what is in knowledge, they would surely seek it, though it were at the shedding of life-blood and the plunging into deeps.
Elucidation: al-muhja is blood, or the blood of the heart, and the spirit. And al-lujja is the main body of water.
«54»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: The seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim man and Muslim woman.
«55»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Seek knowledge, even in China.
«56»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no blame upon one who does not know, that he should ask about what he does not know.

«57»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever goes out from his house to seek a door of knowledge, that he may benefit by it and teach it to another, God writes for him, for every step (1), the worship of a thousand years — the fasting of them and the standing of them in prayer; and the angels encompass him with their wings; and the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea and the beasts of the land pray for him; and God settles him in the station of seventy truthful ones; and it is better for him than that the whole world were his and he should set it in the hereafter.
«58»- ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: Ibn Qulawayh, from Muhammad al-Himyari, from his father, from Harun (2), from
With damma on the kha' and quiescence of the ta': what is between the two feet in walking.

He is Harun b. Muslim. Al-Najashi said in his Fihrist, p. 307: Harun b. Muslim b. Sa'dan the scribe, of Surra Man Ra'a — he had settled there, and his origin was al-Anbar; his agnomen is Abu al-Qasim; trustworthy, of standing. And he held a doctrine concerning compulsion and anthropomorphism. He met Abu Muhammad and Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon them both. He has a book on the divine unity, a book of the excellences, a book of the sermons, a book of the campaigns, and a book of supplication; and he has questions put to Abu al-Hasan the Third, peace be upon him.

178.text: Ibn Ziyad (1), who said: I heard Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them both — and he had been asked about His words, exalted be He, "To God belongs the conclusive argument" — and he said: Indeed God the Exalted will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: Were you a knower? And if he says yes, He says to him: Then why did you not act by what you knew? And if he says: I was ignorant, He says to him: Then why did you not learn, that you might act? So He overcomes him in the argument; and that is the conclusive argument.

«59»- m, the Tafsir of the Imam, peace be upon him: The Imam, peace be upon him, said: Jabir b. 'Abd Allah al-Ansari came in upon the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: O Jabir, the subsistence of this world is by four: a scholar who employs his knowledge; an ignorant man who does not disdain to learn; a rich man generous with his kindness; and a poor man who does not sell his hereafter for the world of another. Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: So when the scholar conceals knowledge from its people, and the ignorant man is vain about the learning of what he cannot do without, and the rich man is miserly with his kindness, and the poor man sells his religion for the world of another — then affliction descends and the punishment is great.

«60»- j', Jami' al-Akhbar: from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: O Abu Dharr, whoever goes out from his house seeking a door of knowledge, God, mighty and majestic, writes for him, for every footstep, the reward of a prophet among the prophets; and God gives him, for every letter that he hears or writes, a city in the Garden. And the seeker of knowledge — God loves him, and the angels love him, and the prophets love him; and none loves knowledge save the felicitous. So blessedness to the seeker of knowledge on the Day of Resurrection! And whoever goes out from his house seeking a door of knowledge, God writes for him, for every footstep, the reward of a martyr among the martyrs of Badr. And the seeker of knowledge is the beloved of God; and whoever loves knowledge, the Garden becomes due for him; and he rises at morning and comes to evening in the good pleasure of God; and he does not depart from this world until he drinks of al-Kawthar and eats of the fruit of the Garden and becomes in the Garden the comrade of al-Khidr, peace be upon him. And all this is under this verse: "God raises up those of you who believe, and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees."

Elucidation: what is meant by the reward of the prophet is either the reward of one of his deeds, or his merited reward — for it is little in comparison with what God the Exalted bestows upon him of reward as a favour; and likewise the martyr.

He is Mas'ada. Al-Najashi set him down in his book, p. 295, saying: Mas'ada b. Ziyad al-Rab'i, trustworthy, of note; he related from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him; he has a book on the lawful and the unlawful, arranged in chapters. Muhammad b. Muhammad informed us, saying: There related to us Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Zurari, who said: There related to us 'Abd Allah b. Ja'far al-Himyari, who said: There related to us Harun b. Muslim, from Mas'ada b. Ziyad, from his book.

179.text: «61»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The subsistence of religion is by four: by a scholar who speaks out and employs it; by a rich man who is not miserly with his bounty toward the people of God's religion; by a poor man who does not sell his hereafter for his world; and by an ignorant man who is not too proud to seek knowledge. So when the scholar conceals his knowledge, and the rich man is miserly, and the poor man sells his hereafter for his world, and the ignorant man is too proud to seek knowledge — the world returns upon its inheritance, backwards. And let not the multitude of mosques deceive you, nor the bodies of a people at variance. It was said: O Commander of the Faithful, how is living in that time? He said: Mix with them outwardly — meaning in the open — and differ from them inwardly; for a man has what he has earned, and he is with whom he loves. And await, along with that, the relief from God the Exalted.

Elucidation: "the world returns upon its inheritance" — thus it is in the copies we have; and perhaps what is meant is that it returns together with what people have inherited of wealth and blessings — that is, their blessings are stripped from people as a punishment for these traits. And the more correct is "upon its rear", as will come (1). And he said in al-Nihaya: in the hadith of Salman, "whoever sets right his inward, God sets right his outward" — he meant by al-barrani the open; and the alif and the nun are among the additions of relation, as they said of San'a', San'ani. And its origin is from their saying: so-and-so went out barran — that is, he went out to the open country and the desert. His words, peace be upon him, "for a man has what he has earned", are an explanation that being with them will not harm you: for you have your own deeds, and you will be gathered in the hereafter with the Imams whom you love.

«62»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: He who journeys forth in the seeking of knowledge is like the one who strives in the way of God. Indeed the seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim; and how many a believer goes out from his dwelling in the seeking of knowledge and does not return but forgiven.
«63»- And he said, peace be upon him: There is no knowledge like reflection, and no nobility like knowledge.

Elucidation: what is meant by al-shukhus is the going out from the town, or what is more general than it and than the going out from the house. And his words, peace be upon him, "there is no knowledge like reflection" — that is, like the knowledge obtained by reflection; or what is meant by knowledge is that which occasions it, figuratively.

The apparent sense is that what is meant by the world's returning to its inheritance is its returning to the first age of ignorance, which the people of the Jahiliyya left behind and which Islam abrogated, spreading beneficial knowledge in the world; and with the abandoning of knowledge and the corrupting of religious upbringing, people return to their first inheritance, which is ignorance and blindness and corruption. T.

180.text: «64»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: O believer, indeed this knowledge and refinement are the price of your soul, so strive in the learning of them both; for whatever increases of your knowledge and your refinement increases in your price and your worth. For by knowledge you are guided to your Lord, and by refinement you perform well the service of your Lord; and by the refinement of service the servant merits His guardianship and His nearness. So accept the counsel, that you may be saved from the punishment.
«65»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Seek knowledge, even in China; for the seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.

«66»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever learns a single question, God will hang upon him on the Day of Resurrection a thousand necklaces of light, and forgive him a thousand sins, and build for him a city of gold, and write for him, for every hair upon his body, a pilgrimage.

«67»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever learns a door of knowledge — whether he acts by it or does not act — it is more excellent than that he should pray a thousand cycles of voluntary prayer.

«68»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Indeed the servant, when he goes out in the seeking of knowledge, God, mighty and majestic, calls to him from above the Throne: Welcome to you (1), O My servant! Do you know what station you seek and what degree you aspire to (2)? You resemble (3) My angels brought near, that you may be a companion to them. I shall surely bring you to your aim, and I shall surely join you to your need. And it was said to 'Ali b. al-Husayn, peace be upon them both: What is the meaning of the resembling of the angels of God, mighty and majestic, brought near, that he may be a companion to them? He said: Have you not heard the words of God, mighty and majestic: "God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels, and those possessed of knowledge, upholding justice; there is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise"? So He began with Himself, and made second His angels, and made third those possessed of knowledge, who are the companions of His angels; and their master is Muhammad, may God bless him and his family, and the second of them is 'Ali, peace be upon him, and the third of them is his family and the most deserving of them of his rank after him. 'Ali b. al-Husayn said: Then you, O company of the Shi'a, the learned by our knowledge, are ta'wilun (4) [taluna lana — followers of us], joined to us and to the angels of God brought near
That is, you have met with room and welcome.
That is, you resemble and are like.
Thus in the copy; and it is possible that it is a corruption of nazilun.

181.text: witnesses for God to His oneness and His justice and His generosity and His bounty, cutting off the excuses of the obstinate among His handmaids and His slaves. So excellent is the judgement you have formed for yourselves, and excellent is the abundant portion you have chosen, and by the noblest felicity you have been made felicitous, when you were joined to Muhammad and his pure family, peace be upon them; and you were made the just ones of God in His earth, proclaiming His oneness and His magnification. And well may it be for you! Indeed Muhammad is the master of the first and of the last; and indeed the companions of Muhammad who take as friends the friends of Muhammad and 'Ali — God's blessings be upon them both — and who dissociate from the enemies of them both, are the most excellent of the communities of the messengers. And indeed God accepts from no one any deed save by this belief, and forgives him no sin, and accepts from him no good deed, and raises for him no degree, save by it.

«69»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, who said: By God, God has not created a creature more excellent than Muhammad and than me and the people of my house; and indeed the angels lay down their wings for the seekers of knowledge among our Shi'a.
«70»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: al-Baqir, peace be upon him, said: The spirit is the pillar of religion, and knowledge is the pillar of the spirit, and clear expression is the pillar of knowledge.

«71»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from Ja'far b. Muhammad al-'Alawi, from Ibn Nahik (1), from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza b. Humran, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The seeker of knowledge among the ignorant is like the living among the dead.
«72»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from 'Ali b. Ja'far b. Musafir al-Hudhali, from

On the pattern of Zubayr. It is the agnomen of 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad b. Nahik, Abu al-'Abbas al-Nakha'i — or 'Ubayd Allah, according to a difference concerning it. Al-'Allama, God's mercy be upon him, gave his entry in al-Khulasa, and al-Shaykh in his Fihrist in the augmentative form, and al-Najashi in the diminutive. Al-Najashi described him at p. 160 with his words: 'Ubayd Allah b. Ahmad b. Nahik, Abu al-'Abbas al-Nakha'i, the truthful shaykh, trustworthy. And the house of Nahik at Kufa is a family of our companions; among them are 'Abd Allah b. Muhammad and 'Abd al-Rahman, the two of Samarra (apparently: al-Samariyyan), and others. He has a book of the Nawadir. There informed us the judge Abu al-Husayn Muhammad b. 'Uthman b. al-Hasan, who said: the licence of Abu al-Qasim Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Musawi comprised — and he showed it to us — all that 'Ubayd Allah b. Ahmad b. Nahik related. And he said: he was at Kufa and went out to Mecca. And Hamid b. Ziyad said in his Fihrist: I heard from 'Ubayd Allah the book of the rites, the book of the pilgrimage, the book of the excellences of the pilgrimage, the book of the three and the four, and the book of the reproaches; and I do not know whether Hamid read them to him and they are of his own compositions, or whether they belong to another.

182.text: his father, from Muhammad b. Ya'la, from Abu Nu'aym 'Umar b. Sabih, from Muqatil b. Hayyan, from al-Dahhak b. Muzahim, from al-Nazzal b. Sabra, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, and from 'Abd Allah b. Mas'ud, from the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — who said: Whoever goes out seeking a door of knowledge, that he may turn back by it a falsehood to a truth or an error to right guidance, that deed of his is like the worship of one who worships forty years.

«73»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Husayn b. Ibrahim al-Qazwini, from Muhammad b. Wahban, from 'Ali b. Hubaysh, from al-'Abbas b. Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from his father, from Safwan, from al-Husayn b. Abi Ghundar, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The perfection of the believer is in three traits: understanding in his religion, patience in misfortune, and measured management in livelihood.

«74»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from Raja' b. Yahya, from Hamdan, from Harun b. Muslim, from Mas'ada b. Ziyad, from al-Sadiq, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: Abu Dharr, God be pleased with him, said in a sermon of his: O seeker of knowledge, let not the world, nor family, nor wealth distract you from your own soul. You, on the day you part from them, are like a guest who has passed a night among them and then gone forth in the morning from them to others. This world and the hereafter are like a lodging from which you have moved to another. And between the raising up and death there is nothing but the like of a sleep you have slept and then awoken from. O ignorant one, learn knowledge; for a heart in which there is nothing of knowledge is like the ruined house that has none to dwell in it.

«75»- It was transmitted from the hand of the vizier Muhammad b. al-'Alqami, who said: The Shaykh al-San'ani — may God the Exalted preserve him — dictated it to me on the third of Safar in the year six hundred and forty-eight. He said: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Two are insatiable and are never filled: the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of the world. As for the seeker of knowledge, he increases in the good pleasure of the All-Merciful; and as for the seeker of the world, he persists in insolence.
«76»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: Knowledge is a noble inheritance, and thought is a clear mirror.
«77»- And he said, peace be upon him: The worth of every man is what he does well.
The Sayyid, God be pleased with him, said: And this is the word for which no worth can be attained, with which no wisdom can be weighed, and to which no word can be paired.
«78»- And he said, peace be upon him: Indeed these hearts grow weary as bodies grow weary; so seek out for them choice pieces of wisdom.

183.text: «79»- And he said, peace be upon him: Indeed the nearest of people to the prophets are the most knowing of them concerning what they brought. Then he, peace be upon him, recited: "Indeed the nearest of people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe"
Elucidation: in some of the copies, "the most active of them"; and that is the more evident.

«80»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: He, peace be upon him, was asked about the good — what is it? And he said: The good is not that your wealth and your children be many; rather the good is that your knowledge be much and your forbearance be great — the report.
«81»- And he said, peace be upon him: There is no nobility like knowledge, and no knowledge like reflection.
«82»- And he said, peace be upon him: Every vessel is straitened by what is placed in it, save the vessel of knowledge — for that expands.
«83»- And he said: Two are insatiable and are never filled: the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of the world.
«84»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: People are the sons of what they do well.
«85»- And he said, peace be upon him: The ignorant man is small, though he be an elder; and the knowing man is great, though he be young (1).
«86»- And he said, peace be upon him: Whoever is known for wisdom, eyes regard him with reverence.
«87»- And he said, peace be upon him: Affection is the most interwoven of kinships, and knowledge the noblest of pedigrees.
«88»- And he said, peace be upon him: There is no treasure more profitable than knowledge, and no evil companion worse than ignorance.

«89»- And he said, peace be upon him: Take to the seeking of knowledge; for the seeking of it is an obligation, and it is a bond between brethren, and an indication of manliness, and a gift in assemblies, and a companion on the journey, and an intimate in a strange land.
«90»- And he said, peace be upon him: The noble is he whom his knowledge has ennobled.
«91»- And he said, peace be upon him: Whoever has come to know wisdom does not bear to refrain from increasing in it.
«92»- And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Kings are rulers over people, and the scholars are rulers over kings.
«93»- And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: A word of wisdom which a man hears and then utters, or acts by, is better than the worship of a year.
«94»- Munyat al-Murid: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever seeks knowledge and attains it, God writes for him two shares (2)
al-kifl: the double portion, of reward or of sin; the share and the portion.

184.text: of the reward; and whoever seeks knowledge and does not attain it, God writes for him one share of the reward.

«95»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever wishes to look upon those whom God has freed from the Fire, let him look upon the learners. For by Him in whose hand is my soul, there is no learner who goes to and fro at the door of the scholar but that God writes for him, for every footstep, the worship of a year, and God builds for him, for every footstep, a city in the Garden; and he walks upon the earth while it seeks forgiveness for him; and he comes to evening and rises at morning forgiven; and the angels bear witness that they are those whom God has freed from the Fire.

«96»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever seeks knowledge is like the one who fasts his day and stands his night in prayer. And indeed a door of knowledge which a man learns is better for him than that Abu Qubays were his in gold and he spent it in the way of God.

«97»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever is come upon by death while he is seeking knowledge that he may thereby revive Islam, there is between him and the prophets a single degree in the Garden.
«98»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: That God should guide by you a single man is better than that the red camels were yours.
«99»- And in another narration: better for you than the world and what is in it.

«100»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: The likeness of that with which God has sent me, of guidance and knowledge, is as the likeness of a rain that fell upon a land. Part of it was good ground, and it accepted the water and brought forth pasture and much herbage (1); and part of it was hard barren patches (2) that held the water, and God benefited people by it, and they drank of it and gave to drink and sowed; and the rain fell upon another part of it which is but bare flats (3) that hold no water and bring forth no pasture. That is the likeness of one who has understanding in the religion of God and has gained understanding of that with which God has sent me, so that he knew and taught; and the likeness of one who did not raise his head to that and did not accept the guidance of God with which I was sent.

«101»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever goes forth at morning in the seeking of knowledge, the angels shade him, and he is blessed in his livelihood, and nothing is diminished of his provision.
al-kala': the plants of the earth of what the cattle graze, both its fresh and its dry; and al-'ushb, with damma and quiescence, is fresh pasture.
al-ajadib: lands in which there is no growth.

With kasra on the qaf, the plural of al-qa', which is level low-lying ground from which the mountains and the hills have drawn apart. Its plural also comes as qi' and qi'a, with kasra on the qaf in both, and as aqwa' and aqwu'.

185.text: «102»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: A sleep with knowledge is better than a prayer with ignorance.

«103»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whatever youth grows up in knowledge and worship until he becomes great, God gives him on the Day of Resurrection the reward of seventy-two truthful ones.
«104»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: A little of knowledge is better than much worship.

«105»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever goes at morning to the mosque desiring nothing but to learn some good or to teach it has the reward of one who performs the lesser pilgrimage complete; and whoever goes at evening to the mosque desiring nothing but to learn some good or to teach it has the reward of a pilgrim whose pilgrimage is complete.

«106»- And from Safwan b. Ghassan, who said: I came to the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — and he was in the mosque, reclining upon a red mantle of his. I said to him: O Messenger of God, I have come seeking knowledge. And he said: Welcome to the seeker of knowledge! Indeed the seeker of knowledge — the angels encompass him with their wings, then they mount one upon another until they reach the heaven of this world, out of their love for that which he seeks.

«107»- And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: It is nobility enough for knowledge that he who is not good at it lays claim to it and rejoices when he is ascribed to it; and it is blame enough for ignorance that he who is in it dissociates from it.

«108»- And from him also, peace be upon him: Knowledge is more excellent than wealth in seven ways. The first: that it is the inheritance of the prophets, while wealth is the inheritance of the pharaohs. The second: knowledge is not diminished by expenditure, while wealth is diminished by it. The third: wealth has need of a keeper, while knowledge keeps its possessor. The fourth: knowledge enters into the shroud, while wealth remains behind. The fifth: wealth is obtained by the believer and the unbeliever, while knowledge is obtained by none but the believer in particular. The sixth: all people have need of the possessor of knowledge in the matter of their religion, and they have no need of the possessor of wealth. The seventh: knowledge strengthens a man for the passing over the Bridge, while wealth holds him back from it.

«109»- And from Zayn al-'Abidin, peace be upon him: If people knew what is in the seeking of knowledge, they would surely seek it, though it were at the shedding of life-blood and the plunging into deeps. Indeed God the Exalted revealed to Daniel: The most hateful of My servants to Me is the ignorant one who makes light of the right of the people of knowledge and abandons the taking of them as an example; and the most beloved of My servants with Me (1)
And in one copy: and the most beloved of My slaves to Me.

186.text: is the God-fearing one, the seeker of the abundant reward, who keeps close to the scholars, who follows the sages (1) [the forbearing], who receives from the wise.

«110»- And in the Gospel, in the seventeenth chapter of it: Woe to him who has heard of knowledge and has not sought it! How shall he be gathered with the ignorant to the Fire? Seek knowledge and learn it; for knowledge, if it does not make you felicitous, will not make you wretched; and if it does not raise you, will not lower you; and if it does not enrich you, will not impoverish you; and if it does not profit you, will not harm you. And do not say: we fear that we shall know and shall not act; but say: we hope that we shall know and shall act. And knowledge intercedes for its possessor, and it is incumbent upon God that He not disgrace him. Indeed God will say on the Day of Resurrection: O company of the scholars, what is your opinion of your Lord? And they will say: our opinion is that You will have mercy upon us and forgive us. And He, exalted be He, will say: Then indeed I have done so. I entrusted My wisdom to you not for an evil I intended by you, but for a good I intended by you. So enter among My righteous servants, into My Garden and My mercy.

«111»- And from Abu Dharr, God be pleased with him, who said: A door of knowledge that you learn is more beloved to us than a thousand cycles of voluntary prayer. And he said: We heard the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — saying: When death comes to the seeker of knowledge while he is in this state, he dies a martyr.

«112»- The book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Shurayh, from Humayd b. Shu'ayb, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Indeed 'Ali, peace be upon him, used to say: Draw near, draw near, and ask; for knowledge is being seized away, a seizing. And he would strike his hand upon his belly and say: Nay, by God, it is not filled with fat, but it is filled with knowledge. By God, there is no verse that came down concerning a man of Quraysh, nor upon the earth, in land or in sea, in plain or in mountain, but that I know concerning whom it came down, and on what day and in what hour it came down.
Chapter 2: The classes of people with respect to knowledge, and the merit of loving the scholars
«1»- l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn 'Isa, from al-Washsha' (2), from Ahmad b.
And in one copy: al-hulama' — the forbearing.

With fatha on the waw and the doubled shin; a relative name from the selling of washy, which is a kind of garment made of silk. And it is the sobriquet of al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Ziyad, whose entry is given in the Rijal of al-Najashi and in other biographical works, with fair mention.

187.text: 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: People rise at morning as three: a scholar, and a learner, and scum. So we are the scholars, and our Shi'a are the learners, and the rest of people are scum.

yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn 'Isa, the like of it. — yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Hamid, from Ibn 'Amira, from Abu Salama (1), from Abu 'Abd Allah, the like of it. — yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from 'Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadija, the like of it. — yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Hashim, from Yahya b. Abi 'Imran, from Yunus, from Jamil, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: People rise at morning as three sorts — and he mentioned the like of it. Elucidation: al-Jawhari said: al-ghutha', with damma and lengthening, is what the torrent carries of rubbish; and likewise al-ghuththa' with the doubling.

«2»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan, from al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad b. Muslim and another, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Rise at morning a scholar, or a learner, or one who loves the scholars; and do not be a fourth, lest you perish by hatred of them.

«3»- l, al-Khisal: Majiluwayh, from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, raising it to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: People are two: a scholar and a learner; and the rest of people are gnats, and the gnats are in the Fire.

Elucidation: al-hamaj, with the vowelling, is the plural of hamaja, which is a small fly like the mosquito that alights upon the faces of sheep and of donkeys and upon their eyes. Thus al-Jawhari mentioned it.

«4»- l, al-Khisal: There related to us Abu al-Hasan Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Shah, who said: There related to us Abu Ishaq al-Khawwas, who said: There related to us Muhammad b. Yunus al-Karimi, from Sufyan b. Waki', from his father, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Kumayl b. Ziyad, who said: 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, came out to me and took my hand and brought me out to the graveyard; and he sat, and I sat. Then he raised his head to me and said: O

This one, and Abu Khadija who preceded in the chain just recited and who comes in the chain following, are both agnomens of Salim b. Mukram b. 'Abd Allah al-Jammal al-Kufi, client of the Banu Asad. His agnomen was at first Abu Khadija, and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, changed it to Abu Salama. He related from Abu 'Abd Allah and Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon them both. Al-Najashi said concerning him: trustworthy, trustworthy.

188.text: Kumayl, retain from me what I say to you. People are three: a divinely learned scholar; and a learner upon a way of deliverance; and the common rabble, the followers of every bleater, swaying with every wind — they have not sought light by the light of knowledge (1) and have not taken refuge in a firm support. O Kumayl, knowledge is better than wealth: knowledge guards you, while you guard wealth; and wealth is diminished by expenditure, while knowledge grows by the expending. O Kumayl, the love of the scholar is a religion by which one is served; it gains him obedience in his lifetime and a fair mention after his death; whereas the benefit of wealth passes away with its passing. O Kumayl, the hoarders of wealth have died while they are alive, but the scholars endure as long as time endures: their persons are lost, but their likenesses are present in hearts. Ah (2)! Indeed here — and he pointed with his hand to his breast — is knowledge, if only I had found bearers for it. Nay, I did find for it a quick-witted one who was not to be trusted, employing the instrument of religion in the seeking of the world, and seeking support by the proofs of God against His creation and by His blessings against His servants, that the weak might take him as an intimate confidant in place of the guardian of the truth; or one compliant toward the bearers of knowledge but having no insight into its bends, in whose heart doubt strikes fire at the first thing that presents itself of ambiguity. Nay, neither this one nor that. So — either one greedy for pleasures, easily led by his appetites, or one enticed by amassing and hoarding: neither of the two is of the shepherds of religion (3); the nearest thing in likeness to them both is grazing cattle. Thus does knowledge die with the death of its bearers. O God, nay — the earth is never empty of one who upholds the proof, whether manifest or hidden (4) [hidden and obscure], lest the proofs of God and His clear signs be void. And how many are they, and where are those? They are the fewest in number and the greatest in worth. By them God preserves His proofs until they deposit them with their peers and sow them in the hearts of their likes. Knowledge has borne them upon the realities of things, so that they have touched the spirit of certainty; and they have found easy what the luxurious found rough, and have grown intimate with what the ignorant shrank from in dread. They have kept company with this world in bodies whose spirits are attached to the highest place. O Kumayl, those are the vicegerents of God and the callers to His religion. Ah, ah — how I long for the sight of them! And I ask forgiveness of God for myself and for you.
«5»- f, Tuhaf al-'Uqul: Indeed these hearts are vessels, and the best of them is the most retentive. Retain from me what I say — to the end of the report.
And in one copy: they have not sought light by the light of knowledge and so been guided.
And in one copy: Ah, ah.
And in the Nahj: neither of the two is of the shepherds of religion in anything.
And in one copy: or one who fears.

189.text: «6»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from al-Saduq, from his father, from Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim Majiluwayh, from Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Sayrafi, from Nasr b. Muzahim, from 'Umar b. Sa'd, from Fudayl b. Khadij (1), from Kumayl b. Ziyad al-Nakha'i, who said: I was with the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, in the mosque of Kufa, and we had prayed the later evening prayer. He took my hand until we went out from the mosque, and he walked until he came out to the back of Kufa, not speaking a word to me. And when he came into the open country he drew a breath, then said: O Kumayl, indeed these hearts are vessels, and the best of them is the most retentive. Retain from me what I say — to the end of the report. Except that in it is: the companionship of the scholar is a religion by which God is served. O Kumayl, the benefit of wealth passes away with its passing. O Kumayl, the hoarders of wealth have died, and the scholars endure as long as time endures: their persons are lost, but their likenesses are present in hearts. Ah, ah! Indeed here doubt strikes fire by an ambiguity — manifest and well known, or concealed and obscure — and His clear signs; and indeed those are the spirits of certainty, what he found rough — the vicegerents of God in His earth and the callers to His religion. Ah, ah — how I long for the sight of them! And I ask forgiveness of God for myself and for you. Then he withdrew his hand from my hand and said: Depart when you wish.

«7»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: Kumayl b. Ziyad said: The Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, took my hand and brought me out to the graveyard. And when he came into the open country he drew a deep sigh (2), then said: O Kumayl, indeed these hearts are vessels (3) — the report.

The book al-Gharat of al-Thaqafi, by his chain, the like of it. Elucidation: this report will come with numerous chains (4) in the chapter on the necessity of the Proof. And al-jabban and al-jabbana, with the doubling, are the open country; and the graveyards are also called by these two names. And ashara means he went out to the open country. And aw'aha — that is, the most retentive of them for knowledge and the most comprehensive. And al-rabbani is a relative form from al-rabb with the addition of the alif and the nun, contrary to analogy, like al-raqbani. Al-Jawhari said: al-rabbani is the devout one who knows God the Exalted; and likewise said al-Fayruzabadi. And he said in al-Kashshaf: al-rabbani is the one firm in cleaving to the religion of God the Exalted and to obedience to Him. And he said in Majma' al-Bayan: he is the one who orders the affair of people by his management and
That is, he breathed a long breath, from weariness or distress.

The plural of al-wi'a — with kasra on the waw and with damma — is that in which a thing is gathered and kept. He, peace be upon him, likened them to vessels because they are the place of the sciences and of the knowledge of realities.
With fatha on the jim and with damma: many.

190.text: by his setting it right (1). And al-hamaj has already passed. And al-ra'a' are the young louts among the common folk and the base and their like. And al-na'iq is the call of the shepherd to his sheep, and it is said also of the cry of the crow. And what is meant is that, having no firmness upon any one of the beliefs and being unsteady in the matter of religion, they follow every caller and believe every claimant, and they blunder as the night-blind camel blunders, without distinguishing between the one in the right and the one in the wrong. And perhaps in the pluralizing of this class and the making singular of the first two classes there is an intimation of the fewness of those two and the multitude of this one, as the Shaykh al-Baha'i, God's mercy be upon him, mentioned. And the firm support is the true, demonstrative, certain beliefs upon which reliance is placed in the repelling of ambiguities and the lifting of the hardship of acts of obedience. And "knowledge guards you" — that is, from the fears of this world and of the hereafter, and from trials and doubts and satanic whisperings. And "wealth — expenditure diminishes it"; and in f, "consumes it". And "knowledge grows by the expending" — that is, it grows and increases by it, either because much study occasions abundance of practice and strength of thought, or because God the Exalted pours out from the treasuries of His knowledge upon one who is not miserly with it.

And the Shaykh al-Baha'i, God's mercy be upon him, said: the word 'ala may be in the sense of ma'a, as they said concerning His words, exalted be He: "And indeed your Lord is possessed of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing" (2); and it may be for causation and reason, as they said concerning His words, exalted be He: "and that you may magnify God for that He has guided you" (3). And in f, after that: "and knowledge is the judge and wealth is that which is judged upon" — since by knowledge judgement is given concerning properties in litigation, and it is taken from one of the two adversaries and turned over to the other; and likewise the expending of it and the gathering of it are in accordance with the knowledge of the ways of acquiring it and of its disbursements. "The love of the scholar is a religion by which one is served": al-din is obedience and recompense — that is, an obedience which is the recompense of the blessings of God and a thanksgiving for them; or its possessor is requited and recompensed by it; or the love of the scholar, who is the Imam, is a religion and a creed by which God is worshipped, and acts of obedience are not accepted save by it.
And in ma: "the companionship of the scholar is a religion by which God is served" — that is, a worship by which God is worshipped.
And in the Nahj al-Balagha: "the knowing of knowledge is a religion by which one is served."
His words "it gains him obedience" — the Shaykh

Ibn Maytham said: it is said they were named thus because they nurture the learners with the lesser sciences before the greater; and it is said: because they nurture knowledge — that is, they undertake the setting of it right.

191.text: al-Baha'i, God's mercy be upon him, said: with damma on the letter of the imperfect, from aksaba; and what is meant is that it gains for the man the obedience of God, or gains for him the obedience of the servants to him. I say: there is no need to transfer it to the fourth form; rather the simple form too has come with this meaning — indeed it is the more eloquent. Al-Jawhari said: al-kasb is gathering; and one says kasabtu ahli khayran, and kasabtu al-rajula malan fa-kasabahu — and this is among what has come as fa'altuhu fa-fa'ala. End. And the pronoun in yuksibuhu refers back to the possessor of knowledge.
And in the Nahj al-Balagha: "it gains the man obedience and a fair mention."

That is, fair speech and praise. And al-uhdutha is the singular of al-ahadith. And in f, after that: "and the benefit of wealth passes away with its passing" — and that is evident. "The hoarders of wealth have died while they are alive" — that is, they are, in the state of their living, under the ruling of the dead, because the benefit of life does not follow upon their living: the understanding of the truth, and the hearing of it, and the accepting of it, and the acting by it, and the employing of the limbs in that for which they were created; as He, exalted be He, said: "dead, not living, and they are not aware" (1). And the scholars, after their death too, endure by their fair mention, and by what has been obtained for them of felicities and delights in the world of the barzakh and in the next arising, and by what follows upon their traces and their sciences, and by what people benefit from their abiding blessings through the length of the ages. And according to the copies of the Amali of al-Shaykh, what is meant is that they died and their mention and their traces died with them, while the scholars after their death endure by their traces and their sciences and their lights. His words, peace be upon him, "and their likenesses are present in hearts" — the Shaykh al-Baha'i said: al-amthal is the plural of mathal, with the vowelling; and it is in origin in the sense of the peer, then used for the current saying whose application is likened to its occasion, then for speech that has consequence and rarity — and this is what is meant here; that is, that their rulings and their admonitions are preserved with their people, who act by them. End. And it is possible that what is meant by their likenesses is their forms and their images; for those who love them, who are guided by them, who follow their traces, remember them always, and their forms are pictured in their hearts — on the supposition that it is the plural of mathal with the vowelling, or the plural of mithl with kasra, for that too is pluralized as amthal. "Indeed here is knowledge": and in the Nahj al-Balagha, "much knowledge" — that is, abundant. "If only I had found bearers for it": hamala, with the fathas, is the plural of hamil — that is, one who is worthy of it. And the apodosis of law is omitted; that is,

192.text: "I would have made it manifest", or "I would have bestowed it upon him" — although the word law, when it is for wishing, does not require an apodosis, according to many of the grammarians. "Nay, I did find for it a quick-witted one": and in the Nahj al-Balagha, "a quick-witted one was found". And al-laqin, with fatha on the lam and kasra on the qaf, is the man of understanding, from al-laqana, which is goodness of understanding. "Not to be trusted" — that is, he divulges it to other than its people and sets it in other than its place. "He employs the instrument of religion in the world"; and in f, "in the seeking of the world" — that is, he makes knowledge, which is an instrument and a means to the winning of everlasting felicities, an instrument and a means to the acquiring of perishing worldly portions.

His words, peace be upon him, "he seeks support by the proofs of God against His creation": perhaps what is meant by the proofs and the blessings are the Imams of truth — that is, he seeks help by these and takes the sciences from them in order to display this knowledge to the people, so that the weak of intellect take him as an inner confidant (1) and an intimate, and he turns people away from the guardian of the truth and calls them to himself. And it is possible that what is meant by the proofs and the blessings is the knowledge which God has given him, and that the two prepositional phrases are attached to the seeking of support — that is, he seeks help by the proofs for the overcoming of the creation, and by the blessings for the overcoming of the servants; and his aim in this seeking of support is the display of excellence, that people may take him as an intimate confidant. Al-Fayruzabadi said: al-walija is the inner confidant, and one's intimate among men, or one whom you take as a reliance from other than your own family. And in f: "and by the blessing of God against His acts of disobedience". "Or one compliant toward the bearers of knowledge": with the undotted ha'; and in some copies with the jim — that is, one who believes in the truth and holds it in a general way; and in f: "or one who professes the sum of the truth". "He has no insight into its bends": with fatha on the hamza, and after it an undotted ha', then a nun — that is, its sides; that is, he has no depth or penetration in it. And in some copies of the two books, and in f, and in some copies of the Nahj also: "in its reviving", with the two-dotted ya' from below — that is, in the promoting of it and the strengthening of it. "Doubt strikes fire": in the passive form; one says qadahtu al-nar — that is, I struck it out with the fire-striker. And in ma, yaqtadihu; and in the Nahj, yanqadihu. And upon all the readings the upshot is that the fire of doubt is kindled in his heart by reason of the first ambiguity that presents itself to him — so how much more when they follow one upon another and come in succession! "Nay, neither this one nor that" — that is, neither the compliant one devoid of insight is worthy to bear knowledge, nor the quick-witted one who is not to be trusted; and this speech is parenthetical between the thing conjoined and that to which it is conjoined. "Or one greedy for pleasures" — that is, eager for them, immersed in them; and al-manhum is in origin the one who is not sated with food. I say: in most copies of the two books, fa-manhum — that is, among the seekers of knowledge
bitanat al-rajul: his family and his intimates.

193.text: or among the people. And in f: "O God, neither this nor that. Then who? — since the one greedy for pleasure, easily led by appetite, or the one enamoured of amassing and hoarding, are not of the shepherds of religion nor of those possessed of insights and of certainty." And in the Nahj: "or one greedy for pleasure, easily led by appetite, or one enamoured". His words, peace be upon him, "easily led" — that is, easy of compliance, without hesitation. "Or one enticed by amassing and hoarding" — that is, intense in eagerness for the gathering of wealth and the hoarding of it, as though someone were enticing him to that and urging him on to it. And al-gharam too is in its meaning: one says fulanun mughramun bi-kadha — that is, cleaving to it, addicted to it. "Neither of the two is of the shepherds of religion": with damma on its first letter, the plural of ra'in in the sense of the governor — that is, the greedy one and the enticed one who have been mentioned are not of the governors of religion. And in it is an intimation that the true scholar is a governor over religion and a custodian of it. "The nearest thing in likeness" — that is, grazing cattle, meaning those that pasture, are the likest of things to these two classes. "Thus does it die" — that is, just as one fit to bear the sciences is lacking, so too are those sciences lost and their traces effaced by the death of the knowing scholars, because they find none after them fit to bear them.

And since the chain of knowledge and gnosis is not cut off altogether so long as the human kind endures — rather there must be in every age an Imam who preserves the religion — the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, made an amendment to this speech of his with his words: "O God, nay." And in the Nahj: "the earth is not empty of one who upholds God's proofs, either manifest and well known, or fearful and obscure"; and in f: "of one upholding a proof, either manifest and uncovered, or fearful and alone, lest the proofs of God and His clear signs and the transmitters of His Book be void." And the manifest, well-known Imam is like the Commander of the Faithful, God's blessings be upon him; and the fearful, obscure one is like the Qa'im in our own age, and like the rest of the Imams who were concealed by reason of fear and dissimulation. And it is possible that the rest of the Imams, peace be upon them, are included in the manifest and well known. And "how many, and where" is a reckoning long of the period of the occultation of the Qa'im, peace be upon him, and a weariness (1) at the extension of the rule of his enemies; or an obscuring of the number of the Imams, peace be upon them, and of the time of their appearance and the period of their rule, because there is no benefit in the declaring of it. Then he, peace be upon him, set forth the fewness of their number and the greatness of their worth. And upon the second view the preservers and the depositors are the Imams, peace be upon them; and upon the first it is possible that what is meant is their Shi'a, who preserve their religions in their occultation. "Knowledge has borne them" — that is, the God-given knowledge brought them up upon the realities of things all at once, and their veils and their coverings were unveiled for them. And al-rawh, with fatha, is rest, and mercy, and the breeze — that is, they found the delight of certainty, and it is of His mercy, exalted be He, and of the breezes of His grace.

194.text: "And they have found easy what the luxurious found rough": al-wa'r of land is the opposite of the level; and al-mutraf is the one given ease — that is, they found easy what those living in ease found hard, of the casting off of appetites and the severing of attachments. "And they have grown intimate with what the ignorant shrank from in dread" — of acts of obedience and of the drawing near and of strivings in religion. "They kept company with this world in bodies", and so forth — that is, though in their bodies they kept company with this creation, yet in their spirits they were set apart from them; rather their spirits were attached to His nearness and His union, exalted be He, keeping company with those brought near to His presence, of the prophets and the angels brought near. "Those are the vicegerents of God in His earth": the defining of the subject by the demonstrative is to indicate that it is worthy of what is predicated of it after it, by reason of its being qualified by the descriptions mentioned before it — as they said concerning His words, exalted be He: "Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the prosperers" (1). And in the copies of the Nahj al-Balagha, "ah, ah"; and in the rest of them, in some "hay hay" and in some "hah hah". And upon all the readings the aim is the showing of longing for them and of grief at parting from them — and if some of these have not come in the lexicon, yet in usage they are current (2). And we have expounded this report with a little exposition because of the abundance of its profit for the seekers; and it is fitting that they look into it every day with the eye of certainty. And we shall clarify some of its benefits in the Book of the Imamate, if God the Exalted wills.

«8»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: al-Hasan b. 'Ali, from al-'Abbas b. 'Amir, from Ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr b. Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Indeed people are two men: a scholar and a learner; and the rest of people are scum. So we are the scholars, and our Shi'a are the learners, and the rest of people are scum.
«9»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, raising it to Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: Rise at morning (3) a scholar of good, and learn good.

«10»- sn, al-Mahasin: Ibn Mahbub, from 'Amr b. Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Rise at morning a scholar or a learner; and beware of being one given to diversion and to pleasure.
«11»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from al-Thumali, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah

And this is among the strange of his words, God's mercy be upon him. How can it be conceived that there should be a word conveying a meaning by usage, employed by one such as he, peace be upon him — and he the most eloquent orator of the Arabs — and then the lexicon not know it? And what is usage but what is known of the language, which its people know at the stage of employment? T.
ghada yaghdu ghuduwwan — that is, he went in the early morning, he set out; and it is used in the sense of "became", so that it raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative.

195.text: , peace be upon him, said: Rise at morning a scholar, or a learner, or love the people of knowledge; and do not be a fourth, lest you perish by hatred of them.

«12»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin; ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no good in living save for two men: a scholar who is obeyed, or a listener who retains (1).

«13»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Rise at morning a scholar, or a learner, or a listener, or one who loves them; and do not be the fifth, lest you perish.
«14»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: The looking upon the face of the scholar is worship.

«15»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: It is related from one of the truthful ones, peace be upon them, that people are four: a man who knows and knows that he knows — that one is a guide, a scholar, so follow him; and a man who knows and does not know that he knows — that one is heedless, so awaken him; and a man who does not know and knows that he does not know — that one is ignorant, so teach him; and a man who does not know and thinks that he knows — that one is astray, so guide him.

«16»- b, Qurb al-Isnad: Ibn Zarif (2), from Ibn 'Ulwan (3), from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon him, that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: If knowledge were suspended at the Pleiades, men of Persia would attain it.

«17»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from 'Abd Allah b. Muhammad b. 'Ubayd Allah b. Yasin, who said: I heard my master Abu al-Hasan 'Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Rida, peace be upon him, at Surra Man Ra'a, saying: The rabble (4)
wa'a the report: he accepted it and pondered it and retained it.

With the dotted za', on the pattern of sharif. He is al-Husayn b. Zarif b. Nasih al-Kufi, trustworthy, with the agnomen Abu Muhammad; he dwelt at Baghdad; he has a book of Nawadir. Thus al-Najashi said at p. 45.

With damma on the undotted 'ayn and quiescence of the lam. He is al-Husayn b. 'Ulwan al-Kalbi. Al-Najashi entered him in his Rijal, p. 38, saying: al-Husayn b. 'Ulwan al-Kalbi, their client, of Kufa, a Sunni; and his brother al-Hasan, with the agnomen Abu Muhammad, is trustworthy. They both related from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him. And al-Husayn has no book; and al-Hasan is more particularly ours and the worthier. And al-Kashshi said at p. 247: Muhammad b. Ishaq, and Muhammad b. al-Munkadir, and 'Amr b. Khalid al-Wasiti, and 'Abd al-Malik b. Jurayj, and al-Husayn b. 'Ulwan, and al-Kalbi — these are of the men of the Sunnis, save that they had an inclination and a strong love. And it has been said that al-Kalbi was concealing his belief and was not an opponent.
al-ghawgha': the base among people and those who rush to evil.

196.text: are the killers of the prophets; and al-'amma is a name derived (1) from al-'ama. God was not content for them that He likened them to cattle, until He said: "nay, further astray from the way."
«18»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: When God makes a servant base, He debars knowledge from him.
Elucidation: that is, He does not grant him success in the acquiring of it.
«19»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Rise at morning a scholar or a learner, and do not be the third, lest you be destroyed.

«20»- The book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Shurayh, from Humayd b. Shu'ayb, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: Rise at morning a scholar of good, or a learner of good.
Chapter 3: Questioning the scholar, studying with him, and coming to his door
al-Nahl — al-Anbiya': "So ask the people of the Reminder, if you do not know"

«1»- l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Mughira, by his chain, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: Knowledge is treasuries, and the keys are questioning. So ask — God have mercy upon you — for indeed four are rewarded in knowledge: the questioner, and the speaker (2), and the listener, and the one who loves them.
The Kanz of al-Karajuki, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, the like of it.

«2»- l, al-Khisal: al-Qattan, from Ahmad al-Hamdani, from 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Faddal, from his father, from Marwan b. Muslim, from al-Thumali, from Ibn Tarif, from Ibn Nubata, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The sages in ages past used to say: it is fitting that the frequenting of doors be for ten purposes. The first of them is the House of God (3), mighty and majestic, for the performing of one's rite and the fulfilling of His right and the discharging of His obligation. And the second, the doors of the kings whose obedience is joined to the obedience of God, mighty and majestic, and whose right is obligatory and whose benefit
What is meant by it is the greater derivation.
And in one copy: the answerer.
What is meant by it are the mosques and the houses of worship.

197.text: is great and whose harm is severe. — And the third, the doors of the scholars from whom the knowledge of religion and of the world is gained. And the fourth, the doors of the people of bounty and of giving, who spend their wealth seeking praise and hoping for the hereafter. And the fifth, the doors of the foolish who are needed in events and to whom recourse is had in needs. And the sixth, the doors of those among the nobles to whom one draws near, seeking comely bearing and manliness and the meeting of need. And the seventh, the doors of those with whom benefit is hoped for in counsel and consultation, and in the strengthening of resolve (1), and in the taking of preparation for what is needed. — And the eighth, the doors of the brethren, for what is due of keeping ties with them and what is incumbent of their rights. And the ninth, the doors of the enemies, whose mischiefs are quieted by conciliation and whose enmity is repelled by devices and gentleness and kindness and visiting. And the tenth, the doors of those by the frequenting of whom one benefits, and from whom good manners are gained, and by whose conversation one is cheered.

Elucidation: it is possible that what is meant by the kings are the kings of religion, of the Imams and their governors; and it is possible that the more general is meant, for obedience to the governors of tyranny too, by way of dissimulation, is of the obedience of God.

His words, peace be upon him, "seeking comely bearing" — that is, that they may meet them with a fair bearing and associate with them with manliness; or that they may have, in the sight of people, by reason of associating with these nobles, a bearing and a manliness. Al-Jazari said: in it, "overlook the slips of those of comely bearing" — they are those who are not known for evil, and one of them slips a slip. And al-hay'a is the form of a thing and its shape and its state; and he means by it those of fair bearing who keep to one bearing and one manner, and whose states do not vary by shifting from one bearing to another. And al-uhba, with damma, is preparation. And al-ghawa'il are evils and calamities. And one says ghashiya fulanan — that is, he came to him.

«3»- sh, the Sahifa of al-Rida, peace be upon him, from al-Rida, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Knowledge (2) is treasuries, and its key (3) is questioning. So ask — God have mercy upon you — for indeed four are rewarded in it: the questioner, and the teacher, and the listener, and the one who loves them (4).
n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him, by the three chains, the like of it.
And in one copy: al-'azm — resolution.
And in one copy: miftahuhu; and in another, mafatihuhu.
The apparent view is that it is identical with what preceded at the end of the first tradition, from the Kanz.

198.text: «4»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: Munif (1) related, from Ja'far b. Muhammad his master, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon him, who said: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said:
I bore patiently the bitterness of affairs, unwillingly — and I was certain, in that, of the right course in the matter —
When you do not know, and you have not been one to ask about knowledge him who knows — you are ignorant and do not know.

«5»- The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Question the scholars, and mix with the sages, and sit with the poor.
«6»- Munyat al-Murid: Zurara and Muhammad b. Muslim and Burayd al-'Ijli related, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, said: People perish only because they do not ask.
«7»- And from him, peace be upon him: Indeed this knowledge has a lock upon it, and its key is questioning.
Chapter 4: Discussing knowledge, keeping company with scholars, attending gatherings of learning, and the censure of mixing with the ignorant

«1»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: Muhammad b. 'Ali, from 'Ali b. Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from his father, from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umar al-'Adani, from Abu al-'Abbas b. Hamza, from Ahmad b. Sawwar, from 'Ubayd Allah b. 'Asim, from Salama b. Wardan, from Anas b. Malik, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The believer, when he dies and leaves behind a single sheet upon which is knowledge, that sheet will be on the Day of Resurrection a screen between him and the Fire; and God, blessed and exalted, gives him, for every letter written upon it, a city seven times wider than this world. And there is no believer who sits an hour with the scholar but that his Lord, mighty and majestic, calls to him: You have sat with My beloved; by My might and My majesty, I shall surely settle you in the Garden with him, and I shall not care.

Perhaps it is a corruption of Mu'attib — with damma on the mim, fatha on the undotted 'ayn, and doubling of the ta' with kasra — the client of Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, trustworthy. Al-Shaykh entered him in his Rijal once among the companions of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, and said: of Medina, he transmitted with a chain from him, peace be upon him; and again among the companions of al-Kazim, peace be upon him, and said: trustworthy. And al-'Allama entered him in the first part of al-Khulasa and declared him trustworthy. And al-Kashshi related at p. 163, by his chain from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: they are ten — meaning his clients — and the best of them and the most excellent of them is Mu'attib; and among them is a traitor, so beware of him; and he is young.

199.text: «2»- thw, Thawab al-A'mal; li, the Amali of al-Saduq: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Sa'dabadi, from al-Barqi, from al-Jamurani, from Ibn al-Bata'ini, from Ibn 'Amira (1), from Ibn Hazim, from al-Sadiq, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The keeping company with the people of religion is a nobility in this world and in the hereafter.

l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Muhammad al-'Attar, from al-Ash'ari, from al-Jamurani, the like of it. Elucidation: the people of religion are the scholars of religion and those who act by its laws.

«3»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq, from Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamdani, from 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Faddal, from his father, who said: al-Rida, peace be upon him, said: Whoever sits in a gathering in which our cause is revived, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die — the report.
Elucidation: the reviving of their cause is by the mention of their excellences and the spreading of their reports and the preserving of their traces.

«4»- fs, the Tafsir of al-Qummi: from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: O people, blessedness to him whom his own fault has occupied away from the faults of people; and who has been humble without any deficiency; and who has sat with the people of understanding and of mercy; and who has mixed with the people of lowliness and destitution; and who has spent wealth that he gathered in other than disobedience — the report.

Elucidation: his words, peace be upon him, "without any deficiency", admit of several aspects. The first: that what is meant is without deficiency in religion, in that the humility is not toward an unbeliever or a transgressor or an oppressor, or for a false cause.

The second: that what is meant by al-manqasa is a fault — that is, that his humility is not on account of a treachery or a transgression or some other of the faults that occasion abasement before people.
The third: that what is meant by al-manqasa is poverty — that is, that his humility is not on account of a lack of wealth, in that what moves him to humility is need and covetousness of wealth.
The fourth: that what is meant is the denying of excess in humility, such that it ends in deficiency and abasement.

His words, peace be upon him, "in other than disobedience": the apparent view is that it attaches to the spending; and its attaching to all of them, or to two of them by way of contention, is far-fetched.
On the pattern of safina. He is Sayf b. 'Amira al-Nakha'i al-Kufi. Ibn al-Nadim counted him in his Fihrist among the jurists of the Shi'a; and his entry has already been given.

200.text: «5»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from 'Ali, from his father, from Hammad b. 'Isa, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said in his testament to his son Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya: And know that the manliness of the Muslim man is two manlinesses: a manliness at home and a manliness on a journey. As for the manliness of home, it is the reciting of the Qur'an, and the keeping company with the scholars, and the looking into jurisprudence, and the guarding of the prayer in congregations. And as for the manliness of the journey, it is the giving of provision, and fewness of dispute with the one who accompanies you, and much remembrance of God, mighty and majestic, at every ascent and descent and halting and standing and sitting.

«6»- n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him: al-Qattan and al-Naqqash and al-Talaqani, all of them from Ahmad al-Hamdani, from 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. Faddal, from his father, who said: al-Rida, peace be upon him, said: Whoever recalls our affliction and weeps and makes others weep, his eye will not weep on the day when eyes weep; and whoever sits in a gathering in which our cause is revived, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die.
Elucidation: the death of hearts at the Resurrection is a metaphor for the intensity of dismay and grief and sorrow and fear.

«7»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from Ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd, from Ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad b. Ishaq, from Bakr b. Muhammad, from Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said: I heard him saying to Khaythama (1): O Khaythama, convey to our friends the greeting of peace, and enjoin upon them the fear of God the Great, mighty and majestic; and that their living should attend the funerals of their dead, and that they should meet one another in their houses — for their meeting is the life of our cause. He said: then he, peace be upon him, raised his hand and said: God have mercy upon a man who revives our cause.

«8»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from Ibn Qulawayh, from al-Qasim b. Muhammad, from 'Ali b. Ibrahim, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Abd Allah b. Hammad al-Ansari, from Jamil b. Darraj, from Mu'attib, the client of Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: I heard him saying to Dawud b. Sirhan: O Dawud, convey from me to my friends the greeting of peace, and that I say: God have mercy upon a servant who gathers with another and they discuss our cause; for the third of them is an angel who seeks forgiveness for them both. And no two gather upon the mention of us but that God the Exalted boasts of them both to the angels. So when you gather, occupy yourselves with the remembrance; for in your gathering and your discussion is our reviving. And the best of people after us is he who discusses our cause and calls to the mention of us.

He is Khaythama b. Khadij b. al-Rahil al-Ju'fi al-Kufi. Al-Shaykh counted him in his Rijal among the companions of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, and the apparent sense is that he was an Imami; and the report indicates that the man was a Shi'i and of the people of trustworthiness.

201.text: «9»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Mufid, from the righteous sharif Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad b. Muhammad b. Tahir al-Musawi, God's mercy be upon him, from Ibn 'Uqda, from Yahya b. al-Hasan b. al-Husayn al-'Alawi, from Ishaq b. Musa, from his father, from his grandfather, from Muhammad b. 'Ali, from 'Ali b. al-Husayn, from al-Husayn b. 'Ali, from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The God-fearing are masters, and the jurists are leaders, and the sitting with them is worship.

«10»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, among them al-Husayn b. 'Ubayd Allah and Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Abdun and al-Hasan b. Isma'il b. Ashnas and Abu Talib b. Kharur and Abu al-Hasan al-Saffar, all of them from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, from Ahmad b. 'Ubayd Allah, from Ayyub b. Muhammad al-Raqqi, from Sallam b. Razin, from Isra'il b. Yunus al-Kufi, from his grandfather Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith al-Hamdani, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — who said: The prophets are leaders, and the jurists are masters, and the keeping company with them is increase. And you are in the passing of night and day, in terms that are being lessened and deeds that are being preserved; and death comes upon you suddenly. So whoever sows good reaps gladness, and whoever sows evil reaps regret.
Clarification: baghtatan — that is, suddenly. And al-ghibta, with kasra, is joy and goodness of state.

«11»- 'a, 'Ilal al-Shara'i': Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Marrar (1), from Yunus, raising it, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, choose the gatherings upon your own eye. If you see a people remembering God, mighty and majestic, then sit with them; for if you are a knower, your knowledge will profit you and they will increase you in knowledge; and if you are ignorant, they will teach you; and perhaps God will overshadow them with a mercy, and it will include you along with them. And if you see a people not remembering God, then do not sit with them; for if you are a knower, your knowledge will not profit you; and if you are ignorant, they will increase you in ignorance; and perhaps God will overshadow them with a punishment, and it will include you along with them.

Elucidation: "choose the gatherings upon your own eye" — that is, upon insight from yourself; or "with your eye", for 'ala sometimes comes in the sense of the ba'; or "prefer them above your own eye". And upon the last, the detailing is a setting forth of the gathering that ought to be chosen above the eye.

On the pattern of shaddad. He is Isma'il b. Marrar. Al-Shaykh counted him in the chapter of those who did not relate from the Imams, peace be upon them, and said: he related from Yunus b. 'Abd al-Rahman, and Ibrahim b. Hashim related from him.

202.text: «12»- m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar: al-Naqqash, from Ahmad al-Kufi, from al-Mundhir b. Muhammad, from his father, who said: There related to me Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, from his father, from his father, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Hasten to the meadows of the Garden. They said: And what are the meadows of the Garden? He said: The circles of remembrance.

Clarification: the circles of remembrance are the gatherings in which God is remembered according to the rule of the sacred law, and in which the sciences of the People of the House, peace be upon them, and their excellences are mentioned; and the gatherings of admonition in which His promise and His threat are mentioned — not the innovated, invented gatherings in which God is disobeyed, for those are gatherings of heedlessness, not circles of remembrance.

«13»- m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar; li, the Amali of al-Saduq: among the words of the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — in the narration of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him: The wisest of people is he who flees from the ignorant of people; and the most felicitous of people is he who mixes with the noble of people.

«14»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: It is related from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said: Meet one another and converse together of knowledge; for by the report the rusted hearts are polished, and by the report is the reviving of our cause. So God have mercy upon one who revives our cause.
Elucidation: al-Jawhari said: al-rayn is the film and the stain. One says: rana 'ala qalbihi dhanbuhu yarinu raynan wa-ruyunan — that is, it overcame it.

«15»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: A number of the shaykhs related, by a sound path, from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said: Indeed God, mighty and majestic, says to His angels, when the people of the gatherings of remembrance and of knowledge disperse to their dwellings: Write the reward of what you have witnessed of their deeds. So they write for each one the reward of his deed, and they leave out some of those who were present with them and do not write him. And God, mighty and majestic, says: What is with you that you have not written so-and-so? Was he not with them, and did he not attend them? And they say: O Lord, he did not share with them by a letter, nor did he speak with them a word. And the Majestic, majestic be His majesty, says: Was he not their sitting-companion? And they say: Yes, O Lord. And He says: Write him with them; they are a people whose sitting-companion is not made wretched by them. So they write him with them. And He, exalted be He, says: Write for him a reward like the reward of one of them.

Elucidation: his words, peace be upon him, "their sitting-companion is not made wretched by them" — that is, by their blessing their sitting-companion is not disappointed of their honour so as to be made wretched; or that their company has an effect upon the sitting-companion, so that he merits by reason of that the reward and the felicity.
«16»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: Discuss together, and meet one another, and converse; for the report is a polishing

203.text: — indeed hearts rust as the sword rusts, and their polishing is the report.

«17»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Indeed God, mighty and majestic, says: The mutual discussion of knowledge among My servants is of that by which dead hearts are revived, when they come in it to My command.
Munyat al-Murid, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, from him — may God bless him and his family — the like of it.

«18»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: The disciples said to Jesus, peace be upon him: O Spirit of God, with whom shall we sit? He said: With him the sight of whom reminds you of God, and whose speech increases you in knowledge, and whose deed makes you desire the hereafter.

«19»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: It is related from one of the truthful ones, peace be upon them, that he said: Sitting-companions are three: a companion from whom you benefit — so keep to him; and a companion whom you benefit — so honour him; and a companion whom you neither benefit nor benefit from — so flee from him.

«20»- ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: al-Maraghi, from Thawaba b. Yazid, from Ahmad b. 'Ali b. al-Muthanna, from Muhammad b. al-Muthanna, from Sababa [Shababa] b. Sawwar, from al-Mubarak b. Sa'id, from Khalil al-Farra', from Abu al-Muhabbar (1), who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Four are a corruption for hearts: seclusion with women, and listening to them, and taking their opinion, and keeping company with the dead. And it was said to him: O Messenger of God, and what is the keeping company with the dead? He said: The keeping company with everyone astray from faith and deviating in the rulings.

«21»- j', Jami' al-Akhbar: from Abu Dharr, God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: O Abu Dharr, the sitting for an hour at the discussion of knowledge is more beloved to God than the standing of a thousand nights in which a thousand cycles of prayer are prayed each night; and the sitting for an hour at the discussion of knowledge is more beloved to God than a thousand campaigns and the reciting of the whole Qur'an. He said: O Messenger of God, is the discussion of knowledge better than the reciting of the whole Qur'an?
