And the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: O Abu Dharr, the sitting for an hour at the discussion of knowledge is more beloved to God than the reciting of the whole Qur'an twelve thousand times. Take to the discussion of knowledge; for by knowledge you know the lawful from the unlawful. O Abu Dharr, the sitting for an hour

Abu al-Mujabbar — with the jim or the undotted ha' — he mentioned him in al-Isaba, vol. 4, p. 172, and related from him, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant him peace: "Whoever supports two daughters, or two sons, or two paternal aunts, or two grandmothers, he is with me in the Garden like these two" — and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant him peace, joined together his two fingers, the forefinger and the one beside it — "and if they be three, he is one made glad; and if they be four or five, then, O servants of God, come to his aid, lend to him, trade with him." He said: and Mutayyan brought it out in al-Sahaba, from al-Himmani.

204.text: at the discussion of knowledge is better for you than the worship of a year whose day is fasted and whose night is stood in prayer; and the looking upon the face of the scholar is better for you than the freeing of a thousand necks.

«22»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: Luqman said to his son: O my son, sit with the scholars and press close to them with your knees; for God, mighty and majestic, revives hearts by the light of wisdom as He revives the earth by the heavy rain of heaven.
Elucidation: zahimhum — that is, crowd in upon them and enter into their throng; "with your two knees" — that is, put your knees into their throng. And al-wabil is rain of great drops and heavy.

«23»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: It is related from one of the Companions, who said: A man of the Helpers came to the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — and said: O Messenger of God, when a funeral and the gathering of a scholar are both present, which of the two is more beloved to you that I should attend? And the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: If the funeral has one to follow it and to bury it, then the attending of the gathering of a scholar is more excellent than the attending of a thousand funerals, and than the visiting of a thousand sick, and than the standing of a thousand nights, and than the fasting of a thousand days, and than a thousand dirhams given in charity to the poor, and than a thousand pilgrimages besides the obligatory one, and than a thousand campaigns besides the obligatory which you campaign in the way of God with your wealth and your self. And where do these attendances fall beside the attendance upon a scholar? Do you not know that God is obeyed by knowledge and worshipped by knowledge, and that the good of this world and of the hereafter is with knowledge, and the evil of this world and of the hereafter is with ignorance?

«24»- kshf, Kashf al-Ghumma: from the hafiz 'Abd al-'Aziz, from Dawud b. Sulayman, from al-Rida, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The keeping company with the scholars is worship, and the looking upon 'Ali, peace be upon him, is worship, and the looking upon the House is worship, and the looking upon the codex is worship, and the looking upon the two parents is worship.

«25»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: al-Mufid, from Abu Ghalib al-Zurari and Ibn Qulawayh, from al-Kulayni, from al-Husayn b. al-Hasan, from Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Ghallabi, from Ibn 'A'isha al-Nasri, raising it, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said in one of his sermons: O people, know that he is not intelligent who is disturbed by false speech about him, nor is he wise who is pleased with the praise of the ignorant upon him. People are the sons of what they do well, and the worth of every man is what he does well. So speak in knowledge — your worths will be made plain.
«26»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: al-Baqir, peace be upon him, said: The recalling of knowledge for an hour is better than the standing of a night.

205.text: «27»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: Musa b. Ja'far, peace be upon them both, said: Conversation with the scholar upon a dunghill is better than conversation with the ignorant upon carpets.

«28»- And he said, peace be upon him: Do not sit with every scholar, save a scholar who calls you from the five to the five: from doubt to certainty, and from pride to humility, and from ostentation to sincerity, and from enmity to sincere counsel, and from desire to renunciation.

«29»- The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: He — may God bless him and his family — said: The looking upon the face of the scholar out of love for him is worship.
«30»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Whoever sits with the scholars is reverenced, and whoever mixes with the base is despised.

«31»- And from it: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Blessedness to him whom his own fault has occupied away from the faults of others; and who has spent what he earned in other than disobedience; and who has had mercy upon the people of weakness and destitution; and who has mixed with the people of understanding and of wisdom.
«32»- And from it: Luqman said to his son: O my son, accompany the scholars and sit with them and visit them in their houses; perhaps you will come to resemble them, and so be one of them.

«33»- 'dda, 'Uddat al-Da'i: from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The sitting of an hour with the scholars is more beloved to God than the worship of a thousand years; and the looking upon the scholar is more beloved to God than a year's retreat in the Sacred House; and the visiting of the scholars is more beloved to God the Exalted than seventy circumambulations around the House, and more excellent than seventy pilgrimages and lesser pilgrimages, righteous and accepted. And God raises for him seventy degrees, and God sends down upon him mercy, and the angels bear witness for him that the Garden has become due for him.

«34»- Munyat al-Murid: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: When you pass through the meadows of the Garden, then graze. They said: O Messenger of God, and what are the meadows of the Garden? He said: The circles of remembrance; for God has roving companies of angels who seek out the circles of remembrance, and when they come upon them they encompass them.

Some of the scholars said: the circles of remembrance are the gatherings of the lawful and the unlawful — how one buys and sells, and prays, and fasts, and marries, and divorces, and performs the pilgrimage, and the like of that.

206.text: «35»- And he — may God bless him and his family — went out, and behold, in the mosque were two gatherings: a gathering gaining understanding, and a gathering supplicating God and asking of Him. And he said: Both of the two gatherings are unto good. As for these, they supplicate God; and as for these, they learn and give understanding to the ignorant — these are the more excellent. With teaching was I sent. Then he sat with them.

«36»- And from al-Baqir, peace be upon him: God have mercy upon a servant who revived knowledge. And it was said: And what is the reviving of it? He said: That he discuss it with the people of religion and of scrupulousness.
«37»- And from him, peace be upon him, who said: The mutual discussion of knowledge is study, and study is a goodly prayer.

«38»- In the Psalms: Say to the rabbis of the Children of Israel and to their monks (1): Converse with the God-fearing among people; and if you do not find among them one who is God-fearing, then converse with the scholars; and if you do not find a scholar, then converse with the men of intellect. For God-fearing and knowledge and intellect are three ranks — I have not placed one of them in a creature of Mine while I desired his destruction.

«1»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Talha b. Zayd, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: The one who acts without insight is like the one who travels off the road; and the swiftness of his travel only increases him in distance from the road.
sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Muhammad b. Sinan and 'Abd Allah b. al-Mughira together, from Talha, the like of it. — da, the Fiqh of al-Rida, peace be upon him, the like of it.

«2»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: al-'Attar, from his father, from Ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan b. Ziyad al-Sayqal, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, saying: God, mighty and majestic, does not accept

al-ahbar is the plural of al-hibr — with fatha on the ha' and with kasra, and quiescence of the ba': the head of the priests among the Jews. And al-kahana is the plural of al-kahin, who is one who claims the knowledge of secrets and of the states of the unseen among the Jews and the idolaters, and who presents the sacrifices and the offerings among the Christians. And al-ruhban is the plural of al-rahib, who is one who withdraws from people to a monastery seeking worship. And monasticism among the Jews and the Christians was praised and current among them; but Islam forbade that with its words, "there is no monasticism in Islam", and urged people to enter into communities and to support their kind in what pertains to civilization and by which the structure of society is raised up.

207.text: any deed save with knowledge, and there is no knowledge save with deed. So whoever knows, his knowledge leads him to the deed; and whoever does not act, he has no knowledge. Indeed faith — part of it is from part.

sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, the like of it. Elucidation: the apparent view is that what is meant by knowledge is the principles of belief; and the more general is possible. His words, "indeed faith — part of it is from part" — that is, the parts of faith, of beliefs and of deeds, are conditioned one upon another, as though the beliefs were parts of the deeds and the reverse; or what is meant is that the parts of faith arise one from another.

«3»- b, Qurb al-Isnad: Harun, from Ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: Beware of the ignorant among the devotees and of the profligate among the scholars, for they are the temptation of every one who is tempted.
I say: we have set down this report, with others suited to this chapter, in the chapter on the censure of the evil scholars.

«4»- l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Malik b. 'Atiyya, from al-Thumali (1), from 'Ali b. al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, who said: There is no pedigree for a man of Quraysh nor for an Arab save by humility, and no nobility save by God-fearing, and no deed save by intention, and no worship save by understanding. Nay — indeed the most hateful of people to God, mighty and majestic, is he who follows the practice of an Imam and does not follow his deeds.

«5»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: Ibn al-Salt, from Ibn 'Uqda, from al-Mundhir b. Muhammad, from Ahmad b. Yahya al-Dabbi, from Musa b. al-Qasim, from Abu al-Salt, from 'Ali b. Musa, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no word save with deed, and no word and deed save with intention, and no word and deed and intention save with the hitting upon the sunna.

Illumination: "there is no word" — that is, no word and belief profits with a complete profit save by the joining of the deed to it; and these two do not profit either save when they are for God, without admixture of ostentation and corrupt purpose; and these three do not profit either save when they accord with the sunna and the deed is not an innovation.
«6»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Azdi, from Abu

A relative from Thumala. And al-Thumali is the sobriquet of Thabit b. Dinar, Abu Safiyya al-Azdi, Abu Hamza al-Kufi, the possessor of the well-known supplication that comes at the pre-dawns of the month of Ramadan. He was of the ascetics of the people of Kufa and of their shaykhs; and the Shi'a are agreed upon his eminence and the loftiness of his standing and the acceptance of his narration without hesitation. And he met four of the Imams: 'Ali b. al-Husayn, and Muhammad b. 'Ali, and Ja'far b. Muhammad, and Musa b. Ja'far, peace be upon them.

208.text: 'Uthman al-'Abdi, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no word save with deed, and no deed save with intention, and no deed and no intention save with the hitting upon the sunna.

«7»- sn, al-Mahasin: Ibn Faddal, from one who related it, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever acts without knowledge, what he corrupts is more than what he sets right.
al-Durra al-Bahira, from al-Jawad, peace be upon him, the like of it.

«8»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: It is related from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said: Two have broken my back: a scholar who casts off restraint, and an ignorant man given to devotion. This one turns people away from his knowledge by his casting off of restraint, and this one turns people away from his devotion by his ignorance.

Clarification: al-Fayruzabadi said: hataka the veil and other than it, yahtikuhu, and it was rent and was torn — he pulled it and cut it from its place until a part of it was split and what was behind it appeared. And a man munhatik and mutahattik and mustahtik is one who does not care that his veil be rent. End. And al-mutanassik is the devotee who strives in worship. And the turning away of the ignorant man from his devotion is either because people, on account of what they see of his ignorance, do not follow him in his devotion; or because by his ignorance he innovates in his devotion, and people follow him in that innovation, and so he turns people away from what is the reality of that devotion.

«9»- ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: Ahmad b. al-Walid, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Musa b. Bakr, from one who heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, say: The one who acts without insight is like the one who travels upon a mirage in a bare flat: the swiftness of his travel only increases him in distance.

Exposition: al-sarab is what is seen in the wilderness of the glittering of the sun upon it at the time of noon, so that it is thought to be water that yasrub — that is, that flows. And al-qi'a is in the sense of al-qa', which is level ground; and it is said that it is its plural, like jar and jira. And it is an allusion to what God the Exalted mentioned concerning the deeds of the unbelievers and their gaining no benefit from them, where He said: "And those who disbelieve — their deeds are like a mirage in a bare flat which the thirsty man reckons to be water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full; and God is swift at the reckoning." (1)

«10»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The devotee without understanding is like the mill-donkey: it goes round and does not move on. And two cycles of prayer from a knower are better than seventy cycles from an ignorant man, because temptation comes to the knower and he goes out from it by his knowledge, and it comes to the ignorant man and sweeps him utterly away. And little deed with much knowledge is better than much deed with little knowledge and with doubt and ambiguity.

209.text: «11»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: So let the scout be truthful to his people, and let him bring his intellect to bear, and let him be of the sons of the hereafter — for from it he came, and to it he returns. So the one who looks with the heart, who acts with sight — let the beginning of his deed be that he know whether his deed is against him or for him. If it is for him, let him go forward in it; and if it is against him, let him hold back from it. For the one who acts without knowledge is like the one who travels off a road: his distance from the road only increases him in distance from his need; and the one who acts by knowledge is like the one who travels upon the clear road. So let the looker look: is he travelling on, or turning back? —
to the end of what will come, expounded, in the Book of the Trials

«12»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Look well into that of which ignorance is not permitted to you, and counsel your souls sincerely, and strive with them (1) in the seeking of the knowledge of that in the ignorance of which you have no excuse. For the religion of God has pillars: whoever is ignorant of them, the intensity of his striving in the seeking of the outward of his worship does not profit him; and whoever knows them and serves by them, the goodness of his moderation does not harm him. And there is no way for anyone to that save by a help from God, mighty and majestic.
Chapter 6: The sciences people are commanded to acquire and which benefit them; including the meaning of ḥikma
al-Baqara: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills; and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good"
al-Isra': "That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom"
al-Zukhruf: "He said: I have come to you with wisdom"
al-Jumu'a: "and He teaches them the Book and the wisdom"

«1»- l, al-Khisal: Majiluwayh, from Muhammad al-'Attar, from al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad b. Muhammad, from Ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Mahziyar, from Hakam b. Buhlul, from Ibn Hammam, from Ibn Udhayna, from Aban b. Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilali, who said: I heard 'Ali, peace be upon him, saying to Abu al-Tufayl
And in the printed Kanz: and strive in the seeking.

210.text: 'Amir b. Wathila al-Kinani (1): O Abu al-Tufayl, knowledge is two knowledges: a knowledge into which people have no latitude but to look — and it is the dye of Islam (2); and a knowledge into which people have latitude to leave off looking — and it is the power of God, mighty and majestic.

Elucidation: al-Fayruzabadi said: al-sibgha, with kasra, is religion and the creed; and the dye of God is the primordial nature of God, or that which God commanded Muhammad, may God bless him and his family, and it is circumcision. End.

I say: what is meant by al-sibgha here is the creed, or everything that dyes a man with the colour of Islam, of true beliefs and good deeds and the rulings of the law. And "the power of God the Exalted" — perhaps what is meant by it here is the determining of deeds and the attaching of God's power to the creating of them; that is, the science of the decree and the determining, and of compulsion and free choice, for there has come a prohibition against reflecting upon them.

And in the Nahj al-Balagha, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said — and he had been asked about the determining — and he said: a dark road, so do not travel it; and a deep sea, so do not enter it; and the secret of God, so do not burden yourselves with it.

«2»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Qasim b. Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Hammad b. 'Isa, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Luqman said to his son: The knower has three marks: the knowledge of God, and of what He loves, and of what He hates — the report.

Elucidation: the knowledge of God includes the knowledge of His existence, exalted be He, and of His attributes, and of the return; rather, of all the necessary beliefs. And it is possible to bring some of them under "what He loves".

«3»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from al-Mu'alla, from Muhammad b. Jumhur al-'Ammi, from Ja'far b. Bashir al-Bajali, from Abu Bahr, from Shurayh al-Hamdani, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Three things by which the Muslim is made complete: understanding in religion, and measured management in livelihood, and patience in misfortunes.

«4»- b, Qurb al-Isnad: Ibn Zarif, from Ibn 'Ulwan, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali, peace be upon him, who said: A man does not taste of the reality of faith until three traits are in him: understanding in religion, and patience in afflictions, and goodness of measured management in livelihood.

The Sunnis and the Shi'a alike entered him in their biographical works, and mentioned that he was one who met the Prophet and then attached himself to the companionship of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and lived long after that; and they did not differ concerning his trustworthiness and the acceptance of his report.
In the printed al-Khisal: and it is the description of Islam.

211.text: Elucidation: measured management in livelihood is the abandoning of extravagance and of stinting and the keeping to the middle — that is, the making of it according to a known measure that accords with the law and with the intellect. And al-nawa'ib are misfortunes.

«5»- li, the Amali of al-Saduq: Ibn Idris, from al-Barqi, from Muhammad b. 'Isa, from al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — entered the mosque, and behold, a company had gathered round a man. And he said: What is this? It was said: A great scholar. He said: And what is a great scholar? They said: The most knowing of people concerning the genealogies of the Arabs and their battle-days and the days of the Jahiliyya, and concerning poetry and the Arabic tongue. And the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: That is a knowledge which does not harm one who is ignorant of it, nor profit one who knows it.

m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Yaqtini, from al-Dihqan, the like of it. — sr, al-Sara'ir, from the book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Sinan al-Dihqan, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Durust, from 'Abd al-Hamid b. Abi al-'Ala', from him, peace be upon him, the like of it.

ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali, from al-Kazim, peace be upon him, the like of it; and he added at the end of it: Then he, peace be upon him, said: Knowledge is only three: a firm verse (1), or an equitable obligation, or an upright practice; and what is besides these is superfluity.

Elucidation: al-'allama is a form of intensification — that is, one of much knowledge; and the ta' is for intensification. His words, may God bless him and his family, "and what is a great scholar" — that is, what is the reality of his knowledge by which he was described as being a great scholar; and it — that is, which kind of the kinds of great scholar, the kinds being by consideration of the kinds of the quality of knowledge. And the upshot is: what is the meaning of "great scholar", which you have said and applied to him. "Knowledge is only" — that is, the profitable knowledge — "three: a firm verse" — that is, of clear signification, or not abrogated; for the ambiguous and the abrogated are not much profited from with respect to meaning. "And an equitable obligation": he said in al-Nihaya: "an equitable obligation" — he meant justice in the apportioning; that is, adjusted to the shares mentioned in the Book and the sunna, without wrong. And it is possible that he means that it is derived from the Book and the sunna, so that this obligation is equated with what is taken from those two. End. And the more evident is that what is meant is obligations absolutely — that is, the required duties, or what is known to be obligatory from the Qur'an; and the first is the more evident, because of its being set opposite the firm verse; and its being described as equitable is because it is midway between excess and defect. And it is said that what is meant by it is what has been agreed upon by
And in one copy: the knowledge of a firm verse.

212.text: the Muslims — and its far-fetchedness is not hidden. And what is meant by the practice is the recommended acts, or what is known by the sunna even if it be obligatory; and upon this it is possible for us to specify the firm verse as what pertains to the principles, or to other than these two of the rulings. And what is meant by "upright" is the abiding, the unabrogated. "And what is besides these is superfluity" — that is, an addition that is void, in the acquiring of which one ought not to waste one's life.

«6»- m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar; l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from al-Isbahani, from al-Minqari, from Sufyan b. 'Uyayna (1), who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: I found the knowledge of all people (2) in four. The first of them: that you know your Lord. And the second: that you know what He has done with you. And the third: that you know what He has willed from you. And the fourth: that you know what takes you out of your religion.

sn, al-Mahasin: al-Isfahani, the like of it. — ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. 'Asim, from al-Minqari, the like of it. — ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: al-Ghada'iri, from 'Ali b. Muhammad al-'Alawi, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Fadl al-Jawhari, from his father, from al-Saffar, from al-Qashani, from al-Isbahani, from al-Minqari, the like of it.

«7»- l, al-Khisal: my father, from Sa'd, from Ibn 'Isa, from al-Bazanti, from a man of Khuza'a, from al-Aslami, from his father, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Learn the Arabic tongue, for it is the speech of God by which He speaks to His creation; and clean the two chewing-places; and bring the signet-rings down.

Illumination: al-madighan are the roots of the two jaws at the springing of the molars, and the cleaning of them is with the toothstick and the toothpick. And al-Saduq said, after mentioning this report: Abu Sa'id al-Adami (3) has related this report and said at the end of it: "bring the signet-rings down" — that is, set the signet-rings at the base of the fingers and do not set them at their tips, for it is related that that is of the practice of the people of Lot. I say: it is possible that it is with the undotted 'ayn — that is, let your fingers be swallowed up in the signet-rings, from swallowing; and in most of the copies it is with the dotted ghayn — that is, bring them down
And in one copy: I found the sciences of all people in four.

He is Sahl b. Ziyad al-Razi. Al-Najashi weakened him in hadith and said: not relied upon in it. And Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa used to testify against him with exaggeration and lying, and expelled him from Qum to Rayy. And the words of al-Shaykh differ concerning his authentication and his weakening.
With damma on the 'ayn: he was of the men of the Sunnis, and some of them, such as Ibn Hajar, have mentioned him and charged him with tadlis and with confusion. He died in the year 198.

213.text: to the base of the fingers, the ba' being redundant. And the apparent view of al-Saduq is that he read the first with the dotted letter and the second with the undotted.

«8»- ma, the Amali of al-Shaykh al-Tusi: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from 'Uthman b. Nusayr the hafiz, from Yahya b. 'Amr al-Tanukhi, from Ahmad b. Sulayman, from Muhammad b. Ja'far, from his father Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father Muhammad b. 'Ali, peace be upon them both, from Jabir b. 'Abd Allah, who said: The Prophet — may God bless him and his family — said: God, mighty and majestic, has not been worshipped by anything more excellent than understanding in religion — or he said: in his religion.
Ahmad said: I mentioned it to Malik b. Anas, the jurist of the people of the Abode of Emigration, and he knew it and confirmed it to me from Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

«9»- 'a, 'Ilal al-Shara'i': my father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Yazid, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad b. Muslim and Burayd, who said: A man (1) said to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him: I have a son who has come to love to ask you about the lawful and the unlawful; he will not ask you about what does not concern him. He said: And he said: And do people ask about anything more excellent than the lawful and the unlawful?

sn, al-Mahasin: Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus b. Ya'qub, from his father, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him: I have a son — and he mentioned the like of it. Elucidation: "about what does not concern him" — that is, what does not matter to him and of which he has no need.

«10»- yr, Basa'ir al-Darajat: Ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Amira, from al-Thumali, from 'Ali b. al-Husayn or from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: One who gains understanding in religion is harder upon Satan than the worship of a thousand worshippers.

«11»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from al-Hasan b. Sayf, from his brother 'Ali, from Sulayman b. 'Umar, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: A servant does not perfect the reality of faith until three traits are in him: understanding in religion, and goodness of measured management in livelihood, and patience under calamities.
Elucidation: al-razaya is the plural of al-razi'a, with the hamza, and it is the affliction.

«12»- sn, al-Mahasin: some of our companions, from Ibn Asbat, from Ishaq b. 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Would that the whips were over the heads of my companions, until they gained understanding in the lawful and the unlawful.
The apparent view is that he is Ya'qub b. Qays al-Bajali al-Duhni, Abu Khalid, the father of Yunus b. Ya'qub who comes in the following report.

214.text: «13»- sn, al-Mahasin: Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Hamid, from his uncle 'Abd al-Salam b. Salim, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: A report concerning the lawful and the unlawful which you take from a truthful one is better than the world and what is in it of gold or silver.

«14»- sn, al-Mahasin: some of our companions, from Ibn Asbat, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: Gain understanding in the lawful and the unlawful; and if not, then you are bedouins.

Elucidation: that is, you are, in your ignorance of the rulings of the law, like the bedouins of whom God said: "The bedouins are more intense in unbelief and hypocrisy" (1) — the verse. And al-a'rab are the dwellers of the desert; it has no singular, and it is pluralized as a'arib.

«15»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from 'Uthman b. 'Isa, from 'Ali b. Hammad, from a man who heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Let not the seeking of your world distract you from the seeking of your religion; for the seeker of the world sometimes attains and sometimes it escapes him, and he perishes for what escaped him of it.
Elucidation: that is, he perishes for abandoning the seeking of religion by reason of the seeking of a matter of this world which he also did not attain — so that he has lost both abodes.

«16»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah and Abu Ja'far, peace be upon them both, said: If a youth of the youths of the Shi'a were brought to me who did not gain understanding, I would surely discipline him.
He said: And Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, used to say: Gain understanding; and if not, then you are bedouins.

«17»- sn, al-Mahasin: in another report of Ibn Abi 'Umayr, raising it, he said: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: If a youth of the youths of the Shi'a were brought to me who did not gain understanding in religion, I would surely make him smart.

«18»- sn, al-Mahasin: in the testament of al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Gain understanding in the religion of God, and do not be bedouins; for whoever does not gain understanding in the religion of God, God will not look upon him on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He count any deed of his as pure.

Elucidation: the not looking is a metaphor for displeasure and wrath; for one who is wroth with another with the utmost wrath does not look at him. And al-tazkiya is praise — that is, He does not accept his deeds.

215.text: «19»- sn, al-Mahasin: 'Uthman b. 'Isa, from 'Ali b. Abi Hamza, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: Gain understanding in religion; for whoever among you does not gain understanding is a bedouin. Indeed God, mighty and majestic, says in His Book: "that they may gain understanding in religion and that they may warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware"
shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Abu Basir, from him, peace be upon him, the like of it.

«20»- sn, al-Mahasin: 'Ali b. Hassan, from one whom he mentioned, from Dawud b. Farqad, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Three are of the marks of the believer: his knowledge of God, and of whom He loves, and of whom He hates.
«21»- sn, al-Mahasin: my father, with an interrupted chain, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, said: The most excellent of worship is the knowledge of God.

«22»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about the words of God, "and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good". He said: It is obedience to God and the knowledge of the Imam (1).
«23»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him — "and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" — he said: The knowledge of realities.

«24»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, saying — "and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" — he said: The knowledge of the Imam, and the shunning of the grave sins for which God has made the Fire obligatory.

«25»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Sulayman b. Khalid, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, about the words of God, "and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good". And he said: Indeed wisdom is the knowledge of realities and understanding in religion; so whoever among you has understanding, he is wise. And there is none of the believers who dies more beloved to Iblis than a jurist.

Elucidation: it has been said that wisdom is the verifying of knowledge and the perfecting of deed; and it has been said, what prevents from ignorance; and it has been said, it is hitting the mark in speech; and it has been said, it is obedience to God; and it has been said, it is understanding in religion. And Ibn Durayd said: everything that leads to a noble quality or prevents from a base one. And it has been said, what comprises the good of the two arisings. And the interpretations are close to one another. And the apparent sense of the reports is that it is the true, profitable sciences together with the acting by what they require. And it is sometimes applied to the sciences that flow from His presence, exalted be He, upon the servant after his acting by what he knows.
«26»- ms, Misbah al-Shari'a: al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: Wisdom is the radiance of the knowledge of realities, and the inheritance of God-fearing, and the fruit of

The apparent view is that the one related from is Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, by the indication of what comes after it; just as the apparent view is that the three narrations related from Abu Basir are one and the same.

216.text: truthfulness. And God has not bestowed upon a servant of His servants a blessing more delightful, or greater, or higher, or more abundant, or more splendid than wisdom. God, mighty and majestic, said: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills; and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good; and none remembers save those possessed of understanding" — that is, none knows what I have deposited and prepared within wisdom save one whom I have purified for Myself and singled out with it. And wisdom is steadfastness; and the quality of the wise is steadfastness at the beginnings of affairs and the halting at their outcomes. And he is the guide of God's creation to God the Exalted. The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said to 'Ali, peace be upon him: That God should guide by your two hands a servant of God's servants is better for you than all upon which the sun rises, from its risings to its settings.

Elucidation: "the radiance of the knowledge of realities": the annexation is either explicative or possessive; and upon the latter, what is meant is the light produced in the heart by reason of that knowledge, or the sciences that flow after it. And steadfastness at the beginnings of affairs is the not being shaken by the trials that arise at the commencing of a deed among the deeds of good; and likewise the halting at their outcomes and their ends, and at what follows upon them of worldly corruptions.

«27»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id b. al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whomever God intends good for, He gives him understanding in religion.
The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — the like of it.
«28»- And by this chain he said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: It is of the goodness of a man's Islam that he leaves what does not concern him.

«29»- sr, al-Sara'ir: in the Jami' of al-Bazanti, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Excellent is the man who has understanding in religion: if he is needed, he profits; and if he is not needed, he profits himself.
«30»- ghw, Ghawali al-La'ali: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: For everything there is a pillar, and the pillar of this religion is understanding.
«31»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: The jurists are the trustees of the Messenger.
«32»- And the Commander of the Faithful, God's blessings be upon him, said to his son Muhammad: Gain understanding in religion, for the jurists are the heirs of the prophets.

217.text: «33»- ja, the Majalis of al-Mufid: Ibn Qulawayh, from al-Kulayni, from al-Husayn b. Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla (1), from al-Washsha', from Hammad b. 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: When God intends good for a servant, He gives him understanding in religion.

«34»- m, the Tafsir of the Imam, peace be upon him: from Abu Muhammad al-'Askari, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: God, mighty and majestic, has not bestowed upon a servant, after faith in God, anything more excellent than the knowledge of the Book of God and the knowing of its interpretation. And whoever God has given a portion of that, and who then supposes that no one has had done for him what has been done for him, when another has been given more than he — such a one has belittled the blessings of God upon him.

«35»- And the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said concerning His words, exalted be He: "O people, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord, and a healing for what is in the breasts, and a guidance and a mercy for the believers. Say: In the bounty of God and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they amass" (2). The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The bounty of God, mighty and majestic, is the Qur'an and the knowledge of its interpretation; and His mercy is His granting of success in the friendship of Muhammad and his pure family and in enmity toward their enemies. Then he — may God bless him and his family — said: And how should that not be better than what they amass, when it is the price of the Garden and its bliss? For by it is gained the good pleasure of God, which is more excellent than the Garden; and by it is merited the being in the presence of Muhammad and his pure family, which is more excellent than the Garden — for indeed Muhammad and the pure family of Muhammad are the noblest adornment of the Gardens. Then he — may God bless him and his family — said: By this Qur'an, and by the knowledge of its interpretation, and by friendship with us, the People of the House, and by dissociation from our enemies, God raises up peoples and makes them leaders in the good [and] guides in the good: their traces are traced out, and their deeds are watched, and their doings are followed as examples; and the angels desire their friendship and stroke them with their wings in their prayers; and there seeks forgiveness for them everything moist and dry — even the fish of the sea and its creeping things, and the beasts of prey of the land and its cattle, and the heaven and its stars.
«36»- dh, Rawdat al-Wa'izin: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The most excellent of worship is understanding, and the most excellent of religion is scrupulousness.
«37»- sr, al-Sara'ir: from the book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Sinan al-Dihqani, from 'Ubayd Allah (3), from

The apparent view, by the indication of his relating from al-Washsha', is that he is al-Mu'alla b. Muhammad Abu al-Hasan al-Basri, concerning whom al-Najashi said: unsettled in report and in doctrine.

The apparent view is that he is 'Ubayd Allah b. 'Abd Allah al-Dihqan al-Wasiti. Al-Najashi weakened him at p. 160 and said: he has a book. And al-'Allama also weakened him in the second part of al-Khulasa.

218.text: Durust, from 'Abd al-Hamid b. Abi al-'Ala', from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever plunges himself wholly into the seeking of grammar is stripped of humility.

Elucidation: the apparent view is that what is meant is the science of grammar; and the later origination of this science and of the name does not conflict with that, because of his knowledge, peace be upon him, of what would later arise. And it is possible that what is meant is the turning of attention to the rules of grammar in the state of supplication. And al-nahw in the language is the road, and the direction, and the intent; and none of these suits the context save with complete artificiality (1).

«38»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Yunus b. 'Abd al-Rahman, that Dawud said: We were with him, and the sky thundered, and he said: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him. And Abu Basir said to him: May I be made your ransom — has the thunder a speech? And he said: O Abu Muhammad, ask about what concerns you and leave what does not concern you.

«39»- The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Indeed of clear speech there is sorcery, and of knowledge there is ignorance, and of poetry there is wisdom, and of speech there is justice.
«40»- al-Durra al-Bahira, from al-Kazim, peace be upon him, who said: Whoever burdens himself with what is not of his knowledge wastes his deed and is disappointed in his hope.
«41»- And al-Jawad, peace be upon him, said: Gaining understanding is a price for everything precious and a ladder to everything lofty.

«42»- al-Jawahir of al-Karajuki: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: The sciences are four: jurisprudence for the religions, and medicine for the bodies, and grammar for the tongue, and the stars for the knowing of the times.

«43»- The Da'awat of al-Rawandi: al-Hasan b. 'Ali, peace be upon them both, said: A wonder at one who reflects upon what he eats — how does he not reflect upon what he takes into his mind, so as to keep from his belly what harms it and to deposit in his breast what destroys him?

«44»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Knowledge is two knowledges: an innate one and a heard one; and the heard does not profit when the innate is not there.

«45»- And he said, peace be upon him — and he had been asked about the determining: a dark road, so do not travel it; and a deep sea, so do not enter it; and the secret of God, so do not burden yourselves with it.
The apparent view is that what is meant by al-nahw is the road, if the report be sound; and what is meant by it is the occupying oneself with knowledge away from deed. T.

219.text: Elucidation: perhaps what is meant by the innate is what he has derived by his understanding and his sound thought, in the principles and the branches, from the rational and the transmitted proofs. And sometimes the innate is restricted to the principles and the heard to the branches.
«46»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: He said, peace be upon him: People are the enemies of what they are ignorant of.

«47»- And he said, peace be upon him: Do not be like the rude ones of the Jahiliyya, neither gaining understanding in religion nor understanding concerning God — like the shells of eggs in ostrich-nests, the breaking of which is a burden of sin, while the hatching of them brings forth evil.

Elucidation: al-qayd is the shell of the egg; and al-adahi is the plural of al-udhiyya, which is the laying-place of the ostrich in the sand. And the bird hadana its egg, hadnan and hidanan: it drew it to itself beneath its wing for hatching. And it is said that the aim is the likening to the eggs of vipers found in the nest of an animal, which cannot be broken because of the possibility of their being from a lawful animal; and if they are left, vipers come forth from them. So likewise are these: if they are left, they become satans who lead people astray; and they cannot be killed, because of the outward of Islam. And the completion of the discourse and its commentary will come in the Book of the Trials.

«48»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: in his testament to al-Hasan, peace be upon him: Plunge into the depths unto the truth wherever it may be, and gain understanding in religion — down to his words, peace be upon him: And understand my testament, and do not turn away from it in disregard; for the best of speech is what profits. And know that there is no good in a knowledge that does not profit, nor is profit had from a knowledge whose learning is not right — down to his words, peace be upon him: And that I should begin with you by the teaching of the Book of God, mighty and majestic, and of its interpretation, and of the laws of Islam and its rulings and its lawful and its unlawful; I do not pass beyond that with you to anything else.

«49»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Five do not gather save in one who is truly a believer, for whom God makes the Garden obligatory by them: the light in the heart, and understanding in Islam, and scrupulousness in religion, and affection among people, and goodness of bearing in the face.
«50»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Knowledge is more than can be numbered, so take of everything the best of it.

«51»- And from it: Luqman said to his son: O my son, learn wisdom and you will be ennobled; for wisdom points to religion, and ennobles the slave above the freeman, and raises the poor man above the rich, and advances the small above the great, and seats the poor man in the assemblies of kings, and increases the noble in nobility, and the master in mastery, and

220.text: the rich man in glory. And how does the son of Adam suppose that the matter of his religion and of his livelihood should be made ready for him without wisdom? And God, mighty and majestic, will never make ready the matter of this world and of the hereafter save by wisdom. And the likeness of wisdom without obedience is the likeness of the body without a soul, or the likeness of the dust without water; and there is no soundness for the body without a soul, nor for the dust without water, nor for wisdom without obedience.
«52»- And from it, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family: Knowledge is two knowledges: the knowledge of the religions and the knowledge of the bodies.
«53»- And he — may God bless him and his family — said: Whomever God intends good for, He gives him understanding in religion.

«54»- 'dda, 'Uddat al-Da'i: The Knowing One, peace be upon him, said: The most fitting knowledge for you is that without which your deed is not sound; and the most obligatory knowledge upon you is that concerning the acting by which you will be questioned; and the most binding knowledge for you is that which points you to the soundness of your heart and makes plain to you its corruption; and the most praiseworthy knowledge in outcome is that which increases your present deed.
«55»- Munyat al-Murid: al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: There is none of the believers who dies more beloved to Iblis than the death of a jurist.
«56»- And from him, peace be upon him: When the believing jurist dies, there is breached (1) in Islam a breach which nothing fills.

«57»- And in the Torah: Magnify wisdom; for I do not place wisdom in the heart of anyone save that I have willed to forgive him. So learn it, then act by it, then bestow it, that you may attain by that My honouring in this world and in the hereafter.
«58»- From Ibn 'Abbas, raised, concerning His words, exalted be He, "He gives wisdom to whom He wills" — he said: Wisdom is the Qur'an.

«59»- And Bashir al-Dahhan (2) related, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, said: There is no good in one of our companions who does not gain understanding. O Bashir, indeed when a man of you is not made independent by his understanding, he has need of them; and when he has need of them, they bring him into the door of their error while he does not know.
«60»- And it is related from him, peace be upon him, that a man said to him: May I be made your ransom — a man has come to know this cause
That is, there arises in Islam a defect which nothing fills.
Of Kufa. Al-Shaykh counted him in his Rijal among the companions of al-Kazim, peace be upon him, and said: he related from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him.

221.text: he kept to his house and did not make himself known to any of his brethren. He said: And he said: How shall this one gain understanding in his religion?

«61»- And from him, peace be upon him: There is no latitude for people until they ask and gain understanding and know their Imam; and it is permitted to them to take by what he says, even if it be dissimulation.

«62»- The book of al-Husayn b. 'Uthman, from more than one, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: A man is not made sound save upon three traits: understanding in religion, and goodness of measured management in livelihood, and patience in misfortune.
Chapter 7: The etiquette of seeking knowledge and its rulings

al-Ma'ida: "O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made plain to you, would grieve you; and if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being sent down, they will be made plain to you. God has pardoned them; and God is Forgiving, Forbearing. A people before you asked about them, then became by them unbelievers"
Ta Ha: "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed; and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge"

«1»- l, al-Khisal: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. 'Ubayd Allah, from al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Four are never sated with four: the earth of rain, and the eye of looking, and the female of the male, and the knower of knowledge.

sn, al-Mahasin: my father, raising it to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, the like of it. — n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him; l, al-Khisal: in the questions of the Syrian, from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, the like of it, save by the dropping of the definite article in all of them.

«2»- shy, the Tafsir of al-'Ayyashi: from Ahmad b. Muhammad, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, wrote to me, and he wrote at the end of it: Were you not forbidden much questioning, and you refused to desist? Beware of that; for those who were before you perished only by the abundance of their questioning. And God said: "O you who believe, do not ask about things" — down to His words, "unbelievers."

222.text: «3»- n, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, peace be upon him: Ibn al-Mughira, by his chain, from al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: There is no wakefulness (1) save in three: one keeping vigil with the Qur'an, or one in the seeking of knowledge, or a bride being conducted to her husband.

The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from al-Kazim, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — the like of it. Elucidation: al-tahajjud is the shunning of hujud, which is sleep; and it is sometimes applied to the prayer at night. And upon the first, what is meant is either the reciting of the Qur'an in prayer, or the more general.
«4»- b, Qurb al-Isnad: Harun, from Ibn Sadaqa, from al-Sadiq, from his father, peace be upon him, who said: There is no harm in wakefulness in the seeking of knowledge.

Elucidation: in some of the copies, "in wandering" — and it is bewilderment, and also a fair gait; and perhaps what is meant is wandering through the lands, that is, travelling, or swiftness in walking. And the first reading is the more evident.

«5»- khts, al-Ikhtisas: al-Baqir, peace be upon him, said: When you sit with a scholar, be more eager to listen than you are to speak; and learn goodness of listening as you learn goodness of speech; and do not cut off anyone's discourse.

«6»- The Nawadir of al-Rawandi, by his chain, from Musa b. Ja'far, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Whoever learns in his youth, it is in the place of the engraving upon stone; and whoever learns when he is old, it is in the place of writing upon the surface of water (2).

«7»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to a questioner who asked him about a knotty matter (3): Ask for understanding and do not ask to confound (4); for the ignorant man who learns is like the knower, and the knower who is arbitrary (5) is like the ignorant.
«8»- And he said, peace be upon him, in censure of a people: Their questioner confounds and their answerer is affected.
With fatha on the undotted sin and ha': the absence of sleep at night.
And in one copy: in the surface of the water.
That is, the closed, difficult question.
ta'annata a man, and against him, in questioning: he asked him by way of entrapment.
ta'assafa in speech: he took it without guidance; he carried it to a meaning whose signification upon it is not evident.

223.text: «9»- And he said, peace be upon him: When answers throng, the right one is hidden.
Elucidation: perhaps in it there is an indication of the forbidding of asking a single question of a large group.
«10»- nhj, the Nahj al-Balagha: He said, peace be upon him: O Kumayl, command your family to go forth (1) in the earning of noble deeds and to travel by night (2) in the need of one who is asleep.
«11»- And he said, peace be upon him: Do not ask about what has not been; for in what has already been there is occupation enough for you.

«12»- And he said, peace be upon him, in his testament to al-Hasan, peace be upon him: The heart of the young man (3) is but like empty ground: whatever is cast into it, it accepts. So I hastened to you with discipline before your heart should harden and your understanding be occupied — down to his words, peace be upon him: And know, O my son, that the most beloved of what you take of my testament is the fear of God, and the restricting of yourself to what God has made obligatory upon you, and the taking of that upon which the first ones of your fathers and the righteous of the people of your house went. For they did not leave off looking to themselves as you look, and thinking as you think; then the end of that brought them back to the taking of what they knew and the withholding from what they were not charged with. So if your soul refuses to accept that without your knowing as they knew, then let your seeking of that be with understanding and learning, not with the plunging into ambiguities and the raising of disputes. And before your looking into that, begin by seeking help upon it from your God, and by turning to Him for your success, and by leaving every doubtful thing that has brought you (4) into an ambiguity or has delivered you over to an error. And when you are certain that your heart has become pure and humbled, and that your judgement has been completed and gathered, and that your concern in that has become a single concern — then look into what I have expounded for you. And if what you love of yourself, and of the freeing of your looking and your thought, is not gathered for you, then know that you are only blundering as the night-blind camel blunders (5), or plunging into the darkness (6); and he is no seeker of religion who blunders or confuses, and the withholding from that is the more proper — down to his words, peace be upon him: And if anything is obscure to you
It is possible that it is from raha yaruhu — that is, he came; or rawwaha, of the second form; or he went in the rawah, that is, the evening; or from raha yurahu, that is, he hastened with joy.
adlaja idlajan: he travelled the whole night, or at the end of it.
That is, has brought you in.

al-'ashwa': the she-camel of narrow sight, or the one that does not see at night and treads upon everything. And the meaning is that you deal with affairs without insight; and it is a proverb for the one who rushes headlong into a thing, and for the one who follows his own head and does not care for its outcome.
That is, you fall into a plight from which escape is not easy. And al-warta, with fatha on the waw and quiescence of the ra': the obscure pit, and destruction.

224.text: of that, then carry it back to your own ignorance of it; for you, when first you were created, were created ignorant, and then you were taught. And how much there is of the matter of which you are ignorant, and in which your judgement is bewildered and your sight goes astray, and then you see it after that! So hold fast to Him who created you and provided for you and shaped you; and let your servitude be to Him, and your desire toward Him, and your fear from Him — down to his words, peace be upon him: And when you are guided to your aim, then be the most humble that you can be toward your Lord.
«13»- The Kanz of al-Karajuki: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Knowledge from smallness is like the engraving upon stone.

«14»- And the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: Showing affection to people is half of intelligence, and goodness of questioning is half of knowledge, and measured management in expenditure is half of living.

«15»- 'dda, 'Uddat al-Da'i: from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — who said: God revealed to one of His prophets: Say to those who gain understanding for other than religion, and who learn for other than deed, and who seek the world for other than the hereafter — they wear for people the skins (1) of rams while their hearts are like the hearts of wolves; their tongues are sweeter than honey and their deeds more bitter than aloes. Me do they seek to deceive, and at Me do they mock. I shall surely appoint for them a trial that will leave the wise man bewildered.

«16»- The book of Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Shurayh, from Humayd b. Shu'ayb, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, saying: O people, fear God and do not multiply questioning; for those who were before you perished only by the abundance of their questioning of their prophets. And God, mighty and majestic, has said: "O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made plain to you, would grieve you." And ask about what God has made obligatory upon you. By God, a man comes to me and asks me, and I inform him, and he disbelieves; and had he not asked me, it would not have harmed him. And God said: "and if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being sent down, they will be made plain to you" — down to His words: "A people before you asked about them, then became by them unbelievers."

«17»- I say: I found in the hand of our Shaykh al-Baha'i, God sanctify his spirit, what follows in his own wording. The Shaykh Shams al-Din Muhammad b. Makki said: I transcribed from the hand of the Shaykh Ahmad al-Farahani, God have mercy upon him, from 'Unwan al-Basri — and he was a great shaykh upon whom ninety-four years had come — who said: I used to frequent Malik b. Anas for years. And when Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, came to Medina, I frequented him and loved to take from him as I had taken from Malik. And he said to me one day: I am a man who is sought after, and along with that I have litanies at every hour of the times of the night and of the day; so do not distract me from my litany. Take from Malik, and frequent

225.text: him as you used to frequent him. So I was grieved at that and went out from his presence, and I said within myself: if he had discerned any good in me, he would not have driven me away from frequenting him and taking from him. So I entered the mosque of the Messenger, may God bless him and his family, and greeted him. Then I returned on the morrow to the Rawda and prayed two cycles in it, and I said: I ask You, O God, O God, that You incline the heart of Ja'far toward me and grant me of his knowledge what I may be guided by to Your straight path. And I returned to my house grieving, and I did not frequent Malik b. Anas, because of what my heart had been made to drink of the love of Ja'far. And I did not go out of my house save to the prescribed prayer, until my patience was exhausted (1). And when my breast was straitened, I put on my sandals and my cloak and made for Ja'far — and that was after I had prayed the afternoon prayer. And when I came to the door of his house I sought leave of him, and a servant of his came out and said: What is your need? And I said: To greet the noble one. And he said: He is standing at his place of prayer. So I sat facing his door; and I had not waited but a little when a servant came out and said: Enter, upon the blessing of God. So I entered and greeted him, and he returned the greeting and said: Sit, God forgive you. So I sat. And he bowed his head a long while, then raised his head and said: Father of whom? I said: Abu 'Abd Allah. He said: God establish your agnomen and grant you success, O Abu 'Abd Allah. What is your question? And I said within myself: if I had of my visiting him and my greeting nothing but this supplication, it would be much. Then he raised his head and said: What is your question? I said: I asked God to incline your heart toward me and to grant me of your knowledge; and I hope that God the Exalted has answered me in the noble one as to what I asked of Him. And he said: O Abu 'Abd Allah, knowledge is not by learning; it is only a light that falls in the heart of one whom God, blessed and exalted, wills to guide. So if you desire knowledge, seek first within yourself the reality of servanthood, and seek knowledge by the employing of it, and ask God for understanding — He will give you understanding. I said: O noble one. And he said: Say, O Abu 'Abd Allah. I said: O Abu 'Abd Allah, what is the reality of servanthood? He said: Three things: that the servant see for himself no ownership in what God has conferred upon him — because slaves have no ownership; they see wealth as the wealth of God and set it where God has commanded them; and that the servant devise no devising for himself; and that the whole of his occupation be in what He, exalted be He, has commanded him and forbidden him. So when the servant sees for himself no ownership in what God the Exalted has conferred upon him, spending becomes easy for him in that in which God the Exalted commanded him to spend. And when the servant entrusts the devising of himself to the One who devises for him, the afflictions of this world become easy for him. And when the servant occupies himself with what God the Exalted has commanded him and forbidden him, he has no leisure from these two for disputation and boasting with people. So when God honours the servant with these three, there becomes easy
In the language: 'ila sabri — that is, it was overturned.

226.text: for him this world, and Iblis, and the creatures; and he does not seek the world for multiplying and boasting, nor seek what is with people for might and exaltation, nor leave his days in vanity. And this is the first degree of God-fearing. God, blessed and exalted, said: "That abode of the hereafter — We appoint it for those who desire neither exaltation in the earth nor corruption; and the outcome is for the God-fearing." I said: O Abu 'Abd Allah, counsel me. He said: I counsel you with nine things, for they are my counsel to those who desire the way to God the Exalted; and God I ask that He grant you success in the employing of them. Three of them are in the disciplining of the soul (1), and three of them are in forbearance, and three of them are in knowledge. So preserve them, and beware of making light of them. 'Unwan said: So I emptied my heart for him. And he said: As for those that are in the disciplining: beware of eating what you do not desire, for it bequeaths foolishness and stupidity; and do not eat save at hunger; and when you eat, eat what is lawful, and name God, and remember the report of the Messenger, may God bless him and his family: no son of Adam has filled a vessel worse than his belly; and if it must be, then a third for his food, and a third for his drink, and a third for his breath. And as for those that are in forbearance: whoever says to you, "if you say one, you will hear ten", say: if you say ten, you will not hear one. And whoever reviles you, say to him: if you are truthful in what you say, then I ask God to forgive me; and if you are lying in what you say, then God I ask to forgive you. And whoever promises you foul speech (2), promise him sincere counsel and regard. And as for those that are in knowledge: ask the scholars about what you do not know, and beware of asking them to confound and to test; and beware of acting by your own opinion in anything; and take to caution in all wherein you find a way to it; and flee from the giving of legal opinion as you flee from the lion; and do not make your neck a bridge for people. Rise from me, O Abu 'Abd Allah, for I have counselled you; and do not spoil my litany for me, for I am a man sparing of myself. "And peace be upon him who follows the guidance."

«18»- Munyat al-Murid: from the Prophet — may God bless him and his family — that Moses, peace be upon him, met al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and said: Counsel me. And al-Khidr said: O seeker of knowledge, indeed the speaker is less wearied than the listener; so do not weary
al-riyada: the refining of the qualities of the soul.

227.text: your sitting-companions when you speak to them. And know that your heart is a vessel, so look to what you stuff your vessel with. And know the world and cast it behind you, for it is no abode for you, nor is there in it a place of settling for you; it was made only a passing provision for the servants, that they might take provision from it for the return. O Moses, set your soul (1) upon patience, and you will meet forbearance; and clothe your heart with God-fearing, and you will attain knowledge; and train your soul upon patience, and you will be delivered from sin. O Moses, free yourself for knowledge if you desire it, for knowledge is only for one who frees himself for it. And do not be one of much speech (2), a prattler (3); for the abundance of speech disfigures the scholars and discloses the faults of the frivolous. But keep to moderation, for that is of success and of rightness. And turn away from the ignorant, and be forbearing toward the foolish, for that is the excellence of the forbearing and the adornment of the scholars. And when the ignorant man reviles you, be silent toward him in peace and shun him in resolve; for what remains of his ignorance toward you and of his reviling of you is more. O son of 'Imran, do not open a door of which you do not know the shutting, and do not shut a door of which you do not know the opening. O son of 'Imran, one whose greed for the world does not come to an end and whose desire in it does not cease — how shall he be a worshipper? And one who belittles his own state and charges God concerning what He has decreed for him — how shall he be a renouncer? O Moses, learn what you learn in order to act by it, and do not learn in order to talk of it, lest its ruin be upon you and its light be upon another.
Elucidation: he said in al-Fa'iq: al-bur, with damma, is the plural of bawar (4); and with fatha it is the verbal noun; and the verbal noun may also be with damma.

«19»- m', Ma'ani al-Akhbar; j, al-Ihtijaj; 'a, 'Ilal al-Shara'i': al-Daqqaq, from al-Asadi, from Salih b. Abi Hammad, from Ahmad b. Hilal, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Mu'min al-Ansari, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him: A people relate that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — said: The difference of my community is a mercy. And he said: They have spoken truly. And I said: If their difference is a mercy, then their coming together is a punishment? He said: It is not as you go, nor as they went. He meant only the words of God, mighty and majestic: "So why should there not go forth from every party of them a group, that they may gain understanding in religion and that they may warn their people
That is, prepare your soul and carry it upon patience.
A man mihdhar, hadhir — that is, he confuses in his speech and says what is not fitting.
And it is destruction and unsaleableness.

228.text: when they return to them, that they may beware." So He commanded them to go forth to the Messenger of God — may God bless him and his family — and to frequent him and learn, then to return to their people and teach them. He meant only their going to and fro from the towns, not a difference in the religion of God; for the religion is but one.

Here ends the first part of Bihar al-Anwar of this edition, adorned with precious and valuable annotations and with many weighty benefits. It comprises the Book of the Intellect and Knowledge and Ignorance in five chapters containing 125 reports, and seven chapters of the Book of Knowledge containing 270 reports. And the second part follows it, beginning from the eighth of the chapters of the Book of Knowledge, "the chapter on the reward of guidance and of teaching". And God is the granter of success in good and in right direction. Sha'ban the Honoured, 1376 AH
